title: TUI: route lsm_warn!/lsm_error! through a sink, not raw stderr (alt-screen safety)
description:
Surfaced by silent-failure-hunter round 2 review of lsm-herx.8.

The render path uses lsm_warn! and lsm_error! macros which write to io::stderr().lock() directly (logging.rs:144,158). When linesmith config is open, the alt-screen owns stdout but stderr writes during a frame draw paint into the alt-screen and corrupt visual state. Worse with LINESMITH_LOG=debug — every draw fires lsm_debug! repeatedly, trashing the screen.

Sites that bypass the preview's warn callback today:
- layout/mod.rs:475-507 (try_shrink contract violations)
- input/mod.rs (15+ schema-drift warns inside claude::normalize during preview JSON parse)
- All apply_layout decisions (priority drop, shrink succeed, reflow succeed, width-bound truncation)

Needs: thread a LogSink trait through the entire render path so lsm_warn!/lsm_error! get routed to the same Vec<String> the preview already collects. Or install a process-wide stderr-redirect for the duration of the alt-screen.

The preview's captured-warnings channel from lsm-herx.8 only covers the direct callback paths (build_lines, render_to_runs segment errors). The macro-based diagnostics still leak.

Blocks: any TUI screen that triggers segment rebuild or stress-tests the layout engine should not be considered shippable until this is settled. lsm-herx.7 (Items Editor) will exercise these paths heavily.
close_reason: LogSink trait + StderrSink/CapturedSink/SinkGuard in linesmith-core; TUI installs CapturedSink for alt-screen lifetime via SinkGuard; preview::render_lines drains it per-frame into warnings panel; flush_captured_to_stderr surfaces boot-failure diagnostics. 3 v0.2 follow-ups filed (lsm-67go concurrent emit/swap race, lsm-ah52 buffer growth bound, lsm-1m42 plugin eprintln fallback).

title: TUI event loop: filter on KeyEventKind::Press to avoid Windows double-fire
description:
Today the crossterm event dispatch in tui/mod.rs:127-129 routes every CtEvent::Key(key) into Event::Key(key), regardless of key.kind. On Windows, crossterm emits both Press AND Release for every keystroke; on macOS/Linux only Press by default. Result: every keypress in linesmith config fires update twice on Windows (Press once, Release once), which would double-trigger every Action verb, double-toggle move-mode on Enter, etc.

Fix: gate the match arm on key.kind == KeyEventKind::Press. Add a test that constructs a Release-kind KeyEvent and asserts poll_event maps it to None (or filters it before reaching update — depending on which layer the gate lands).

Pre-existing: introduced in lsm-herx.3, surfaced during lsm-herx.4 review by code-reviewer agent.
close_reason: Added classify_event filter in tui/mod.rs that routes only KeyEventKind::Press to Event::Key. Release and Repeat key kinds drop to None, preventing the Windows double-fire (Press+Release) and keeping autorepeat behavior consistent (OS produces Press stream for held keys). Extracted into a separate fn so the dispatch logic is unit-testable; 5 new tests pin Press routing, Release/Repeat filtering, Resize routing, and Focus/Paste fall-through.

title: fix(doctor): convert FileCascadeEnv struct literals to ::new() constructor
description:
Two FileCascadeEnv struct-literal sites in cli's doctor tests at crates/linesmith/src/doctor/mod.rs:6447, 6451 fail E0639 'cannot create non-exhaustive struct using struct expression' on Linux + Windows.

The tests are gated #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))] (cascade behavior on non-mac platforms), so cargo check on macOS skips them entirely — local verification was a false positive throughout the lsm-1nh0 workspace split + subsequent rounds. CI on ubuntu-latest + windows-latest catches it because they DO compile the gated tests.

Fix: replace struct literals with FileCascadeEnv::new(claude_config_dir, xdg_config_home, home) — the public constructor that already exists in linesmith-core.

Caught when CI failed on the release-plz PR (#3) following the lsm-1nh0 + lsm-y7md push.
close_reason: Replaced both FileCascadeEnv struct literals at doctor/mod.rs:6447, 6451 with FileCascadeEnv::new(claude, xdg, home) calls. Local mise run check clean. Cross-platform compile gap is a separate concern: the macOS-gated tests should ideally run on macOS too (perhaps as #[ignore]d compile-only) so future cross-crate non_exhaustive struct breakage gets caught pre-push.

title: parse_context_window TypeMismatch on null sub-fields tanks entire statusline render
description:
Surfaced via lsm-mdd7 capture analysis on 2026-04-25. Pre-first-API-call CC stdin payload (CC 2.1.120, every fresh session ~15s window) has context_window present but used_percentage/remaining_percentage/current_usage all null:

```json
"context_window": {
  "total_input_tokens": 0,
  "total_output_tokens": 0,
  "context_window_size": 200000,
  "current_usage": null,
  "used_percentage": null,
  "remaining_percentage": null
}
```

parse_context_window calls require_f64("context_window.used_percentage") which throws TypeMismatch on null. The whole stdin parse fails, driver renders ? for the entire statusline (all segments — model, git_branch, workspace, cost, effort) for ~15 seconds at session start.

Real impact: every linesmith user sees a broken statusline at the start of every fresh CC session. Reproducible by replaying any captured pre-first-API-call payload through linesmith.

**Quick fix scope (this bead):**
- parse_context_window catches null sub-fields and returns Ok(None) for the whole field, mirroring the existing "context_window: null" handling.
- Add regression test using the captured fixture.
- Optional defensive sweep of parse_cost / parse_workspace / parse_model / parse_effort for similar required-but-can-be-null patterns.

**Architectural follow-up:** ADR-0008 (in flight) generalizes this into best-effort parse + per-segment Option-shaped isolation. The quick fix here lands first to stop the bleeding for v0.1.2; the ADR refactor lands later as a focused effort.

**Acceptance:** the captured pre-first-API-call payload renders successfully through linesmith with model/git/workspace segments visible and the context_window segment hidden.
close_reason: Quick fix for pre-first-API-call ?-everywhere bug. parse_context_window now returns Ok(None) when any required leaf (used_percentage, context_window_size, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens) is JSON null, mirroring the existing context_window: null early-return. Diagnostic at lsm_debug! per project logging convention. 5 new tests including a real CC 2.1.119 fixture; structural assertions to survive fixture re-capture. Architectural follow-up (per-leaf Option widening) remains in lsm-9zvh.

title: Upgrade rustls-webpki patch + gix 0.67 to 0.82+ to clear 20 dependabot alerts
description:
Pre-v0.1.1 release work. Dependabot reports 20 open alerts across two advisories.

HIGH (1 alert): rustls-webpki GHSA-82j2-j2ch-gfr8 — DoS panic on malformed CRL. Patch 0.103.12 → 0.103.13 available, cargo update -p rustls-webpki.

MEDIUM (19 alerts): gix family (18) GHSA-2frx-2596-x5r6 — SHA-1 collision detection missing; gix-date (1) GHSA-6mw6-mj76-grwc — TimeBuf::as_str can return non-UTF-8. Both fixed by bumping gix from 0.67 to 0.82+ in Cargo.toml workspace deps.

Scope: (1) cargo update -p rustls-webpki. (2) bump gix pin in Cargo.toml from 0.67 to 0.82 keeping the same feature set (max-performance-safe, status, revision). (3) fix compile errors in git_branch and workspace segments from API churn across 15 minor versions. (4) re-run full test suite. (5) verify dependabot shows 0 open alerts.

Threat model: linesmith uses gix read-only for branch, ahead/behind, and dirty state. No auth, no sign/verify. SHA-1 collisions at worst mis-name a branch.

Acceptance: dependabot API query for open alerts returns count 0.
close_reason: rustls-webpki patched 0.103.12 → 0.103.13 (clears HIGH GHSA-82j2-j2ch-gfr8). gix bumped 0.67 → 0.82 + explicit sha1 feature (default-features = false had silently stripped sha1, leaving gix-hash::Kind as an empty enum that rustc 1.82+ rejects). API churn handled in data_context/git.rs classify_kind: gix 0.82 consolidated Kind::Bare + Kind::WorkTree{is_linked:false} into Kind::Common and moved bare detection to Repository::is_bare(); Kind::WorkTree{is_linked:true} is now Kind::LinkedWorkTree. Deprecated peel_to_id_in_place replaced with peel_to_id. 950 tests pass, release binary 4.1MB.

title: from_terminal() returns None when stdout is piped; CC spawns always pipe linesmith so TrueColor themes never activate
description:
Surfaced via lsm-mdd7 live-capture session. User configured `theme = \"catppuccin-mocha\"` expecting the mocha palette. Under Claude Code (which always spawns with piped stdout), `supports_color::on(Stream::Stdout)` returns None, `from_terminal()` drops to `Capability::None`, and `force_color_detect()` falls back to `Capability::Palette16`. Catppuccin themes then render as default Palette16 ANSI (BrightBlue/BrightBlack/etc.) — indistinguishable from the built-in `default` theme.

Net effect: every TrueColor theme silently downgrades to the 16-color fallback under real CC usage. Mocha/Frappe/Macchiato/Latte all end up identical to `default`.

**Fix sketch:**
- In `Capability::from_terminal()` at `crates/linesmith/src/theme/mod.rs:199`, when `supports_color` returns None, check env independently: `COLORTERM=truecolor|24bit` → TrueColor; `TERM` matching 256color/xterm-ghostty/xterm-kitty/alacritty/tmux-256color → Palette256; else Palette16 (fresh fallback since we know the TTY-capability probe failed but we are still likely being rendered by a real terminal).
- Alternatively: probe stderr as a secondary signal since statusline spawns often leave stderr as a TTY.
- Tests: env fixture with COLORTERM=truecolor and stdout=piped should yield TrueColor; env fixture without COLORTERM should still yield Palette16 (not None), matching current `--force-color` behavior.

**Why this matters:** this is table stakes for a tool that ships curated Catppuccin/Dracula/Nord presets as a v0.1 differentiator (per linesmith-project-vision memory). No user will ever see the catppuccin palette under current detection.
close_reason: force_color_detect rewritten to use Capability::force_from(tty, env) — picks richer of supports-color TTY probe and COLORTERM/TERM env probe, floors at Palette16 so force-color intent is never silently dropped. COLORTERM and TERM threaded through CliEnv snapshot so tests and embedders stay hermetic (Codex P2 regression guard). Auto-color stays pipe-safe: from_terminal unchanged, still returns None when stdout isn't a TTY. Pure helpers from_env_vars and force_from are unit-tested; a hermeticity test locks the CliEnv-only read path.

title: parse_effort rejects Claude Code's object-shaped effort field
description:
Surfaced via lsm-mdd7 live-capture. CC 2.1.119 emits:

```json
"effort": {
  "level": "xhigh"
}
```

`parse_effort` at `crates/linesmith/src/input.rs:536-538` expects a bare string:
```rust
let raw = value.as_str().ok_or_else(|| type_mismatch("effort", JsonType::String, JsonType::of(value)))?;
```

This rejects the real payload as TypeMismatch, collapses the whole stdin parse, and renders `?`. Spec at `docs/specs/input-schema.md:358` still says "Claude Code doesnt emit yet" — spec is stale too.

**Fix sketch:**
- Accept the object form `{"level": "xhigh"}` as canonical (thats what CC actually sends).
- Keep bare-string tolerance as a defensive fallback if its ever seen.
- If effort is an object with no `.level`, surface MissingField("effort.level") with full path.
- Update `docs/specs/input-schema.md` edge-case row.
- Tests: object-happy, object-missing-level, bare-string-back-compat, null, absent, type-mismatch (non-object non-string non-null).

**Acceptance:** replaying the captured stdin JSONL record tagged `baseline-200k` through linesmith renders the Opus 4.7 statusline without error, and the effort level flows into `StatusContext.effort = Some(EffortLevel::XHigh)`.

Also surfaced: the pre-existing cargo-installed binary (~/.cargo/bin/linesmith) still has the old stdin `rate_limits` parser that rejects the numeric `resets_at`. Fixed in source (no longer parsed); just needs cargo install --path to refresh.
close_reason: parse_effort accepts both object form {level: string} (canonical per CC 2.1.x live capture) and bare-string (back-compat). Errors carry full JSON path — effort.level for object-form failures, effort for primitive rejection. 8 new tests cover null at outer/inner, missing level, non-string level, unknown values, non-object non-string, and both happy paths. Spec edge-case table updated. Integration fixture claude_worktree.json flipped to object form to exercise the canonical path end-to-end.

title: Amend config.md with [usage] section + fix stale visible_if example
description:
data-fetching.md and rate-limit-segments.md reference usage.cache_duration, usage.api_base_url, usage.timeout but config.md does not define the [usage] section — only per-segment [segments.rate_limit_5h] tables. Slices 3 (HTTP client) and 4 (cache) both need these knobs to exist in the config schema before the code reads them.

Also fixes a stale reference: config.md line 131 example uses ctx.rate_limits.kind == "both" for visible_if. That shape is the stdin-payload RateLimits enum, which slice 7 drops in favor of ctx.usage(). The example must be updated to reference ctx.usage so plugin authors do not learn a path we are about to delete.

Ships: new [usage] section in config.md defining cache_duration (default 180s), api_base_url (default https://api.anthropic.com), timeout (default 2s), plus cross-link to data-fetching.md §OAuth usage cache stack. Updated visible_if example referencing ctx.usage.five_hour.utilization > 50 (or similar ctx.usage shape) with cross-link to rate-limit-segments.md. Change-log entry in config.md noting the additions.
design: Values match ccometixline-rust-patterns.md §Config-driven base URL and TTL convention (api_base_url, cache_duration, timeout at the [usage] level, not [segments.*]). api_base_url enables self-hosters / proxies without code changes — cheap to support, high user-demand signal. Deliberately NOT documenting extra hidden knobs (retry counts, lock TTL) since those are v0.1 implementation details subject to change; expose only what the ADR + specs already expose.
acceptance_criteria: config.md contains [usage] section with the three keys, their defaults, and prose explaining each tradeoff. visible_if example no longer references ctx.rate_limits. Spec lints clean (markdownlint). Cross-links added to data-fetching.md and rate-limit-segments.md so slice 3 + slice 4 have a canonical schema reference.
close_reason: config.md rev to v0.1.1: added [usage] top-level section (cache_duration, api_base_url, timeout) for the OAuth rate-limit endpoint knobs; migrated [segments.rate_limit_5h] visible_if example from ctx.rate_limits to ctx.usage tagged-map shape; reciprocal cross-links added in data-fetching.md §OAuth usage cache stack and rate-limit-segments.md §Staleness bounds. lsm-7xv + lsm-b9w now have the config schema they read against.

title: Wire 5 rate-limit segments to ctx.usage() + add 3 new segments
description:
Per rate-limit-segments.md §Interface + §Render semantics. Replaces stdin-payload ctx.status.rate_limits path in existing rate_limit_5h.rs / rate_limit_7d.rs / rate_limit.rs (combined) with ctx.usage() reads. Adds 3 new segments: rate_limit_5h_reset, rate_limit_7d_reset, extra_usage.

Ships: data_deps() override returning &[DataDep::Usage] on all 5 segments (currently missing). Render body reading ctx.usage() + matching Ok(UsageData) → format OR Err(UsageError) → render error string. Config schemas per rate-limit-segments.md §Config schema: format, invert, progress_width, icon, label, stale_marker, compact, use_days. Format helpers: format_percent, format_progress_bar, format_duration (compact + use_days), format_currency. Error rendering table (8 strings per rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table). UsageSource::Jsonl detection → prepend stale_marker. Drops stdin-payload rate_limits path entirely (docs-review Decision 3).
design: Drop stdin rate_limits path (docs-review Decision 3): endpoint+JSONL is strictly richer; avoids three code paths. Pro/Max users who had only stdin data now get endpoint data at least as rich. format_duration shared between _5h_reset + _7d_reset; use_days max 4-digit cap per rate-limit-segments.md §Edge cases. Currency: UsageData.extra_usage.currency.unwrap_or("USD"); "USD" renders $, anything else renders ISO code prefix per rate-limit-segments.md §Precision. Progress bar: reuse existing bar helper from context_bar work if it lands first, else ship local + refactor later.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot tests per segment × format variant × invert × error state per rate-limit-segments.md §Testing strategy. Integration: full render with stubbed DataContext::usage() returning happy-path / each error variant / JSONL-source — assert exact output. rate_limit_5h_reset hides when resets_at is in the past (per rate-limit-segments.md §Edge cases). extra_usage hides when is_enabled=false (no empty state) but renders error strings when fetch fails. stale_marker="" suppresses JSONL indicator. Existing tests in rate_limit.rs / rate_limit_5h.rs / rate_limit_7d.rs migrate to new contract OR are deleted if superseded — no dead tests reading ctx.status.rate_limits.
notes: Explicit scope addition: this slice also DELETES input::RateLimits enum + RateLimitWindow struct + the rate_limits field on StatusContext (crates/linesmith/src/input.rs). Those types exist only to parse the stdin-payload rate_limits field which this slice stops consuming. AGENTS.md 'no backwards-compatibility hacks' — delete completely rather than leave parsed-but-unused. Any tests still referencing StatusContext { rate_limits: ... } in fixtures must migrate to ctx.usage() stubs.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 10 slices landed. rate-limit + usage segments ship end-to-end: OAuth cascade (lsm-wwd), multi-tier cache (lsm-b9w), credential reader (lsm-a7a), JSONL aggregator (lsm-26y), HTTP client (lsm-7xv), typed response (lsm-6cc), 5 segment implementations (lsm-7po), config-side visible_if fix (lsm-4wl), doctor diagnostics (lsm-dct), jsonl-aggregation spec (lsm-tia). Deferred to follow-ups per epic scope: JSONL → UsageBucket tier-aware mapping (lsm-xhu), per-model weekly segments, daemon mode (ADR-0012 v0.2+).

title: DataContext::usage() fallback cascade orchestrator
description:
Ties slices 1-5 together. Replaces Arc::new(Err(UsageError::NotImplemented)) in DataContext::usage() with the real cascade per data-fetching.md §OAuth fallback cascade (which reorders ADR-0011 to put cache reads before credentials — same behavior, avoids Keychain subprocess on cache hits).

Cascade order:
1. In-memory OnceCell hit → return
2. Disk cache (usage.json) fresh + schema_version matches → populate memory, return
3. Lock file active AND disk cache has stale data → return stale
4. Read credentials via ctx.credentials() (triggers Keychain subprocess if not yet resolved)
5. No token → record UsageError::Credentials(NoCredentials) → JSONL fallback (step 7)
6. Hit endpoint with 2s timeout → 200 cache+return; 429/timeout/network + stale cache → serve stale; 429/timeout/network without stale → JSONL fallback; 401 → Unauthorized recorded → JSONL fallback
7. JSONL fallback via aggregate_jsonl(): success → return UsageData { source: Jsonl }; failure → surface original recorded error
8. Fresh endpoint 200 writes usage.json AND updates usage.lock with blocked_until = now + cache_duration (other processes see via cache, not retry)

Ships real impl behind DataContext::usage() using slices 1-5; UsageSource::Jsonl tag propagation to segments; UsageApiResponse → UsageData conversion (endpoint path) + JsonlAggregate → UsageData (fallback path).
design: Cache-before-credentials ordering follows data-fetching.md §OAuth fallback cascade explicitly — deliberate departure from ADR-0011 written cascade order for same user-visible behavior. Documented here so future reviewers do not "fix" it back. Lock file write on successful fetch: blocked_until = cached_at + cache_duration. Expired lock = cache stale = other process retries. Error recording order: record first real failure (credentials missing, endpoint error) then try JSONL; on JSONL success error is discarded; on JSONL failure it is surfaced. JsonlError wraps into UsageError::Jsonl(...) per slice 1 taxonomy. No retry loop at this layer; stale-cache serve IS the retry.
acceptance_criteria: Cascade test per branch: fresh-memory, fresh-disk, stale-disk + active-lock, cache-miss + 200, cache-miss + 401, cache-miss + 429 with stale, cache-miss + 429 without stale, cache-miss + timeout with stale, cache-miss + timeout without stale → JSONL success, all-error → original error surfaces. NoCredentials masking guarantee: no token → [No credentials], NOT [Timeout], even when JSONL also fails. Fresh-cache hit does NOT trigger credential resolution (counter on test double). Running linesmith twice with warm usage.json triggers zero HTTP requests and zero Keychain subprocesses. Concurrent processes with stale lock: second process serves stale data. UsageSource flows: endpoint → Endpoint; JSONL → Jsonl (asserted by segment test stub).
close_reason: DataContext::usage() cascade orchestrator: pure resolve_usage function (cache/lock/transport/creds/jsonl/clock injected), wired through DataContext::usage() with defaults. Cache-before-credentials short-circuit; active lock blocks fetch even on cold cache (Codex P1); 429/timeout/401 persist usage.lock with Retry-After or error-TTL backoff so concurrent processes honor it (Codex P1). CredentialError gets lossy Clone so UsageError::Credentials(variant) propagates through Arc-shared boundaries (rate-limit-segments.md error table). write_cache/write_lock debug_assert loudly on failure with TODO(lsm-logger) anchors; reads silently degrade. DataContext::preseed_usage pre-populates the OnceCell so tests and plugin-dev harnesses skip the cascade. v0.1 JSONL path: ctx.usage ignores JSONL result (can't populate tier-aware utilization), follow-up tracked as lsm-xhu.

title: JsonlAggregate + JsonlTailer (5h block + 7d window aggregator)
description:
Terminal fallback source for DataContext::usage(). Scans ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl, aggregates into 5h blocks + 7d windows, dedupes on message.id. Wire shape defined by jsonl-aggregation.md spec (slice 0).

Ships: JsonlAggregate struct + JsonlError taxonomy per jsonl-aggregation.md; JsonlTailer { path, last_offset, last_size } with read_new::<T>() -> Result<Vec<T>, JsonlError> per data-fetching.md §JSONL incremental tail; 5h block aggregation per research/jsonl-data-source.md §3 (port ccusage _session-blocks.ts math); 7d rolling window (second pass); dedup seen message.id within window; project-root discovery cascade $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/ → ~/.config/claude/projects/ → ~/.claude/projects/; truncation/rotation detection (size < last_size → reset offset); aggregate_jsonl() -> Result<JsonlAggregate, JsonlError> entry point consumed by slice 6.
design: Per-process JsonlTailer with last_offset = 0 at start (v0.1 no daemon per ADR-0012). Daemon mode reuse is a spec follow-up. Malformed lines logged at warn!, offset advances past them (per data-fetching.md §JSONL). Tailer does NOT hold file open across calls — opens + reads + closes per invocation; rotation detection via stat before read. Partial struct with #[serde(default)]: only consume documented fields; unknown silently skipped per ADR-0009. Dedup set bounded by 7d window, not whole file — bounded memory regardless of transcript size.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: empty file, single line, many lines, truncation, partial trailing line (no \\n), malformed JSON lines logged + skipped, offset monotonicity invariant. 5h block boundary tests: entries exactly 5h apart, entries within 5h, gap-block emission for idle >5h. Dedup tests: same message.id twice → counted once. Directory-cascade tests: only $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/ exists → read from there; none exist → JsonlError::DirectoryMissing. Integration test: realistic multi-file fixture under tests/fixtures/jsonl/ matching actual Claude Code output; aggregate output matches ccusage reference.
close_reason: JSONL aggregator: offset-tailing JsonlTailer, project-root cascade ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR → XDG → ~/.claude) with dedicated XDG-without-HOME handling, ccusage-derived 5h billing-block math with FiveHourBlock::end method, 7d window with clock-skew guard. Non-UTF-8 lines skip per-line via read_until + lossy convert (not whole-file abort). 30+ tests cover boundary math, cross-root dedup, offset monotonicity, and clock-skew edge cases.

title: OAuth /api/oauth/usage HTTP client (ureq + retry/timeout/backoff)
description:
HTTP surface between the fallback orchestrator (slice 6) and the Anthropic OAuth usage endpoint. Returns Result<UsageApiResponse, UsageError>; orchestrator layers cache + credentials + JSONL fallback on top.

Ships: fetch_usage(creds: &Credentials, timeout: Duration) -> Result<UsageApiResponse, UsageError>. Headers per ADR-0011 §Endpoint contract: Authorization: Bearer {token}, anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20, User-Agent: linesmith/{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}. 2s default timeout. Status handling: 200 → deserialize; 401 → Unauthorized; 429 → parse Retry-After (integer-seconds AND HTTP-date per ADR-0011) → RateLimited { retry_after }; 4xx/5xx other → NetworkError; timeout/connect failure → Timeout/NetworkError; malformed JSON → ParseError.
design: ureq (project-standard). No async runtime. Inject HTTP surface via small trait (UsageEndpoint) with blanket impl over ureq::Agent so tests swap a fake — avoids mockito dev-dep balloon. Retry-After HTTP-date parser: httpdate crate. Token redaction: format!("Bearer {}", creds.token()) locally, never logged; if ureq adds trace-level request logging later we add a redaction hook. No retry loop — this is the bottom layer; retries (stale-cache serve, JSONL fallback) live in slice 6.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests with trait-injected HTTP surface (or mockito) covering: 200 happy path; 401; 429 with integer Retry-After; 429 with HTTP-date Retry-After; 429 without Retry-After (default 300s backoff); timeout; connect refused; malformed JSON. Golden-fixture integration: feed live-captured response, assert deserialization matches. Token does not appear in any error Display/Debug output when request fails with 401 (verified via format!). User-Agent string includes CARGO_PKG_VERSION.
close_reason: OAuth /api/oauth/usage HTTP client landed in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/fetcher.rs (~500 LOC + 23 tests). UsageTransport trait + UreqTransport impl + fetch_usage(); maps HTTP statuses onto UsageError taxonomy per rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table. Retry-After parsed as integer or RFC 9110 HTTP-date with 24h cap + 300s fallback. Response body capped at 64 KiB. User-Agent cached on struct + exposed via default_user_agent() for regression testing. Workspace MSRV raised to 1.85 for ureq 3.3 + rustls. Credentials::for_testing helper added. 623 tests passing. Unblocks lsm-wwd (cascade orchestrator).

title: Multi-tier OAuth usage cache (usage.json + usage.lock + atomic rename)
description:
Disk-backed layer of the cache stack per data-fetching.md §OAuth usage cache stack + §Atomic writes + §Concurrent processes. In-memory OnceCell already on DataContext; this slice adds disk tiers and lock file.

Ships: CacheStore with read() -> Result<Option<CachedUsage>, CacheError> + write(&CachedUsage); CachedUsage { schema_version: u32, cached_at: DateTime<Utc>, data: Option<UsageApiResponse>, error: Option<CachedError> } matching data-fetching.md shape; LockStore with read() + write(blocked_until: u64, error: &str); atomic-rename writes via tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist; schema_version mismatch → treat as miss; path resolution XDG_CACHE_HOME/linesmith/ → ~/.cache/linesmith/; default 180s data TTL (configurable via usage.cache_duration), 30s error TTL, 30s lock TTL.
design: One module (cache.rs) owning both CacheStore + LockStore; shared path-resolution and atomic-write helpers. schema_version = 1 for v0.1, const so bumps visible in review. CachedError mirrors UsageError taxonomy but serialized as tagged string ("NoCredentials", "Timeout", etc.) — NOT the full Rust enum with inner CredentialError data. Errors cached briefly (30s) are intentionally lossy across process boundaries — live errors from this process take precedence. Directory creation via fs::create_dir_all at write time, not init. Lock file coordination uses SAME atomic-rename helper as data writes; no flock/LockFileEx gymnastics.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip: write → read returns equivalent CachedUsage. schema_version mismatch → read() returns Ok(None) (miss, not error). Clock skew (cached_at > now) → treated as stale miss. Zero-byte/corrupt cache file → Ok(None) miss, never hard-errors. Concurrent write smoke: 2 threads both writing different payloads; assert final file is one-or-the-other, never interleaved (atomic rename demo). title: Credential reader: Keychain primary + multi-account fallback + file cascade
description:
Per credentials.md §Interface + §Resolution cascade. Replaces CredentialError::NotImplemented stub in data_context::credentials().

Ships: Credentials { token: SecretString, scopes: Vec<String>, source: CredentialSource } with Debug redacting the token; CredentialSource (5 variants: MacosKeychainPrimary, MacosKeychainMultiAccount {service, mdat}, EnvDir, XdgConfig, ClaudeLegacy); CredentialError (6 variants: NoCredentials, SubprocessFailed, IoError, ParseError, MissingField, EmptyToken); resolve_credentials() entry point; #[cfg(target_os="macos")] primary via `security find-generic-password -a $USER -w -s "Claude Code-credentials"` + multi-account fallback via `security dump-keychain` with mdat sort + per-candidate find-generic-password retry; all platforms file cascade $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json → ~/.config/claude/.credentials.json → ~/.claude/.credentials.json with 1MB size cap; wire into DataContext::credentials() with process-lifetime memoization.
design: secrecy crate for SecretString (already referenced in credentials.md). `security` invoked via std::process::Command with Stdin::null() and a short deadline matching endpoint budget. mdat parsing: hex-ASCII blobs from `security dump-keychain`; stable sort, mdat-DESC (newest first), no-mdat entries last by dump order. File size cap: 1MB hard limit pre-parse → ParseError if exceeded. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="" → treated as unset (user-intent honoring). No Windows Credential Manager (v0.2+ per ADR-0011).
acceptance_criteria: resolve_credentials unit tests per credentials.md §Testing strategy (valid JSON, null token, missing field, invalid JSON, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to existing/non-existing, XDG preferred over legacy, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="" treated as unset). #[cfg(target_os="macos")] integration: inject fake `security` binary on PATH returning controlled output; assert primary path, multi-account fallback, mdat sort picks newest. Credentials::Debug does NOT leak token (visual assert with format!). Token never at trace/debug level (grep tests/ for bare token use). DataContext::credentials() returns cached Arc<Result<...>>; subprocess invoked once per process.
close_reason: Credential reader + OAuth token resolution landed in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/credentials.rs (~850 LOC + 30 tests). Credentials/CredentialSource/CredentialError types with SecretString-redacted Debug; flat code() taxonomy; resolve_credentials() runs the cascade (macOS Keychain primary + multi-account mdat-newest + file cascade). macOS run_security enforces 2s + 500ms grace via try_wait polling with reader-thread drain; errSecItemNotFound (44) falls through cleanly; other non-zero exits preserve stderr (truncated at 512 bytes). AccessToken uses Option<Option<String>> with deserialize_with to distinguish MissingField from EmptyToken. FileCascadeEnv DI sidesteps unsafe env mutation. DataContext::credentials() wired + memoized. 602 tests passing. Unblocks lsm-7xv (HTTP), lsm-wwd (cascade), lsm-l35 (doctor). Follow-ups filed: lsm-yq8 (macOS PATH-injection integration test), lsm-iz6 (plugin-api.md MissingField/EmptyToken taxonomy update).

title: UsageApiResponse (wire) + UsageData/UsageSource/UsageError (internal) types
description:
Foundation types for every other y6m slice. Replaces the #[non_exhaustive] pub struct UsageData {} stub + single-variant UsageError::NotImplemented in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/mod.rs and errors.rs.

Ships: UsageApiResponse (wire shape per ADR-0011 §Endpoint contract) with Option<UsageBucket> fields (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_oauth_apps), Option<ExtraUsage>, #[serde(flatten)] unknown_buckets: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value> catch-all. UsageBucket { utilization: Percent, resets_at: DateTime<Utc> } reusing input::Percent (already has [0,100] clamp). ExtraUsage per rate-limit-segments.md §extra_usage. UsageData (internal) = wire fields + source: UsageSource { Endpoint, Jsonl } tag used by stale_marker rendering. UsageError (flat, 8 variants) per rate-limit-segments.md §Error message table: NoCredentials, Credentials(CredentialError), Timeout, RateLimited { retry_after: Option<Duration> }, NetworkError, ParseError, Unauthorized, Jsonl(JsonlError).
design: Wire shape (UsageApiResponse) separate from internal (UsageData) so endpoint-client → cache → segment conversion is explicit — slice 3 owns UsageApiResponse → UsageData (endpoint path), slice 5 owns JsonlAggregate → UsageData (fallback path). UsageError::Credentials(CredentialError) wrapping (docs-review Decision 1) over flat 8 variants: segment renderer matches on inner variant for three credential-flavored strings [Keychain error]/[Credentials unreadable]/[No credentials]. Percent reuse: input::Percent::new(f32) → Option<Self>; no new type. #[serde(default)] on every Option field so partial responses never fail parse. #[non_exhaustive] on UsageApiResponse and UsageError for non-breaking growth.
acceptance_criteria: Golden-fixture serde round-trip: feed live-captured /api/oauth/usage response from docs/research/claude-data-files.md §Raw data, assert lossless parse; feed a response with an injected codename ("quokka_experimental") and assert it lands in unknown_buckets. Error rendering smoke test: for each UsageError variant, produce the exact rendered string per rate-limit-segments.md table. UsageData exposes source(), five_hour(), seven_day(), extra_usage() accessors. ctx.usage() still returns an Err sentinel until slice 6 wires the real fetcher.
close_reason: UsageApiResponse (wire) + UsageBucket + ExtraUsage + UsageData + UsageSource + UsageError (8 variants with flat code() delegation) landed in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/{usage,errors,mod}.rs. Live-capture golden test + clamp edges + null-resets + codename catch-all + code() delegation pinned. ctx_mirror swapped to e.code() for stable plugin-facing short tags. chrono gained serde feature. 568 tests passing. Unblocks lsm-7xv (HTTP), lsm-b9w (cache), lsm-26y (JSONL aggregator), lsm-wwd (cascade).

title: Draft docs/specs/jsonl-aggregation.md (JsonlAggregate shape + 5h/7d block math)
description:
data-fetching.md §JSONL explicitly defers the JsonlAggregate shape to a dedicated spec. rate-limit-segments.md JSONL-fallback path, the 5h/7d segment hiding rules when fallback kicks in, and the UsageSource::Jsonl tag all depend on this spec existing. Blocks y6m slice 5 (JSONL aggregator implementation).

Spec defines: JsonlAggregate struct shape (5h block bucket list, 7d rolling window, per-entry tokenCounts, source_paths, dedup_seen_ids); JsonlError taxonomy (IoError, ParseError, DirectoryMissing, NoEntries); 5h block math per research/jsonl-data-source.md §3 (ccusage _session-blocks.ts port); 7d window math (second pass); dedup on message.id; project-root discovery cascade ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/ → ~/.config/claude/projects/ → ~/.claude/projects/); per-line partial struct (timestamp, message.usage.*, message.model, message.id, costUSD, usageLimitResetTime); integration contract with JsonlTailer from data-fetching.md; edge cases (log rotation, dedup collisions, usageLimitResetTime provenance).
design: JSONL fallback produces only 5h and 7d, not per-model buckets or extra_usage (per ADR-0011 §Fallback cascade). Scope: read + aggregate only, not write. Performance contract: byte-offset tail = O(new bytes); dedup set bounded by 7d window, not file size. MIT-licensed ccusage TypeScript is the reference implementation — cite + port, do not re-derive.
acceptance_criteria: Spec lands in docs/specs/jsonl-aggregation.md with status=draft, version=0.1; cross-linked from data-fetching.md §JSONL (remove "shape deferred" comment) and rate-limit-segments.md §JSONL-fallback display; JSON examples for each record type; follows docs/specs/0000-template.md conventions.

JsonlAggregate + FiveHourBlock + SevenDayWindow + TokenCounts + JsonlError with code() taxonomy; per-line record schema; project-root cascade; 5h block math ported from ccusage _session-blocks.ts; dedup on message.id; malformed-line handling. title: Epic: v0.1 rate-limit + usage segments (OAuth endpoint + JSONL fallback)
description:
Highest-signal user demand per research memory (44+ reactions on anthropics/claude-code#8412). Rate-limit visibility is THE feature every competitor ships.

**Architecture resolved (ADR-0011 + spec lane):** Primary source is `GET api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with OAuth Bearer token + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` header. JSONL aggregation (ccusage-style) is the fallback when auth is unavailable. This supersedes the earlier 'JSONL-scraping only' framing — live capture of the endpoint (see docs/research/claude-data-files.md §Raw data) confirmed the shape, and ccstatusline + CCometixLine both verified hitting the same endpoint.

**Spec coverage (all landed):**
- docs/adrs/0011-rate-limit-data-source.md — endpoint + credentials + fallback cascade decisions
- docs/specs/data-fetching.md v0.1.1 — DataContext + OAuth multi-tier cache + DataDep::Git/Usage wiring
- docs/specs/credentials.md — macOS Keychain cascade + file fallback + SecretString redaction
- docs/specs/rate-limit-segments.md — 5 segment IDs (rate_limit_5h, rate_limit_7d, rate_limit_5h_reset, rate_limit_7d_reset, extra_usage), config schemas, error rendering, JSONL fallback stale_marker

**Implementation slices to file as dependent beads:**
- OAuth HTTP client (ureq, 2s timeout, 429 backoff with Retry-After parsing, stale-on-error)
- Credential reader: macOS Keychain primary + multi-account Keychain dump fallback + XDG/legacy file cascade
- Multi-tier cache (memory OnceCell + disk data JSON w/ schema_version + disk lock file + atomic rename writes)
- JSONL 5h-block aggregation (ccusage math per docs/research/jsonl-data-source.md)
- Fallback cascade orchestration (cache → credentials-before-endpoint-but-after-cache-reads → JSONL terminal → original-error surface)
- The 5 segment implementations against the trait from segment-system.md v0.3
- Forward-compat serde struct: serde(default) + Option + #[serde(flatten)] catch-all for codenamed buckets (omelette_promotional etc.)
- linesmith doctor integration (check credentials, cache, endpoint reachability)

**Out of scope (deferred):**
- Tier detection (no competitor does it; lsm-043 closed)
- Per-model weekly segments (rate_limit_7d_sonnet etc.) — follow-up after v0.1
- jsonl-aggregation.md dedicated spec — needed when JSONL fallback implementation begins; file as follow-up
- Daemon mode for cross-session OAuth cache (ADR-0012 deferred to v0.2+)

**Privacy note for README:** all data-fetching is local (Keychain + ~/.claude/ + anthropic.com via user's own OAuth token). No telemetry.

**Acceptance:** rate_limit_5h / rate_limit_7d / rate_limit_5h_reset / rate_limit_7d_reset render live data for any user with a Claude Code OAuth session; extra_usage renders when enabled; JSONL fallback kicks in on auth failure; segment parity with ccstatusline's BlockTimer / BlockResetTimer / WeeklyUsage / WeeklyResetTimer; no long-lived secrets; linesmith doctor reports actionable diagnostics.

Description rewritten 2026-04-20 to reflect ADR-0011 + the three rate-limit-lane specs landed tonight. Prior description framed this as JSONL-only; actual architecture is OAuth endpoint primary + JSONL fallback.

description:

title: Epic: v0.1 release pipeline via cargo-dist + release-plz
description:
Epic anchor for the v0.1 release pipeline per [ADR-0007](../adrs/0007-cargo-dist-distribution.md) (cargo-dist distribution). Spec: docs/specs/release-process.md.

**Scope covered by this epic:**
- cargo-dist config (dist-workspace.toml) — 7 targets: macOS x86_64/aarch64, Linux x86_64/aarch64 + x86_64-musl, Windows x86_64/aarch64. Shell + powershell + homebrew installers per release-process.md
- Homebrew tap repo (oakoss/homebrew-tap) — cargo-dist writes Formula/linesmith.rb on release
- release-plz config (release-plz.toml) — changelog + version bumps + crates.io publish via OIDC trusted publishing
- git-cliff config (cliff.toml) — Conventional-commit CHANGELOG format per release-process.md §CHANGELOG contract
- Two chained workflows per release-process.md §Workflow structure:
  - .github/workflows/release-plz.yml (push to main + workflow_dispatch; opens release PR; tags + publishes on merge)
  - .github/workflows/release.yml (tag-push triggered by release-plz; cargo-dist matrix + global-publish + attest)

- First v0.1.0-rc1 dry-run + v0.1.0 cut (depends on other v0.1 work complete)

**Acceptance:** pushing a v*.*.* tag produces GH Release with 7 target binaries, Homebrew formula pushed to oakoss/homebrew-tap, CHANGELOG.md updated, crates.io publish succeeds via OIDC, SLSA attestations attached. Reference: jbabin91/autocomplete-rs uses the same stack.

description:
