title: TUI save UX: replace invisible Ctrl+S with auto-save or apply menu
description:
Today every linesmith TUI screen uses a 2-stage commit: Enter commits to the in-memory DocumentMut (visible in preview, in is_dirty(), in subsequent screens); Ctrl+S flushes to disk via atomic rename. The ConfirmQuit modal warns on dirty quit. This pattern matches text editors but feels wrong for a structured config UI — users expect 'I picked it, it's saved' (macOS Settings model), not 'now press an invisible keybind to persist.'

Two directions to consider:

(A) **Auto-save on every screen-level commit.** Each screen's commit path calls model.save() after writing to the document. Drops ConfirmQuit modal (no dirty state). Drops Ctrl+S (or keeps as a no-op for muscle memory). Pro: simplest mental model. Con: no try-and-back-out semantics; one disk write per commit (still atomic via temp + rename).

(B) **Add an Apply / Save Changes menu option.** Keeps the 2-stage pattern but makes save discoverable: a row on MainMenu (gated on is_dirty? always visible?) triggers model.save(). Ctrl+S can stay as a power-user shortcut. Pro: smaller change, preserves try-and-discard. Con: doesn't fully solve 'I picked it' expectation — still 2-stage.

Either direction affects all 5 edit screens (theme_picker, items_editor, line_picker, type_picker, raw_value_editor) and the quit logic. Worth a focused slice with its own review + ccstatusline-parity check.

Open questions for the design ADR:
- Does ccstatusline's TUI auto-save or use explicit apply?
- Undo strategy if we go auto-save (revert via picking the prior selection? Esc-back-out window?)
- Ctrl+S disposition under auto-save (drop, keep as no-op, keep as 'force flush' for plugin caches?)
- ConfirmQuit modal removal or repurpose?
- Footer keybind hints (orthogonal but related)

Triggered by user feedback on lsm-herx.21 manual TUI testing: 'I find it bad UX' / 'either auto-save or apply menu option instead of ctrl+s'.

title: Refactor LoadOutcome to enum + split SaveOutcome NoTarget reasons
description:
Surfaced by lsm-herx.9 type-design-analyzer review.

`LoadOutcome` currently encodes 4 distinct outcomes (no-path / missing-file / clean-parse / parse-error / parser-skew) as a flat product struct with implicit field-combination invariants documented as prose. A reader has to cross-reference the doc comment to know which combinations are legal.

Refactor to a sum:

```rust
pub(super) enum LoadOutcome {
    NoPath,                                    // path == None
    MissingFile { path: PathBuf },             // path provided, NotFound
    Loaded { config, document, original_text, path },
    ParseError { warning: String },            // refuse save, defaults loaded
    ParserSkew { config, warning: String },    // toml accepts, toml_edit rejects
}
```

Pair with splitting `SaveOutcome::NoTarget` into `NoPath` vs `RefusedDueToParseError` so the user-facing `apply_save` warning can name the specific reason instead of OR'ing two distinct conditions in one sentence.

The current shape works for v0.1 (single producer in `load_config`, single consumer in `run`), but a second producer (e.g., a future "reload config" feature) would force every site to know the four-bullet outcomes. Refactoring also makes the `Model::new` call site clearer (a match instead of 7 positional args).

Defer until items editor (lsm-herx.7) lands so the second consumer materializes.

title: CapturedSink inter-frame buffer has no growth bound
description:
Surfaced by lsm-wyph silent-failure-hunter review.

`CapturedSink.entries` is an unbounded `Vec<String>`. `preview::render_lines` only drains it during a frame draw. For v0.1 (synchronous render, draws fire on every event), the buffer drains fast enough that growth isn't observable.

Once v0.2 background plugins land (or any emitter that fires between draws on an idle screen), the buffer grows without limit until the next keypress triggers a redraw. Long-idle TUI sessions could accumulate megabytes of warn/debug strings.

When relevant:
- Cap entries at N most-recent (drop-oldest with a counter)
- Add a wake signal so the event loop redraws when the sink crosses a threshold
- Add timestamps so the user can see "this happened 5 minutes ago" not just "this happened"

Relevant code: crates/linesmith-core/src/logging.rs:189-232 (CapturedSink). The trait doc at the same file already notes drain timing.

title: LogSink concurrent emit/swap race window
description:
Surfaced by lsm-wyph reviews (type-design-analyzer + silent-failure-hunter).

`current_sink()` (logging.rs) reads the slot mutex, clones the active `Arc<dyn LogSink>`, then releases the mutex BEFORE calling `emit`. If a `SinkGuard::drop` (or raw `install_sink`) runs between the clone and the `emit` call, the emission lands on the just-orphaned sink — refcounted alive by the in-flight clone, but its buffer will never be drained because the consumer has already moved on.

For v0.1 (single-threaded TUI render path), this is latent: nobody emits from a non-render thread today. The trait advertises `Send + Sync` so the door is open for v0.2 background plugin emitters, at which point this race becomes a real silent-drop on shutdown.

Fix options when needed:
- Hold the slot mutex across `emit` (kills the cheap-clone rationale)
- Add a quiesce protocol (drain plugin emitters before swap)
- Use `arc-swap` to make the swap atomic w.r.t. readers
- Document the constraint and require single-threaded emission

Relevant code: crates/linesmith-core/src/logging.rs:225-258 (current_sink + install_sink). The trait doc at logging.rs:137-160 already calls out this gap.

title: TUI: thread CliEnv through tui::run instead of reading process env directly
description:
Surfaced by silent-failure-hunter round 2 review of lsm-herx.8.

tui::run currently reads live process env via XdgEnv::from_process_env() (mod.rs:69) and Capability::detect() (which reads NO_COLOR directly). Production driver carefully snapshots env into CliEnv (driver.rs:97-108) and passes that down so tests and embedders stay hermetic.

Two consequences:
1. Hermeticity break: tests against the TUI can't override env without mutating process env.
2. Embedder gap: linesmith config can't be invoked from an embedder that wants to pass env via API.

Fix: change tui::run signature to accept &CliEnv and reuse driver::cli_env_to_xdg + driver::resolve_color_capability (already exposed as private fns). The single caller (driver::config_action) already constructs CliEnv.

This also lets the TUI honor --no-color / --force-color CLI flags at the process level, even though the TUI itself doesn't take args — those flags would be threaded via CliEnv.

Related: H-1 from same review — Capability::detect() ignores 4 of 6 driver inputs. lsm-herx.8 added partial config-side handling for [layout_options].color but full parity needs CliEnv.

title: Layout engine: surface priority-drop/shrink/reflow/width-bound decisions to caller
description:
Surfaced by silent-failure-hunter round 2 review of lsm-herx.8.

apply_layout in linesmith-core/src/layout/mod.rs makes layout decisions silently:
- Priority drop: segment with lower priority dropped to fit width — silent
- Shrink succeed: segment shrunk to its hide_below_cells minimum — silent
- Reflow succeed: truncatable segment reflowed with ellipsis — silent
- Width-bound min-drop: rendered.width < bounds.min causes hide — silent
- Width-bound max-truncation: ellipsis insertion in truncate_to — silent

For the production stdout path this is correct (the user sees the result directly). For the live preview in the editor, the user is consciously evaluating layout decisions — they need a signal when 'cost was dropped at this width' or 'workspace got truncated to claude-sonn…'.

Needs: extend the warn callback contract on render_to_runs to emit layout-decision events, optionally gated by a 'verbose' flag the preview path opts into. Production driver passes verbose=false; preview passes verbose=true.

Or: add a separate decision-event callback distinct from the warn channel, so production code doesn't pay the cost of formatting messages it'll discard.

Without this, the live-preview's promise ('see what your config does at this width') is half-broken — it shows the result but not the reasoning.

title: Preview: hold last-valid output during transient invalid edit states
description:
ADR-0016 §preview-as-persistent-header mentions: 'Holds last-valid output during transient invalid states (e.g., template editor mid-typing).' This isn't implemented — the preview re-renders on every state change, so an invalid intermediate state (e.g. mid-typing in a future template editor) would produce empty/partial output and flicker.

Needs:
1. A 'last good' snapshot field on Model (e.g. last_preview: Option<Vec<Line<'static>>>).
2. Detection of invalid state from the editor screen (e.g. parse error from toml_edit).
3. Render the cached snapshot with a dim italic '(frozen — invalid input)' overlay so the user knows the preview is stale.

Defer until the first mutating screen lands (lsm-herx.7 Items Editor or whichever lands first) — there's no transient invalid state today since model.config is immutable across the session.

title: markdownlint: exclude auto-generated CHANGELOGs (release-plz CI fails on MD022)
description:
The release-plz PR for v0.1.3 (PR #5) fails CI on Static Analysis (markdown lint) because the auto-generated CHANGELOG files don't have a blank line above the new heading. Errors:

  crates/linesmith-core/CHANGELOG.md:7 MD022/blanks-around-headings
  crates/linesmith-plugin/CHANGELOG.md:7 MD022/blanks-around-headings

The CHANGELOGs are produced by release-plz / git-cliff at PR-creation time, not hand-edited. Linting auto-generated content fights the tool that generated it.

Options:

1. Add **/CHANGELOG.md to the markdownlint ignores list (.markdownlint-cli2.yaml). Simplest, but loses lint coverage on the existing hand-edited root CHANGELOG.md and crates/linesmith/CHANGELOG.md if they ever get manual edits.

2. Add the per-crate generated paths only (crates/linesmith-core/CHANGELOG.md, crates/linesmith-plugin/CHANGELOG.md) to ignores. Targeted but couples the ignore list to the crate layout — needs touching whenever a new crate gets a CHANGELOG.

3. Fix release-plz/git-cliff to emit the blank line MD022 wants. Look at cliff.toml or release-plz config for the changelog template; ensure there's a blank line between the heading and any preceding content.

4. Disable MD022 in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml entirely. Loses an actually-useful lint on hand-edited markdown; not recommended.

Recommend (3) if the template fix is small, otherwise (1). The auto-generated content is exactly what should be ignored, not what should drive the lint rules.

Once landed, the release-plz PR's Static Analysis check should go green. The Required CI Checks ruleset gates merge on CI Summary (which depends on static-analysis), so this is a release blocker for v0.1.3.
close_reason: Fixed in cliff.toml: dropped trailing - on endmacro tag and removed the now-redundant blank line in the body template. Root cause was git-cliff's internal \n separator combining with the template's whitespace control to leave only one newline between header preamble and the first ## heading. Verified locally with git-cliff + markdownlint-cli2 (0 errors).

title: ListScreen MoveSwap contract: cursor-mutation timing rethink
description:
Design follow-up surfaced by review of lsm-herx.4. Should be settled before lsm-herx.7 (Items Editor) starts consuming the contract, since herx.7 is the first production caller of MoveSwap.

Two related contract concerns to design together:

## Concern A — MoveSwap is advisory; cursor mutation timing

Today, handle_key returns ListOutcome::MoveSwap { from, to } AND mutates state.cursor = to before returning. The caller is expected to swap rows from/to in their own row vector. If a caller forgets the MoveSwap arm, the highlighted row changes but the underlying data doesn't — the user sees the cursor visit the new position while their actual ordering stays unchanged. Silent UI/data desync.

Options:

1. Don't mutate state.cursor in the widget on MoveSwap. Caller takes full responsibility — moves data and cursor together when acknowledging. A missed swap arm is then visually obvious (cursor doesn't move) instead of silent.
2. Rename MoveSwap to MoveSwapRequested + harden the doc contract. Cosmetic, doesn't change behavior.
3. Debug-build-only swap-acknowledgement tracking: widget records that a MoveSwap is outstanding; next handle_key debug_asserts the swap was performed. Heavyweight but enforces the contract.
4. Leave as-is and document more aggressively at the variant site.

Recommend (1) for the cleanest semantics — partial-state-update bugs are notoriously hard to debug.

## Concern B — move-mode redispatch reinterprets user keypresses

Surfaced by silent-failure-hunter round 2. The defensive clamp added in round 1 of lsm-herx.4 now clears state.move_mode = false whenever move_mode_supported = false. If a caller flips move_mode_supported from true to false between two handle_key calls (e.g., a screen disables reorder while a confirmation modal is open), the user holding ↓ in move-mode will see their next ↓ silently reinterpreted from "swap with the row below" to "navigate down" — and the swap they intended is lost, with no diagnostic.

Test move_mode_supported_false_clears_stale_state_move_mode pins this as the current behavior (Consumed, navigate). Whether that's right depends on the answer to A:

- If A's resolution is "widget owns cursor on swap" (option 1), the redispatch is fine because the redispatched key gets clean normal-mode semantics.
- If A's resolution is "widget surfaces a partial-state intent", the redispatch needs to either drop the keypress (return Unhandled) or log the mode-flip transition.

Both should be settled together. Defer until lsm-herx.7 has a concrete reorder UX to design against.

Blocks: lsm-herx.7 should not start until both A and B are resolved.
close_reason: Resolved as ADR-0022: ListScreen MoveSwap is advisory; widget no longer mutates state.cursor on swap, caller acknowledges via rows.swap + state.set_cursor. Redispatch path returns Unhandled when move_mode_supported flips mid-key (no key reinterpretation). Implementation lands under lsm-herx.7.

title: Decide LineItem clone story for TUI items editor (lsm-herx.7 prerequisite)
description:
The TUI items editor (lsm-herx.7) round-trips a Vec<LineItem> through TOML edits. Box<dyn Segment>: !Clone is the blocker for naive duplication.

Two architectural options surfaced during the lsm-herx.2 review pipeline (type-design-analyzer, round 1):

(a) **Sibling LineItemConfig enum** that round-trips TOML cheaply (Clone + Serialize) and only materializes Vec<LineItem> at render time. Keeps Segment trait clean. More plumbing.

(b) **Segment::clone_box(&self) -> Box<dyn Segment>** (DynClone-style). Cascades to every built-in segment + RhaiSegment. Possible state-clone problems for stateful plugins (cached AST, etc.).

Type-design-analyzer's recommendation was (a) — cleaner, avoids hyperlink-clone-explosion problems with stateful plugin segments.

Decide before lsm-herx.7 starts. Decision belongs in an ADR (likely deepening/extending ADR-0021 or a new ADR on TUI editor data model). Implementation lands as a follow-up bead under the lsm-herx epic.
close_reason: Resolved as ADR-0023: TUI items editor operates on model.document (DocumentMut) directly; rejects LineItemConfig sibling enum and Segment::clone_box cascade. Threads a LineKey enum through helpers so single-line ([line]) and multi-line ([line.N]) entries from Main Menu and Line Picker share one editor implementation. Per-mutation Config::from_str_validated refresh keeps model.config in sync for the existing preview path. Implementation lands under lsm-herx.7.

title: Folder-graduate data_context/{cascade,credentials,jsonl}/ — pair with lsm-0a4e
description:
Three flat files in \`crates/linesmith-core/src/data_context/\` exceed both the LOC smell trigger and the ≥3-concept folder trigger:

- \`cascade.rs\` — 1820 LOC (1358 tests, 462 code)
- \`credentials.rs\` — 1490 LOC (1413 tests, 77 code; macOS keychain + filesystem fallback are the two impl concerns; 95% test ratio means folder-graduation primarily for ADR-0021 rule 2)
- \`jsonl.rs\` — 1459 LOC (822 tests, 637 code; parser + aggregator + window-derivation are distinct sub-concepts)

Each becomes \`data_context/<name>/\` with mod.rs + concept-named sub-files + tests.rs (per ADR-0021 rules 2-4).

**Pair with lsm-0a4e (env: thread non-UTF-8 XDG/HOME paths through CliEnv + EnvVarState).** That bead's scope was expanded on 2026-05-02 to absorb the env-cascade DRY opportunity (4 open-coded \`(LINESMITH_CONFIG, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, HOME)\` triples scattered across config.rs, credentials.rs, jsonl.rs, xdg.rs). The env-cascade refactor naturally lands inside the new \`credentials/\` and \`jsonl/\` folders. Sequence option A: do lsm-0a4e first, fold the resulting EnvCascade type into the folder structure here. Sequence option B: do the folder graduations first, then weave EnvCascade through the new files. Pick during planning — the work is the same, the order is the question.

Acceptance: cascade, credentials, jsonl are folder modules; lsm-0a4e's env-cascade refactor merged in (or filed as explicit follow-up); all import sites updated; \`mise run check\` + \`mise run test\` green.

Driven by ADR-0021 follow-up #6. Tightly coupled to lsm-0a4e.
close_reason: Folder-graduated data_context/{cascade,credentials,jsonl}/ per ADR-0021 rule 2. Each flat .rs became <name>/{mod.rs, tests.rs}: cascade (1820 LOC → 463 impl + 1355 tests), credentials (1490 LOC → 1009 impl with mod macos kept inline + 474 tests), jsonl (1459 LOC → 636 impl + 820 tests). Pure mechanical extraction — no semantic changes, no visibility bumps required, public API path-equivalent. Stale '// --- Tests ---' section banners removed from credentials/mod.rs and jsonl/mod.rs (leftover artifacts pointing at extracted-out test blocks). Impl-splits per ADR-0021 rule 3 (cascade ~6 helper categories, jsonl 3 sub-concepts) deferred as optional follow-up. mise run check + 1524 tests green.

title: Split segments/builder.rs (2397 LOC) into segments/builder/ folder
description:
\`crates/linesmith-core/src/segments/builder.rs\` is 2397 LOC and mixes five concerns — comfortably above ADR-0021 rule 1's smell trigger and well past rule 3's ≥3-concept threshold.

Candidate decomposition (subject to revision once inside the work):

- \`segments/builder/mod.rs\` — re-exports + thin orchestration
- \`segments/builder/dispatch.rs\` — \`build_default_segments\`, \`build_segments\`, \`build_lines\`, \`build_one_line\`
- \`segments/builder/layout.rs\` — \`validated_numbered_lines\`, \`extract_line_segments\`, \`parse_layout_separator\`, \`apply_layout_separator\`, \`validate_powerline_width\`, \`single_line_ids\`, \`resolve_layout_separator\`
- \`segments/builder/plugins.rs\` — \`bundle_plugins\`, \`apply_override\`, \`toml_table_to_dynamic\`, \`toml_value_to_dynamic\`
- \`segments/builder/toml_describe.rs\` — \`describe_toml_value\` (small helper used by warning paths)
- \`segments/builder/tests.rs\` — extracted test block (~1795 LOC today)

Watch for visibility: builder is a coordination point used by the runtime. Keep the public façade in \`mod.rs\` (per ADR-0021 rule 4) and use \`pub(super)\` aggressively for cross-file helpers inside the folder.

This is the most invasive split of the seven follow-ups — touches the rhai \`Dynamic\` conversions and the layout-validation paths. Land bead lsm-NEW-1 (workspace lints) first so \`unreachable_pub\` catches over-exposed helpers in CI.

Acceptance: \`segments/builder.rs\` removed; \`segments/builder/\` folder with mod.rs + named files; all imports updated; \`mise run check\` + \`mise run test\` + benches still green.

Driven by ADR-0021 follow-up #5.
close_reason: Split segments/builder.rs (2397 LOC) into segments/builder/ folder per ADR-0021 rules 2-4. mod.rs (12) is the façade with pub use dispatch::{...}; dispatch.rs (262) holds the 3 public dispatchers + private build_one_line; layout.rs (245) holds 8 layout/validation helpers (6 pub(super), 2 private); plugins.rs (100) holds 4 plugin/override helpers (3 pub(super), 1 private toml_value_to_dynamic); tests.rs (1802) is the extracted test block with rewritten imports (super::{dispatch,layout,plugins}::* + explicit segments parent imports). 3 redundant //! file headers removed during de-slopify. Stale config.rs:145 doc reference 'segments::builder::apply_override' fixed (apply_override is now private in the plugins submodule). External API path crate::segments::builder::build_segments resolves identically. mise run check + 1524 tests + mise run bench (188s) all green.

title: Graduate segments/rate_limit/ to a folder + UsageWindow seam (DRY 1+4)
description:
Two concerns folded into one bead because they share the same seam:

**Folder graduation (ADR-0021 rule 3).** The five rate-limit files (`rate_limit_5h.rs`, `rate_limit_5h_reset.rs`, `rate_limit_7d.rs`, `rate_limit_7d_reset.rs`, `rate_limit_format.rs`) plus a new `window.rs` exceed the ≥3-concept trigger. Target shape:

```
segments/rate_limit/
  mod.rs            (re-exports + module decls; per ADR-0021 rule 4)
  format.rs         (existing rate_limit_format.rs contents minus the parts that move)
  config.rs         (CommonRateLimitConfig + extras parsing)
  window.rs         (UsageWindow + WindowResolution + HideReason — the new seam)
  five_hour.rs      (RateLimit5hSegment + RateLimit5hResetSegment)
  seven_day.rs      (RateLimit7dSegment + RateLimit7dResetSegment)
  tests.rs          (per ADR-0021 rule 2 — sibling once we're a folder)
```

**DRY refactor (architecture review 2026-05-02 candidates 1+4).** Today rate_limit_5h vs rate_limit_7d are near-clones differing only in the window selector (`e.five_hour` vs `e.seven_day`) plus a 5h-only "JSONL block inactive; hide" branch. Same for the `*_reset` pair. Introduce a `UsageWindow` accessor in `window.rs` that takes `&UsageData` and returns a `WindowResolution` enum (Endpoint bucket / Jsonl 5h window / Jsonl 7d window) or a typed `HideReason`. The four segments collapse to thin wrappers that delegate render to a shared function parameterized by `UsageWindow`.

Per the design conversation: keep 4 named segment structs (preserves grep-ability and the `[segments.rate_limit_5h]` config-table dispatch in builder.rs); use typed `HideReason` so each segment emits its own `lsm_debug!` call site (preserves ops grep-ability of the hide-string wording).

Out of scope: extra_usage and tokens are usage-driven but not windowed — they don't fit the UsageWindow seam and stay alone.

Acceptance: 4 segment files collapse to 2 (five_hour.rs, seven_day.rs) with thin segment wrappers; UsageWindow enum + WindowResolution + HideReason live in window.rs; all existing tests pass; rate_limit segment behavior is unchanged (verified by snapshot or string-equal asserts).

Driven by ADR-0021 follow-up #4 + 2026-05-02 architecture review candidates 1+4. Supersedes the deferred lsm-tek6 (DepName newtype) which can be revisited once the window seam exists.
close_reason: Phase 2: UsageWindow seam (window.rs) + per-window resolve_*_reset functions collapse the Endpoint-vs-JSONL match dance into typed calls (-305 LOC net). rate_limit folder shape settled: config.rs split from format.rs (CommonRateLimitConfig, format enums, parse_*_format, PRIORITY); file pairs merged (five_hour_reset.rs into five_hour.rs, seven_day_reset.rs into seven_day.rs). Workspace-level parse_bool extracted to segments/extras.rs (git_branch + 4 rate-limit segments stop reaching across families). 7d-reset asymmetry encoded in the type system: resolve_seven_day_reset returns Result<DateTime<Utc>, _> (no JsonlBlockEnd variant) per ADR-0013, eliminating the unreachable!() arm. Phase 1 (folder graduation) shipped as 5378415.

title: Folder-graduate input.rs + layout.rs to extract test blocks per ADR-0021 rule 2
description:
Under ADR-0021 rule 2, sibling \`tests.rs\` files are only available once a flat \`.rs\` file graduates to \`foo/mod.rs\`. The \`#[path]\` form is forbidden by rule 2 and Confirmation criterion 3.

Two flat files have inline test blocks dominating their content but are not otherwise covered by the planned folder graduations (rate_limit / builder / data_context):

- \`crates/linesmith-core/src/input.rs\` — 2280 LOC total, 1118 LOC tests (49% tests, but the largest absolute test block in the workspace; the implementation half is also 1161 LOC and would benefit from a sub-concept split per rule 3).
- \`crates/linesmith-core/src/layout.rs\` — 1793 LOC total, 1551 LOC tests (86% tests).

For each: graduate to \`foo/mod.rs\` + \`foo/tests.rs\`. Within \`foo/\`, optionally split the implementation by sub-concept if rule 3 (≥3 concepts) applies.

The other inline-test-heavy files (\`credentials.rs\`, \`cascade.rs\`, \`segments/builder.rs\`, \`jsonl.rs\`) are covered by beads lsm-NEW-4/5/6 — their test extraction comes free with their planned folder splits.

Acceptance: input/ and layout/ folders exist with mod.rs + tests.rs; all import sites updated; \`mise run check\` + \`mise run test\` green.

Driven by ADR-0021 follow-up #3.
close_reason: Folder-graduated input.rs (2280 LOC → mod.rs:1162 + tests.rs:1116) and layout.rs (1793 LOC → mod.rs:444 + tests.rs:1349) per ADR-0021 rule 2. Pure mechanical extraction of inline mod tests {} blocks to sibling tests.rs files (4-space dedent + #[cfg(test)] mod tests; declared in mod.rs). One drive-by fix: include_bytes!('../tests/fixtures/...') in input/tests.rs:264 became '../../tests/fixtures/...' for the deeper file path. layout/mod.rs:243 keeps the inline #[cfg(test)] fn render_items helper since it accesses private impl items (mirrors the lsm-p50v Credentials::for_testing pattern). External crate::input::X / crate::layout::X paths unchanged. mise run check + 1524 tests green. Closes the seven-bead ADR-0021 follow-up sequence (started lsm-v1ec → lsm-zou5 → lsm-oszc → lsm-0a4e → lsm-p50v → lsm-iash → lsm-8reb).

title: Rename errors.rs → error.rs + verify linesmith-plugin placement
description:
ADR-0021 rule 5 standardizes on singular `error.rs` to match ecosystem convention (hyper, reqwest, sqlx, fd, bat). Two existing files need renaming:

- `crates/linesmith-core/src/data_context/errors.rs` → `crates/linesmith-core/src/data_context/error.rs`
- `crates/linesmith-plugin/src/errors.rs` → `crates/linesmith-plugin/src/error.rs`

Update all import sites; the rename is otherwise mechanical.

**Placement check (the non-mechanical part).** Rule 5 says crate-root `error.rs` is for cross-cutting errors and module-root for module-scoped domains. `linesmith-plugin/src/errors.rs` lives at the crate root — confirm whether that's still right under the new rule. If the plugin crate's errors are genuinely cross-cutting across discovery/registry/engine/header, keep the placement. If they cluster around a single concept, file a follow-up to relocate.

Acceptance: both files renamed singular; import sites updated; placement of linesmith-plugin's error.rs explicitly documented (either in the file's header doc or as a closing note on this bead).

Driven by ADR-0021 follow-up #2.
close_reason: Renamed errors.rs → error.rs in linesmith-core/data_context (module-scoped) and linesmith-plugin (crate-root, placement confirmed cross-cutting per rule 5). 9 files updated: import paths, rustdoc intra-doc links, pub mod declarations, pub use re-exports. Rename invisible at crate boundary.

title: Migrate per-crate lints to [workspace.lints]
description:
Consolidate the per-crate `unsafe_code = "forbid"` configs (currently in linesmith-core, linesmith-plugin, linesmith Cargo.tomls) into a single `[workspace.lints]` block in the root Cargo.toml. Add `unreachable_pub = "warn"` (rust) and `clippy::redundant_pub_crate = "warn"` so ADR-0021 rule 6 (visibility ladder) is mechanically enforced rather than prose.

Preserve linesmith-plugin's existing `[lints.clippy] disallowed_methods = "allow"` as a per-crate override — that crate is the *home* of the disallowed method (`linesmith_plugin::build_engine`), and without the override the workspace-level lint from clippy.toml (per ADR-0020) would fire on its own implementation.

Each member crate should declare `[lints] workspace = true` to opt in. MSRV is 1.85, well above the 1.74 needed for `[workspace.lints]`.

Acceptance: `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace` is green; the existing `unsafe_code = "forbid"` rules survive in workspace block; linesmith-plugin's clippy override survives.

Driven by ADR-0021 follow-up #1.
close_reason: Centralized lints in [workspace.lints]: unsafe_code (forbid), unreachable_pub (warn), clippy::redundant_pub_crate (warn). linesmith-plugin keeps inline-duplicate + disallowed_methods carve-out (stable Cargo doesn't support per-lint workspace inheritance alongside the override). unreachable_pub caught StatusContext::normalize → pub(super). Drift detection filed as lsm-adv4.

title: Integration test: plugin log() output flows through LINESMITH_LOG when host emitter installed
description:
Per pr-test-analyzer on lsm-v2o3, the install_warn_emitter wiring at linesmith-core/src/runtime/plugins.rs (which bridges plugin log() to lsm_warn!) has no end-to-end test that proves the bridge actually fires. Plugin-side rate-limit tests assert against LOG_EMITTED counters directly, never through the emitter.

Add an integration test in crates/linesmith/tests/ (or driver.rs tests) that:
1. Sets LINESMITH_LOG=warn
2. Invokes cli_main with a config pointing at a plugin whose render() calls log("hello")
3. Asserts captured stderr contains 'linesmith [warn] plugin <id>: hello'

Then a paired test with LINESMITH_LOG=off asserts the line is suppressed. This catches the regression silent-failure-hunter and Codex flagged on lsm-v2o3 (eprintln fallback bypassing LINESMITH_LOG) at integration level rather than relying on visual inspection of driver.rs wiring.

Note: existing 'host_log_invokable_from_script' inside linesmith-plugin only smoke-tests that log() doesn't panic. The OnceLock is one-shot per process, so the integration test needs careful isolation (likely a #[test] that runs cli_main once with a captured stderr writer). Source: pr-review-toolkit pr-test-analyzer.
close_reason: Added crates/linesmith/tests/log_bridge.rs with two subprocess-based integration tests: LINESMITH_LOG=warn asserts the captured stderr contains the literal 'linesmith [warn]: plugin echo: hello'; LINESMITH_LOG=off asserts neither the message body nor the warn-level prefix appears (matches both core-emitter and plugin-fallback formats — drops the colon to catch the colonless eprintln! fallback). Subprocess via env!(CARGO_BIN_EXE_linesmith) sidesteps the OnceLock-per-process isolation problem; env inherits the runner's vars (Windows portability) and overrides only XDG_CONFIG_HOME + LINESMITH_LOG, removing LINESMITH_CONFIG to prevent override of the fixture's config-discovery. 2 follow-ups filed: lsm-diko (subprocess timeout watchdog) and lsm-5ygs (LOG_LINES_PER_PLUGIN integration coverage).

title: Narrow linesmith-core::plugins re-exports to items only
description:
Per type-design review on lsm-v2o3, linesmith-core/src/plugins/mod.rs re-exports BOTH items (PluginError, PluginRegistry, etc.) AND submodules (engine, errors, registry, header, discovery) from linesmith-plugin. This duplicates surface area: crate::plugins::PluginError and crate::plugins::errors::PluginError both resolve to the same type.

The submodule re-export was load-bearing during the lsm-v2o3 extraction — about 16 callsites in doctor/mod.rs and segment.rs use crate::plugins::engine::* and crate::plugins::errors::*. Mechanical pass to drop those prefixes (use the flat re-exported names instead) lets the linesmith_plugin submodule layout become a free refactor target. Without this, a future caller pinning crate::plugins::engine::install_warn_emitter freezes that incidental layout into the de-facto public surface.

Cost: ~5-10 line edits per affected file (doctor/mod.rs, segment.rs). Out of scope for lsm-v2o3 itself — the cleanup pass touches files lsm-v2o3 didn't, which violates the bead's scope discipline. Source: pr-review-toolkit type-design-analyzer.
close_reason: Dropped both the submodule re-exports (errors/header/registry/discovery) AND the flat plugin-type re-exports (PluginRegistry, PluginError, CompiledPlugin, etc.) from linesmith-core::plugins. Engine shim also removed — the bypass is now an explicit cross-crate import. Per consume-from-origin (Codex round 2 / 3 P2/P1 sharpening): each consumer reaches plugin types from linesmith_plugin directly. Cli adds linesmith-plugin as a direct dep; cli's own lib re-exports narrowed to pub(crate) so the published library surface stays minimal (cli, doctor, cli_main, CliEnv only). Workspace clippy.toml channels callers to linesmith_core::plugins::build_engine via disallowed_methods. Scope exceeded the bead's nominal text; release commit will use refactor! + BREAKING CHANGE footer so release-plz bumps to 0.2.0.

title: release: verify release-plz publishes linesmith-core before linesmith on next release
description:
After lsm-1nh0 lands, the release pipeline now needs to publish two crates atomically: linesmith-core and linesmith. cargo 1.90+ supports cargo publish --workspace for atomic interdependent-crate publishing.

release-plz (used in .github/workflows/release-plz.yml) handles dependency-ordered publishing automatically: it walks the workspace dep graph and publishes leaves first. So in theory the next release will publish linesmith-core first, then linesmith. But this needs verification:

1. On the next release-plz PR, confirm both crates appear in the version-bump commit
2. After merge, watch the Release PLZ workflow logs to confirm publish order: linesmith-core THEN linesmith
3. If publish order is wrong or fails, options:
   - Add explicit ordering via release-plz.toml [[package]] sections
   - Switch to cargo 1.90+ cargo publish --workspace if release-plz lags
   - Add CI step that runs cargo package --workspace as a smoke test pre-publish

Acceptance: a test release (could be 0.1.2 with a no-op feat commit) successfully publishes both crates to crates.io in the right order, and `cargo install linesmith` still works on the new version.

Filed during lsm-1nh0 review by Codex's P1 publish-blocker finding.
close_reason: Empirically verified on the v0.1.2 release: release-plz published linesmith-core@0.1.2 first, then linesmith@0.1.2, both via OIDC trusted publishing. Cargo.toml only had [workspace.package].version bumped (1-line diff) — release-plz did NOT auto-bump [workspace.dependencies].linesmith-core.version, but this turned out to be a non-issue because cargo's caret-default semantics on '0.1.1' resolve to the latest matching ^0.1.1 (which is 0.1.2 once published). Cargo 1.90+ atomic workspace publish mode would also handle this transparently via temp-registry. Loose-pin pattern works correctly for our scaffolding-publish use case.

title: adrs: write superseding ADR for linesmith-core publish-from-v0.1 reality
description:
ADR-0018 §Decision Outcome states: 'linesmith-core — Workspace-internal in v0.1; potential publish post-v1.0 if a third-party consumer asks.'

Empirically (verified during lsm-1nh0 implementation), this is impossible in cargo today. cargo publish requires every transitive dep of a published package to (a) have a version requirement AND (b) be resolvable from crates.io. A path-only dep with no version, OR a dep marked publish=false, fails manifest validation at package time. No flag (--no-verify, --allow-dirty, --dry-run) bypasses this. Survey of every comparable Rust workspace (ripgrep, serde, tokio, clap, ratatui, starship, bat, eza) found the universal pattern: unpublished workspace members are always leaves (xtask, fuzz, benches, examples) — no mainstream Rust project ships a published binary that depends on a publish=false library crate.

ADR-0018 §Open follow-ups noted 'Reserve linesmith-core, linesmith-plugin, linesmith-cli on crates.io with stub 0.0.0 placeholder releases (defends against name-squatting; [package.publish] = false keeps them local until v0.2)' but did not reconcile that linesmith's existing crates.io publish workflow forces real (not stub) versions for any dep linesmith uses.

Resolution chosen during lsm-1nh0: linesmith-core publishes alongside linesmith starting v0.1.x as workspace-internal-scaffolding. Same pattern as serde_derive / tokio-macros / clap_derive: crate exists on registry to satisfy cargo's transitive-dep rule, not to advertise stable API. Crate description signals 'No SemVer guarantee for direct dependents — depend on the linesmith binary or accept breakage between minor versions'.

Acceptance:
- New ADR (next number after 0018) under docs/adrs/ following MADR v4.0
- Status: accepted
- Cites lsm-1nh0 evidence (cargo package empirical test, workspace survey)
- Updates ADR-0018 status to 'superseded by [new ADR]'
- Per AGENTS.md ADR immutability rule: ADR-0018 is NOT rewritten, just gets the superseded status footer

Filed during lsm-1nh0 review after Codex caught the publish blocker.
close_reason: ADR-0019 written documenting the publish-from-v0.1 reality. ADR-0018 status updated to 'superseded by [ADR-0019]' per AGENTS.md immutability rule (body untouched, single-line status-footer change). ADR-0019 covers: empirical cargo behavior verified on 1.94.1 (both pre-fix and post-add-version failure modes shown), workspace survey of serde/tokio/ratatui (leaf-pattern) plus ripgrep/clap (publish-everything) and starship/bat/eza (single-crate non-workspaces), serde_derive precedent (~53M downloads/month per crates.io 2026-05-01) with explicit acknowledgment that linesmith-core's description-level disclaimer strengthens the implicit precedent convention, release-plz multi-crate ordering noted as expected with first-release verification tracked in lsm-8tam. Closes the publish-blocker resolution loop.

title: env: thread non-UTF-8 XDG/HOME paths through CliEnv + EnvVarState
description:
XdgEnv now uses Option<OsString> internally and from_os_options preserves non-UTF-8 paths, but both call sites collapse them upstream:
- CliEnv (driver.rs:59-60) stores Option<String>, populated via std::env::var().ok() — drops VarError::NotUnicode
- EnvVarState::nonempty() in doctor/mod.rs:321-326 collapses NonUtf8(_) → None

Net: a user with XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/srv/café-bin in a non-UTF-8 locale silently loses their setting in both runtime and doctor paths, even though XdgEnv's plumbing could carry it.

AGENTS.md flags Unix-paths-as-byte-strings as a project rule. The fix requires:
- Widening CliEnv::xdg_config_home and ::home to Option<OsString>, populated via std::env::var_os
- Threading EnvVarState::NonUtf8(raw) through doctor's runtime_xdg_env build (e.g. by mapping NonUtf8 → Some(raw))
- Updating tests that construct CliEnv with String literals

Convergent finding from lsm-e4m1 code-reviewer + silent-failure-hunter passes.
notes:
**Scope addition (2026-05-02 architecture review):** the env-cascade triple is open-coded at 4 sites with inconsistent empty-string handling — fold into this bead's surface rather than ship a separate refactor.

Sites:
- linesmith-core/src/data_context/xdg.rs:44-46 — (XDG_CACHE_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, HOME)
- linesmith-core/src/data_context/credentials.rs:429-431 — (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, HOME)
- linesmith-core/src/data_context/jsonl.rs:272-278 — XDG_CONFIG_HOME with non_empty() helper
- linesmith-core/src/config.rs:521-523 — (LINESMITH_CONFIG, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, HOME)

Only jsonl.rs has the non_empty guard; others silently treat \"\" as set. While widening these to OsString, give them a single typed seam (something like EnvCascade { override_key, xdg_subdir, home_subdir }) so empty-string semantics become uniform and lsm-0a4e closes the door on a 5th open-coded site appearing later.
close_reason: Threaded non-UTF-8 XDG/HOME paths through CliEnv + EnvVarState. CliEnv::{linesmith_config, xdg_config_home, home} widened to Option<OsString> via var_os. EnvVarState::NonUtf8 widened from String to { lossy: String, raw: OsString } with new nonempty_os() accessor. resolve_config_path widened to Option<&OsStr>. Doctor migrations: runtime XdgEnv config build, derive_cache_root, find_claude_binary (signature widened to Option<&OsStr>), and snapshot_claude_home call site all use nonempty_os() so non-UTF-8 paths flow through to all 3 doctor categories (config, cache, claude_code). Test fixtures converted from lossy String to OsString. Type-design refactor (NonUtf8 dual-storage → single OsString) filed as lsm-ne8y; real-bytes regression test filed as lsm-1o5e.

title: Finalize linesmith-cli rename + workspace cleanup + cargo-dist verify
description:
Final bead: rename the binary-producing crate to linesmith-cli (if not already renamed in lsm-1nh0), align Cargo.toml metadata across all three crates, verify cargo-dist + the release pipeline still produce the same artifacts, update AGENTS.md to document the workspace structure.

Tasks:
- Rename crates/linesmith → crates/linesmith-cli if .3 deferred this (use git mv to preserve history)
- Cargo.toml: package.name = 'linesmith-cli', [[bin]] name = 'linesmith' (binary name unchanged)
- Workspace.dependencies: ensure all three crates inherit consistently (no drift between core, plugin, cli)
- Workspace.lints: confirm shared lint config applies cleanly per crate
- AGENTS.md update: new ## Architecture section or expand the existing one to document the three-crate split + the dependency graph + which crate owns what
- cargo-dist: verify the release workflow still produces a single 'linesmith' binary (smoke run cargo dist plan)
- CI verify: GitHub Actions matrix passes for the workspace shape (each crate's clippy + test still gates)
- Doctor parity audit: file follow-up beads for any mirror that's still in place after the workspace lands (likely zero — runtime predicates should all be directly callable now)

Acceptance: workspace stable; cargo-dist plan output matches pre-split; AGENTS.md documents the new shape; lsm-2it2 (parity audit) closes if no new mirrors surface; mise run check + test + the full release pipeline (when next exercised) green.

Per ADR-0018. Depends on lsm-v2o3.
close_reason: CLI stays as 'linesmith' (already published on crates.io). Rename to 'linesmith-cli' would have broken the established install path (cargo install linesmith) per ADR-0019. Captured in lsm-v2o3 implementation notes; lsm-opc5 will record the cli-naming deviation in a new ADR.

title: Extract linesmith-plugin (rhai engine + caps + discovery + registry)
description:
Move the rhai plugin host out of the cli into a new linesmith-plugin crate. ctx_mirror.rs (DataContext → rhai::Map adapter) moves to cli/ FIRST so plugin/ is fully self-contained — no linesmith domain types in the public surface.

Pre-step (single PR):
- Move crates/linesmith-cli/src/plugins/ctx_mirror.rs → crates/linesmith-cli/src/ctx_mirror.rs (or keep under cli/src/plugins/ subdir as namespacing — see ADR-0018 open follow-ups)
- Verify ctx_mirror imports nothing from plugins/{engine, errors, discovery, registry} except what passes through the rhai surface

Then:
- New crates/linesmith-plugin/Cargo.toml with rhai as the headline dep, package.publish = false, workspace.dependencies inherited where applicable
- Move crates/linesmith-cli/src/plugins/{engine,errors,discovery,registry,mod}.rs → crates/linesmith-plugin/src/
- Public API takes rhai::Map constructed by the consumer; pub use rhai; for version-pinning
- Generic over consumer's @data_deps shape: Vec<String> at the engine layer; cli maps to its DataDep enum at registration time (per ADR-0018 grilling Q3 conclusion)
- Public API: PluginEngine, PluginCaps, PluginRegistry, CompiledPlugin, PluginMetadata, PluginError; build_engine(caps), discover_plugins(dir), compile_plugin, render
- Doctor's PluginRegistry::load_with_xdg call routes through the new crate; parity-rule checked

Acceptance: linesmith-plugin builds standalone (cargo check -p linesmith-plugin); no linesmith-core types leak into its pub surface; doctor's plugins category still passes for real plugins; mise run check + test green.

Per ADR-0018. Depends on lsm-1nh0 (workspace setup must exist).
notes:
Implementation notes (what shipped vs. the original description):

- CLI was NOT renamed to linesmith-cli; stays as `linesmith` (already published, see ADR-0019). lsm-494l ('Finalize linesmith-cli rename') should be closed wontfix.
- ctx_mirror did NOT move to cli. The bridge layer (ctx_mirror, RhaiSegment, output) stayed in linesmith-core. linesmith-plugin holds only engine/errors/discovery/header/registry — pure rhai host with no linesmith domain types in its public surface. Reason: 'cli should use not define' design call; moving ctx_mirror would have cascaded segment.rs and core::segments::builder out of core. See lsm-opc5 for the ADR addendum.
- Vec<DataDep> at the seam decoupled to Vec<String> per the bead description; KNOWN_DEPS made pub for cross-crate drift tests.
- linesmith-core::plugins::build_engine is now a wrapper that installs the warn-emitter bridge (so plugin log() output respects LINESMITH_LOG) before delegating to linesmith_plugin::build_engine. Closes Codex-flagged regression for direct API consumers using linesmith_core::plugins::*.
- Engine submodule re-export in linesmith-core/plugins/mod.rs is selective (omits build_engine) so the bypass path can't be reached accidentally.

Follow-up beads filed:
- lsm-tek6: DepName newtype at the seam (defer to v0.2)
- lsm-doar: narrow linesmith-core::plugins re-exports to items only
- lsm-65r7: integration test for LINESMITH_LOG gating end-to-end
- lsm-opc5: ADR recording bridge-stays-in-core deviation
close_reason: Extracted linesmith-plugin workspace crate (rhai engine/discovery/registry/header/errors); pure host with no linesmith domain types in pub surface, declared deps cross as Vec<String>. Bridge (ctx_mirror, RhaiSegment, output) stayed in linesmith-core per 'core should hold the bridge' call. linesmith-core::plugins::build_engine wraps the bare constructor with a one-shot LINESMITH_LOG bridge install so every entry point through core picks it up. KNOWN_DEPS exposed for cross-crate drift tests. 4 follow-ups filed (lsm-tek6, lsm-doar, lsm-65r7, lsm-opc5).

title: Cargo workspace skeleton + extract linesmith-core
description:
Convert the single linesmith crate into a cargo workspace and move data_context/, segments/, theme/, layout/, input/, config/, presets/, runtime/ into a new linesmith-core crate.

Workspace setup:
- Root Cargo.toml gains [workspace] with members = ['crates/linesmith-core', 'crates/linesmith-cli'] (linesmith-plugin lands in next bead)
- workspace.dependencies for shared deps (serde, serde_json, gix, rhai, etc.)
- workspace.lints for shared lint config
- crates/linesmith-core/Cargo.toml: package.publish = false (workspace-internal in v0.1 per ADR-0018)
- existing crates/linesmith renamed in place to crates/linesmith-cli (or kept as crates/linesmith for now if rename is risky; .5 handles the final rename)
- linesmith-cli depends on linesmith-core via workspace path

Code moves:
- crates/linesmith/src/{data_context,segments,theme,layout,input,config,presets,runtime}/ → crates/linesmith-core/src/
- linesmith-core/src/lib.rs re-exports the public surface; pub use core::* in cli for backwards-compat during transition
- pub(crate) → pub for everything cli needs from core (per the runtime-extraction-already-done pattern)
- doctor/ stays in cli (depends on core's runtime predicates)

CI:
- mise run check should iterate per-crate or use --workspace
- cargo-dist config verified to still produce a single 'linesmith' binary from cli

Acceptance: workspace builds; mise run check + test green; cargo-dist dry-run produces the same release artifacts as before; no behavior change for end users.

Per ADR-0018. Depends on lsm-vsab + lsm-e4m1 landing first.
close_reason: Cargo workspace skeleton + linesmith-core extraction. New crate at crates/linesmith-core/ hosts data_context, input, config, logging, theme, segments, layout, presets, plugins, runtime modules. crates/linesmith stays at the same directory + package name (preserves crates.io continuity); lib.rs shrinks to cli/doctor/driver + pub use linesmith_core::*. linesmith-core publishes as workspace-internal scaffolding (serde_derive pattern) — Codex P1 publish blocker resolved per Option A; ADR-0018 amendment tracked as lsm-y7md. Doctor parity hardened: 7 #[non_exhaustive] enum fallback _ arms in cli; 3 critical sites (load_config, read_config_at, snapshot_credentials) wired with explicit diagnostics; check_plugins_compile uses new PluginError::kind() to avoid leaking author-controlled message strings. cargo package --workspace --allow-dirty succeeds; 1113 + 362 lib + 42 integration tests pass; cargo dist plan still produces single linesmith binary across 7 targets. Filed lsm-9t9f, lsm-yw3r, lsm-y7md, lsm-8tam as follow-ups.

title: Extract runtime predicates from driver.rs into a dedicated module
description:
Sweep candidate #4. Lift the runtime predicates currently buried as private fns in driver.rs into a new crates/linesmith/src/runtime/ module. Still inside the single crate — workspace split happens in the next bead and this prep makes that move mechanical.

Predicates to extract (driver.rs line numbers):
- :792 load_plugins
- :831 xdg_segments_dir
- :904 user_themes_dir
- :914 build_theme_registry
- :984 resolve_theme
- :1013 load_config
- :935 resolve_color_capability

Each becomes pub(crate) in linesmith::runtime::*.

Doctor stops mirroring:
- snapshot_plugins → call runtime::load_plugins directly
- collect_known_theme_names → call runtime::build_theme_registry directly
- read_config_at → call Config::load_validated via runtime (closes lsm-8sus)
- xdg_subdir → call runtime::xdg::resolve_subdir (depends on lsm-vsab landing first)

Acceptance: doctor/snapshot.rs shrinks; the lsm-efmu parity-rule audit needs to find no new mirrors after this lands. mise run check + test green. driver.rs becomes 'argv → action → call into runtime → render'.

Why before the workspace split: the runtime/ module is the natural inhabitant of linesmith-core; lifting it inside the existing crate first means the eventual core extraction is a directory move, not a refactor. Doing both in one commit would couple two unrelated risks.

Per ADR-0018 driving deepening candidates. Closes lsm-8sus when read_config_at routes through Config::load_validated.
close_reason: Lifted runtime predicates (load_plugins, xdg_segments_dir, user_themes_dir, build_theme_registry, load_config) into crates/linesmith/src/runtime/{config,plugins,themes}.rs. Doctor + driver now share Config::load_validated through ConfigLoadOutcome (carries unknown-key warnings on every variant including ParseError/IoError). Doctor's snapshot_plugins, collect_known_theme_names, read_config_at delegate directly. doctor::from_process builds runtime_xdg_env once and reuses across predicate calls. Closes lsm-8sus parity angle. Filed lsm-zaom (doctor folds plugin load_errors), lsm-0a4e (non-UTF-8 XDG/HOME propagation), lsm-4av2 (ConfigLoadOutcome refactor), lsm-iqio (Windows separator sweep).

title: Prep: lift credentials env reads + collapse XDG cascade
description:
Two architecture-sweep candidates landed before the workspace split so the core/cli boundary is sharp instead of scattered.

Candidate #1 (credentials env-snapshot):
- Lift FileCascadeEnv (data_context/credentials.rs:370) to pub
- Change resolve_credentials() signature to take env state as a parameter instead of reading std::env::var_os internally
- Process-env reads happen at the call boundary in driver.rs once
- Doctor's snapshot_credentials drops the is_path_source carve-out
- Tests stop needing process-env mutation

Candidate #2 (XDG cascade collapse):
- Three runtime adapters today implement the same XDG_*_HOME → linesmith → <subdir> cascade: data_context/cache.rs:211 (default_root), driver.rs:831 (xdg_segments_dir), driver.rs:904 (user_themes_dir). Plus doctor/snapshot.rs:30 (xdg_subdir) mirroring all three.
- Extract data_context/xdg::resolve_subdir(scope: XdgScope, sub: &str, env: &XdgEnv) -> Option<PathBuf>
- XdgScope::{Cache, Config}; one cascade definition
- driver builds XdgEnv from CliEnv once; doctor builds one from EnvVarState

Acceptance: mise run check + test green. snapshot_credentials no longer takes three EnvVarState params. xdg::resolve_subdir is the single XDG cascade implementation; default_root, xdg_segments_dir, user_themes_dir, xdg_subdir all delegate.

Why before the workspace split: makes the core/cli boundary 'data layer / wiring layer' cleanly. After-the-split version of this would have to grapple with 'this fn reads env, do I leave it or refactor?' on every move.

Per ADR-0018 driving deepening candidates.
close_reason: XDG cascade collapsed into single source data_context::xdg with OsString-typed env (preserves non-UTF-8 byte paths); cache::default_root + driver::{xdg_segments_dir,user_themes_dir} + doctor::{xdg_subdir,derive_cache_root} all delegate. credentials::FileCascadeEnv lifted to pub with new() constructor + from_process_env() factory using var_os; resolve_credentials_with(env) is the explicit-env companion to resolve_credentials(). doctor::snapshot_credentials takes FileCascadeEnv directly so non-UTF-8 paths flow through (was building env via EnvVarState::nonempty() which collapsed NonUtf8 → None, breaking parity with runtime resolve_credentials). 1474 lib + 16 doctor_integration + 16 integration + 10 plugins green. ADR-0018 lands as the driving doc for the whole core/plugin/cli workspace epic.

title: (EPIC) Split linesmith into core / plugin / cli workspace crates
description:
Per ADR-0018: cargo workspace with linesmith-core (workspace-internal, may publish post-v1.0), linesmith-plugin (workspace-internal in v0.1+v0.2; publish post-v0.2), linesmith-cli (binary-only, never publishes as lib).

Sliced into 5 beads. Each gates on the previous so mise run check is green at every step:
- .1 prep deepening: credentials env-snapshot (sweep #1) + XDG cascade collapse (sweep #2)
- .2 extract runtime predicates from driver.rs (sweep #4) — still inside the single crate
- .3 cargo workspace skeleton + extract linesmith-core
- .4 extract linesmith-plugin (with ctx_mirror.rs moved to cli/ first)
- .5 rename remaining crate to linesmith-cli + workspace cleanup + cargo-dist verify

Acceptance: workspace builds clean; mise run check + test green; cargo-dist still produces a single 'linesmith' binary; doctor parity-rule beads (lsm-2it2, lsm-8sus, lsm-x9vo) close as runtime predicates become directly callable.

Driving ADR: docs/adrs/0018-cargo-workspace-core-plugin-cli.md
close_reason: Workspace split shipped per ADR-0018: linesmith-core + linesmith-plugin + linesmith-cli, all 5 children complete, mise run check + test green, cargo-dist still produces single linesmith binary.

title: doctor cache root probe writes to filesystem (read-only contract)
description:
Codex flagged during lsm-l35.8/.9/.10 review: stat_cache_root in crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs (lines ~430-465, currently around 457-460) probes cache directory writability by creating a temp file in the first existing ancestor directory when the cache root itself doesn't exist yet (e.g. fresh $XDG_CACHE_HOME). This violates the doctor command's documented read-only contract.

The probe-write was originally added in lsm-l35.6 fix round to address the parity violation where the previous immediate-parent probe failed for valid first-run setups (XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/new-root where the cache parent doesn't exist but runtime's create_dir_all walks recursively). Walking the parent chain fixed the parity but kept the probe-write.

Why this matters:
- Plain 'linesmith doctor' on fresh setups now performs filesystem writes
- Write-restricted or audit-monitored environments (corporate macOS / sandboxed builds) can fail or trigger noise on a command users invoke for diagnostics
- Spec implies doctor is read-only (no "will modify state" warning anywhere)

Options:
1. Remove the writability probe entirely; report cache state as 'absent, will be created on first run'. Loses one signal but matches read-only contract.
2. Move the writability probe behind an opt-in flag (--cache-probe), defer until users actually report cache-write failures. Probably overkill for v0.1.
3. Use access(W_OK) (read-only OS call) instead of probe-write. Loses some signal vs actual write attempt but stays read-only.

Recommended: option 1 for v0.1 — the cache failure modes that matter (read-only filesystem, missing perms) usually surface as runtime errors anyway, and doctor's job is to surface those if they happen, not to predict them.

References:
- crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs (stat_cache_root)
- lsm-l35.6 fix round commit (parity walk fix)
- Codex review output at /private/tmp/.../bvfxhidvl.output
close_reason: stat_cache_root rewritten to read-only stat per option 1 from the bead. New CacheRootState variants: Exists (PASS), Absent (PASS, runtime creates on first fetch), NotADirectory (WARN, real read-only-detectable misconfig), Unreadable{message} (WARN, surfaces io::Error), Unresolved (SKIP). Dropped ParentWritable + ParentNotWritable (the probe-write paths). Real write failures (read-only fs, missing perms, NFS root-squash, immutable flags) now surface at first runtime fetch as concrete errors rather than being predicted by a probe-write that violated doctor's read-only contract. Spec updated: §Cache check catalog row + §Edge cases symlink-to-readonly-fs + change-log entry. Tests: 3 new check_cache_dir tests (PASS-on-Absent / WARN-on-NotADirectory / WARN-on-Unreadable), 2 obsolete tests removed; plain-mode coverage entries replaced (cache.absent_first_run / cache.not_a_directory / cache.unreadable). 1461 lib + 16 doctor_integration + 16 integration + 10 plugins green; mise run check clean; live binary smoke-tested.

title: Audit .3-.5 doctor snapshot helpers against runtime predicates
description:
The lsm-efmu parity-rule audit (closed as part of lsm-l35.6) applied the rule to .6's new code (Plugins via PluginRegistry::load_with_xdg, Git via resolve_repo) but did not sweep prior-slice snapshot helpers. Codex caught two .5-era violations during the .6 review that the audit was supposed to find:

1. stat_cache_root: probe-write only in immediate parent; failed for valid first-run setups like XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/new-root where the cache parent doesn't exist yet but the runtime's atomic_write_json calls create_dir_all recursively. (Fixed in .6 fix round — walks parent chain to first existing ancestor.)

2. stat_usage_lock: hand-rolled JSON peek instead of delegating to LockStore::read; disagreed with runtime on legacy non-JSON locks (mtime fallback) and pathological far-future blocked_until (runtime caps). (Fixed in .6 fix round — delegates to LockStore::read.)

Both fixes landed; this bead exists to ensure no other latent parity violations escaped the audit in the .3 (Config), .4 (Claude Code), and .5 (Credentials/Cache/Endpoint) snapshot helpers.

Acceptance: trace each snapshot helper in doctor/snapshot.rs and confirm it either (a) calls the runtime predicate directly (resolve_credentials, fetch_usage, ThemeRegistry::with_user_themes, etc.), or (b) replicates the runtime's predicate exactly with a comment citing the runtime function it mirrors. Any unverified delta becomes a follow-up bead. Likely candidates: stat_usage_json (uses CachedUsage deserialize — verify cached_at gate matches runtime), find_claude_binary (verify is_runnable mirrors which(1) on Unix), stat_claude_dir / stat_claude_sessions (verify against the runtime — if any consumer exists).
close_reason:
Audit complete across all 20 helpers in crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs.

Confirmed parity (call runtime predicate directly, no replication risk): snapshot_plugins → PluginRegistry::load_with_xdg; snapshot_git → resolve_repo; collect_known_theme_names → ThemeRegistry::with_built_ins().with_user_themes(); snapshot_credentials → resolve_credentials(); stat_usage_lock → LockStore::read.

Confirmed parity (mirror with citation, no runtime call needed): xdg_subdir mirrors driver.rs's xdg_segments_dir / user_themes_dir verbatim; derive_cache_root mirrors cache::default_root verbatim; stat_cache_root intentionally does NOT mirror runtime probe-write per lsm-oqm6 (now read-only stat).

Doctor-only with no runtime parity to violate: find_claude_binary / is_runnable (linesmith never shells out to claude); stat_plugin_dirs (supplementary diagnostic, not a parity replica); read_claude_json / stat_claude_dir / stat_claude_sessions (no runtime parser yet — ClaudeJson is a stub); snapshot_update_probe / classify_update_response_inner / clamp_diag / sanitize_tag (GitHub probe is doctor-only); collect_unexpected_endpoint_keys (doctor-specific); classify_endpoint_response severity differences from interpret_status are intentional and documented.

Two real gaps fixed inline:
1. probe_endpoint_via_ureq + classify_endpoint_response hardcoded Duration::from_secs(2) instead of reading fetcher::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT — replaced with the runtime constant so a future tuning flows through doctor automatically.
2. stat_usage_json's UTF-8-strict read_to_string diverges from runtime's fs::read + from_utf8 (silently collapses non-UTF-8 to miss). Added a citation comment explaining the intentional severity divergence: doctor surfaces corruption; runtime treats it as a transient miss to be overwritten on next fetch.

One gap filed as follow-up bead lsm-8sus (P3, v0.2):
- read_config_at uses bare toml::from_str, runtime uses Config::load_validated which warns on unknown keys. Doctor 'Config parses' PASSes on configs with typos like [segmnts.echo] that the runtime warns about. Real feature gap (needs new ConfigReadOutcome::LoadedWithWarnings variant + check), not just a citation; out of scope for the audit.

title: Doctor checks must use the same predicate as the runtime they diagnose
description:
silent-failure-hunter's lsm-l35.5 review surfaced a cross-cutting pattern: 5 of 7 silent-failure findings shared one root cause — doctor checks use cheaper / different validation logic than the runtime they're diagnosing. Examples flagged: stat_usage_json missing the cached_at <= now gate (fixed in l35.5), stat_cache_root false-PASS on permissions().readonly() (fixed), stat_usage_lock not cross-checking lock mtime against system clock (open).

The category 'Doctor' carries an implicit contract: PASS means 'the runtime will succeed when it consumes this state'. Today's checks promise less; without intervention, doctor's PASS verdicts will keep drifting away from runtime reality on every refactor of data_context/*.

Acceptance: every doctor check that inspects on-disk state delegates to (or thinly wraps) the runtime predicate. Where the runtime collapses many failure modes into 'cache miss', doctor SHOULD distinguish them (that's its job) — but the underlying parse/stat path must be shared. Expect ~3 helpers in data_context/ to expose validation predicates that doctor consumes via reference, plus a follow-up audit when l35.6 ships.
notes: Audit lens for lsm-l35.6 (Plugins + Git): every check delegates to the runtime predicate (PluginRegistry::load_with_xdg, gix::discover, etc.) rather than re-implementing validation. Rolled into l35.6's acceptance — closing this bead becomes part of l35.6's close criteria.
close_reason: Parity rule applied as part of l35.6: plugins category delegates to PluginRegistry::load_with_xdg (the runtime predicate via plugins/registry.rs), git category delegates to data_context::git::resolve_repo. Cache + credentials parity work landed in l35.5. Audit lens carried forward into the doctor module's design.

title: Doctor integration tests: --plain golden output + exit-code matrix + tree wrapping
description:
Round-trip integration tests for the assembled doctor command per docs/specs/doctor.md §Testing strategy §Integration tests.

**Tests:**
- --plain golden output: snapshot test for ASCII-only rendering (CI-friendly, log-capture-friendly)
- Exit-code matrix: all-PASS → 0, WARN-only → 0, any-FAIL → 1, usage error → 2
- Tree wrapping: render at 40, 60, 80, 120 cell widths; verify no broken box-drawing
- Short-circuit propagation: missing $HOME → file checks SKIP; config parse fail → segment checks SKIP; missing token → endpoint probe SKIP
- Non-tty stdout → WARN (not FAIL) so '--plain | tee' in CI doesn't gate exit-1
- Token redaction smoke: assert no bearer-token bytes in any output path

**Out of scope:** Per-category unit tests (live with each slice 2–6); --json output (deferred to v0.2).

**Acceptance:** Tests pass under 'mise run test'; golden snapshots committed; exit-code matrix exercised in CI.
close_reason: Doctor integration tests landed at crates/linesmith/tests/doctor_integration.rs. 16 tests cover: render-layer goldens for plain/default modes (full envelope + failure envelope), exit-code matrix (PASS/WARN/SKIP-only → 0; any FAIL → 1; FAIL-with-warnings → 1), plain-mode ASCII contract per spec §plain caveat (renderer strings only; user content passes through), summary separator pinning (default '·' vs plain '/'), token redaction smoke (no sk-ant-/Bearer/ya29./oat_ substrings), box-drawing-glyph absence (renderer remains line-based + width-agnostic), and CLI exit-code matrix via cli_main (unknown flag → 2; --help → 0 listing doctor; --plain outside doctor → 2). Added Report::new pub constructor (struct was #[non_exhaustive] + pub but had no constructor — unconstructible from outside the crate). Help text gap fixed: HELP missed 'linesmith doctor [--plain]' USAGE line and the 'doctor' SUBCOMMANDS entry — integration test caught it. Spec acceptance met: tests pass under 'mise run test'; goldens committed inline as raw strings (insta deferred — adds workspace dep cost not justified for v0.1).

title: linesmith init auto-runs doctor + --no-doctor opt-out
description:
Wire doctor into the 'linesmith init' onboarding flow per docs/specs/doctor.md §linesmith init integration.

**Scope:**
- After 'linesmith init' writes config.toml + prints Claude Code snippet, automatically run doctor
- Add '--no-doctor' flag to skip the auto-run (CI / scripted onboarding)
- Doctor failures during init should NOT cause init to exit non-zero (init succeeded; doctor is informational)
- Doctor output appears after the snippet, with a separator line

**Tension flagged in slice 1:** doctor is intentionally hidden from --help until slice .2 lands a useful catalog (lsm-l35.1 ships only one PASS check; advertising 'diagnose your setup' would be a false promise). When this slice lands, decide:

- (a) Init auto-running doctor IS the discoverability path — first-run users learn doctor exists by seeing it run after init. Defensible, ships now.
- (b) Defer slice .7 until doctor is discoverable in --help (i.e., wait for slice .2's catalog to expand first).

Recommendation: pick (a). Initialization is exactly the moment when 'see what doctor reports' is most useful, and the user is already engaged with the tool. But don't claim 'run linesmith doctor anytime' messaging in init's output until --help advertises it.

**Acceptance:** 'linesmith init' writes config and runs doctor; 'linesmith init --no-doctor' writes config without running doctor; init exit code reflects init outcome only, not doctor outcome.
close_reason: linesmith init now auto-runs doctor inline after writing config + snippet. --no-doctor opts out (CI / scripted onboarding). Spec §linesmith init integration: init's exit code propagates from doctor (a doctor FAIL after a clean init means the env around the new config is broken). Doctor inherits the resolved config path so it inspects exactly the file we just wrote, not whatever its own cascade re-resolves. Help text + USAGE updated. CLI parser rejects --no-doctor outside init. 6 new tests: 3 cli parser tests (parses, both flag orderings, rejected outside init), 3 driver integration tests (no-doctor skips, runs inline, exit-code propagation).

title: Doctor checks: Plugins + Git category
description:
Implement Plugins and Git check categories per docs/specs/doctor.md §Plugins, §Git.

**Plugins checks (doctor.md §Plugins):**
- Plugin discovery directory readable (XDG_CONFIG_HOME/linesmith/plugins)
- Each discovered .rhai file: parses, declares valid role, no panics on init
- 0-byte plugin file handling (per lsm-7wh follow-up — confirm spec/impl alignment)
- Reuse plugins::discovery + plugins::registry

**Git checks (doctor.md §Git):**
- git binary on PATH
- CWD is inside a git repo (or report 'not a git repo' as PASS — informational)
- Linked-worktree detection (per lsm-9to follow-up: verify worktree render path)
- Repo health smoke (HEAD resolvable)

**Acceptance:** Broken plugin → FAIL with file path + parse error; missing git → WARN; non-repo cwd → informational PASS; worktree → reports linked-worktree status.
close_reason: Plugins + Git: 7 checks across 2 categories (4 + 3). DoctorPluginsSnapshot consolidates with collect_known_segment_ids into one PluginRegistry::load_with_xdg call; DoctorGitSnapshot delegates to data_context::git::resolve_repo. PluginError variants partitioned at the orchestrator: Compile → plugins.compile, MalformedDataDeps/UnknownDataDep → plugins.deps_valid, IdCollision split by CollisionWinner (Plugin vs BuiltIn) into the two collision rows. Git carve-out: not-in-repo SKIPs when no git_* segment configured, WARNs when git_branch is enabled. Plain-mode contract preserved (HEAD label uses ASCII '->' arrow, not Unicode '→'). 18 new unit tests including PluginError partitioning, NotInRepo carve-out branches, and Head variant rendering.

title: Doctor checks: Credentials + Cache + Rate-limit endpoint category
description:
Implement the data-pipeline diagnostics: Credentials, Cache, and Rate-limit endpoint check categories per docs/specs/doctor.md §Credentials, §Cache, §Rate-limit endpoint. This is the slice that consumes the work originally scoped to lsm-dct (which closed administratively when its building blocks landed).

**Credentials checks (doctor.md §Credentials):**
- Credential source report: MacosKeychainPrimary / MacosKeychainMultiAccount / EnvDir / XdgConfig / ClaudeLegacy
- Path / service detail (no token bytes — REDACTED)
- Reuse data_context::credentials (lsm-a7a)

**Cache checks (doctor.md §Cache):**
- usage.json presence, cached_at, schema_version, TTL remaining, parse-ok
- usage.lock presence, blocked_until, TTL remaining
- Reuse multi-tier cache (lsm-b9w)

**Rate-limit endpoint (doctor.md §Rate-limit endpoint):**
- Always-run; no opt-in flag (--full was dropped from the v0.1 surface — see doctor.md change log 2026-04-29)
- Single dry-run probe against /api/oauth/usage with current credentials
- Report HTTP status + response time
- Do NOT mutate cache state (dry_run=true bypasses write-on-success)
- Transport-level errors (no network, captive portal, proxy refusal) → WARN, not FAIL (per spec edit)
- 4xx other than 429 → FAIL (definitive bad answer)
- Short-circuit: missing token → SKIP probe (doctor.md §Cross-category)

**Acceptance:** Token redaction verified by inspecting format! output (no bearer bytes); expired cache, active lock, credentials-but-no-network all produce distinct messages (WARN for offline, FAIL for revoked); no cache mutation during doctor run.
close_reason: Credentials + Cache + Rate-limit endpoint: 10 checks across 3 categories. Snapshot extends DoctorEnv with credentials/cache/endpoint fields. title: Doctor checks: Config category
description:

title: Doctor checks: Environment + Self category
description:
Implement the Environment and Self check categories per docs/specs/doctor.md §Check catalog.

**Environment checks (doctor.md §Environment):**
- HOME set + readable (FAIL if dirs::home_dir() returns None — short-circuits file-based checks in later slices per §Cross-category short-circuits)
- XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_CACHE_HOME (if set, valid path)
- TERM / COLORTERM (truecolor detection — uses existing theme::Capability infrastructure)
- NO_COLOR (PASS — user preference, not degradation)
- TTY status of stdout (non-tty / piped → WARN, not FAIL — see doctor.md §Cross-category)
- Terminal width (cols available for rendering; reuses linesmith::detect_terminal_width)

**Self checks (doctor.md §Self):**
- linesmith version (already wired in scaffold; expand with build metadata if available)
- Binary path / install location (std::env::current_exe)
- GitHub update check: always-run per spec edit on 2026-04-29 (--full was dropped). Transport-level errors → WARN, not FAIL (no network is a network problem, not a setup problem). 2s timeout.

**ID naming:** per spec convention (env.<check_name>, self.<check_name> in snake_case).

**Short-circuit propagation:** if HOME resolves to None, this slice marks the FAIL but doesn't try to short-circuit downstream — those slices (Config, Claude Code, Credentials, Cache) wire their own SKIP checks in lsm-l35.3 / .4 / .5.

**Out of scope:** Config/Claude Code/Credentials/Cache/Plugins/Git checks (separate slices).

**Acceptance:** Both categories appear in the report tree; non-tty stdout produces WARN not FAIL; NO_COLOR=1 produces PASS; offline run produces WARN on update check (not FAIL), exit 0; smoke test confirms 'linesmith doctor' shows useful output.
