title: Bench: end-to-end cold-start perf regression test (full render pipeline)
description:
linesmith-project-vision claims '<20ms cold start' as a flagship differentiator (#4: single-binary kills npx). lsm-rv4o covers git-segments perf budget but not full pipeline. Without an end-to-end benchmark gating CI, we could silently ship v1 at 30ms+ and lose the differentiator.

Scope:
- Criterion bench: full pipeline (process spawn → stdin parse → segment build → render → stdout write)
- Real CC stdin fixture (use captured payloads from lsm-mdd7 live-capture work)
- Multiple configurations: minimal (model + branch only), default preset, all-segments
- Baseline budget: <20ms p95 cold; <5ms p95 warm
- CI integration: bench runs on every PR; fail if >30% regression vs main baseline
- README: add 'How fast' section pointing to bench results

Acceptance: PRs that regress cold-start past threshold fail CI with a specific bench number; the project's flagship perf claim has automated regression protection.
close_reason: End-to-end render perf measurement shipped: (1) crates/linesmith/benches/render.rs as local regression detector with stable gix-init fixture repo and silent-segment-skip protection; (2) mise run bench:cold-start runs hyperfine against release binary for the user-facing wall-clock signal. CI perf gate was dropped after research (docs/research/perf-benchmarking-survey.md) showed peer Rust CLIs at our scale don't gate either; the path forward is CodSpeed for managed bare-metal CI (filed as follow-up). Release-time hyperfine publication also filed as follow-up.

title: Fetcher: honor HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY env vars for OAuth usage endpoint
description:
ureq agent in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/fetcher.rs uses default config — does not consult HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY env vars. ccstatusline (parity target) honors HTTPS_PROXY for direct Anthropic usage API calls. Without it, corporate-network users hit silent OAuth failures on day 1 and get 'no rate-limit data' with no actionable error.

Scope:
- fetcher.rs: read HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY at agent construction; configure ureq proxy
- Respect NO_PROXY exclusion list (api.anthropic.com may need to bypass corporate proxy in some configs)
- Surface proxy-resolution failures via existing UsageError taxonomy (not silent)
- Tests: agent honors HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY exclusion / malformed proxy URL

Acceptance: corporate users with HTTPS_PROXY env set see rate-limit segments populate via the proxy; misconfigured proxy yields a structured error, not silence.
close_reason: UreqTransport::new() now wires ureq::Proxy::try_from_env (ALL_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY + lowercase variants + NO_PROXY exclusion). Malformed env vars emit an lsm_warn! with variable name only (proxy URLs can carry user:pass@; echoing value would leak to stderr / CI logs). Filed lsm-7j6p for the warn-asserting test refactor (blocked on lsm-8mbh warn-sink injection).

title: Rate-limit reset segments: absolute-timestamp format with timezone + locale + 12/24h
description:
rate_limit_5h_reset and rate_limit_7d_reset only support DurationFormat (relative: '4h12m'). ccstatusline ships absolute-timestamp variants with IANA timezone + locale + 12/24h ('resets at 7:00 PM PT'). Real UX gap on a flagship segment — many users prefer 'when will it reset' over 'how long until reset'.

Scope:
- New ResetFormat enum: Duration | Absolute { timezone: Tz, locale: Locale, hour_format: Hour12 | Hour24 }
- chrono-tz dep for IANA timezone parsing (lookup current cost in size budget per linesmith-project-vision)
- Format string with strftime-like placeholders OR fixed format with config knobs
- TOML schema: format = 'absolute' { timezone = 'America/Los_Angeles', hour = 12 }
- Default tz = system local; default hour = 24
- Snapshot tests covering Duration + Absolute (multiple zones + 12/24h)

Acceptance: users can render 'resets at 7:00 PM' or 'resets at 19:00' or '4h12m' on the same segment; tz/locale errors fall back to UTC + 24h with structured warn.
close_reason: Added absolute-timestamp format to rate-limit reset segments (rate_limit_5h_reset, rate_limit_7d_reset). New TOML schema: format = 'absolute' + timezone (IANA name, default = system local) + hour_format ('12h' | '24h', default 24h) + locale ('en-US', v0.1 ships English-only, #[non_exhaustive] for v0.2 expansion). New types: ResetFormat (replaces DurationFormat), AbsoluteFormat, HourFormat, Locale, Timezone (encapsulates jiff::tz::TimeZone behind Iana payload variant). Renderer uses jiff strftime ('%H:%M %Z' / '%-I:%M %p %Z'). Picked jiff over chrono-tz to read system tzdb on Unix instead of embedding the IANA database — net binary impact +16KB vs predicted +250-400KB. 14 new tests covering absolute output (24h, 12h with PM, 12h morning zero-pad, explicit Asia/Tokyo zone, dispatch through format_reset, JSONL+absolute stale-marker, DST transition both sides, end-to-end TOML→render) + parser fallbacks (full knobs, defaults, bad tz, bad hour_format, unsupported locale, duration value backwards-compat) + 2 regression tests for invalid_progress_width-clobbers-absolute bug. Also fixed validate_keys allow-list (was missing the 3 new keys → spurious warnings). Spec doc docs/specs/rate-limit-segments.md updated with the new format value, knobs, and render examples. Filed lsm-3912 as follow-up to migrate the rest of the workspace from chrono → jiff. mise run check + 1541 tests + bench all green; binary 4.22MB.

title: OSC 8 hyperlink emission: Style.hyperlink plumbing + sgr_open emit + truncation-safe encoding
description:
Today the plugin output type accepts a 'hyperlink' field but theme/mod.rs explicitly documents it as 'silently ignored' and plugins/output.rs ignores it on emission. ccstatusline (parity target) emits OSC 8 hyperlinks across Branch, Root Dir, PR, remote-owner widgets, and a generic Link widget — and preserves them through ANSI-aware truncation.

Without engine-level OSC 8 support: themes can't link, the future Custom Link widget has no path, and built-in segments (e.g. branch → GitHub URL, workspace → IDE deep-link) can't ship hyperlink affordances.

Scope:
- Add 'hyperlink: Option<String>' to Style (or wherever the spec slot lives — verify spec drift first per lsm-7n2)
- Emit OSC 8 open/close in sgr_open / sgr_close (or new layer); supports-hyperlinks gating via Capability
- Layout/truncation: ensure ellipsis-truncation doesn't split an OSC 8 sequence. Track open hyperlinks across truncation boundary so closing OSC 8 always emits.
- Plugin output: stop dropping hyperlink in segments/output.rs; thread to host
- Test: snapshot tests covering hyperlink emit + truncation-mid-link safety
- Update theme/mod.rs and plugins/output.rs doc-comments

Acceptance: a built-in or plugin segment can render text with an attached URL; truncation never produces a half-emitted OSC 8 escape; supports-hyperlinks downgrades to plain text on incapable terminals.
close_reason: OSC 8 hyperlinks wired end-to-end. Style.hyperlink + with_hyperlink, runs_to_ansi gains hyperlinks bool, push_osc8_open strips control chars (ESC/BEL/NUL/DEL/C1 ST) before emit, RunContext detects via supports-hyperlinks, plugin output threads hyperlink (empty folds to None, non-string rejected), OverriddenSegment merges user-style overrides preserving inner hyperlink. 14 new tests. theming.md + plugin-api.md updated for the new contracts.

title: Segment: version — render Claude Code CLI version
description:
CC stdin payload includes a version field (visible in JSONL fixtures: '"version":"1.0.85"'). ccstatusline ships this widget; it's trivial wiring.

Scope:
- Verify version field source — top-level stdin vs JSONL-only (see jsonl.rs fixtures); plumb through StatusContext
- New segments/version.rs: optional 'v' prefix toggle, hide-when-empty
- TOML schema entry + default off (opt-in)
- Snapshot tests

Acceptance: CC CLI version renders when available; degrades silently when absent.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-04-28: Earlier 2026-04-28 notes were based on outdated docs/specs/input-schema.md:327 which incorrectly claimed CC stdin doesn't include 'version'. Verified against official Claude Code docs at code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline: 'version' IS a top-level stdin field (e.g. "version":"2.1.90"). ccstatusline's StatusJSONSchema confirms this. Original 'trivial wiring' design was correct — implemented as plain stdin pull through StatusContext.version: Option<String>. No shellout needed. Spec heuristic at input-schema.md:327 also corrected (Qwen-vs-CC distinguisher was the version field; that's no longer valid since CC 2.x added it).
close_reason: Implemented as stdin-derived segment (the original design). Added StatusContext.version: Option<String>, parser, segments/version.rs with prefix toggle (default 'v'), spec input-schema.md fixes for both the canonical model and the heuristic detection. 9 new tests.

description:

title: README v0.1 polish: layout_options + themes + version segment + OSC 8
description:
README polish for the v0.1 release. The crate has shipped to crates.io + homebrew at v0.1.1; this update reflects the user-visible surfaces that landed since the previous README iteration.

**Shipped scope:**
- New "What you'll see" section between "Design" and "Install" with two text rendering examples (space separator vs. powerline). Uses the actual Nerd Font U+E0B0 chevron in the powerline example with a parenthetical noting the tofu fallback for non-Nerd-Font readers.
- Color-policy paragraph documenting `NO_COLOR` / `TERM` / `COLORTERM` auto-detection and the `[layout_options].color = "always"` override (the common setting since Claude Code captures stdout).
- OSC 8 hyperlink paragraph honestly describing what's wired today: end-to-end plumbing (`Style.hyperlink`, terminal detection via `supports-hyperlinks`); plugins can populate URLs; built-in workspace/branch hyperlinks are tracked for v0.2.
- Configure section's TOML example extended with a `[layout_options]` block (`color`, `separator`, `powerline_width`) plus inline comments explaining each knob.
- Curated segment list: defaults (model, context_window, cost, effort, git_branch with dirty + ahead/behind, workspace) + commonly-used opt-ins (rate_limit_*, version, token counts, vim/agent/output_style mode indicators) + pointer to docs/specs/segment-system.md for the full inventory of 20 built-ins.
- Themes subsection: 11-row table of built-in themes (default, minimal, 4 catppuccin flavors, dracula, nord, gruvbox, tokyo-night, rose-pine) + pointer to docs/specs/theming.md for the role schema.
- Tightened the line-25 rhai claim from "on the roadmap" to "runtime scaffolding shipped; the script loader lands in v0.2" for accuracy.

**Out of scope (deliberate):**
- Screenshots: skipped per user direction. The text-rendering examples in "What you'll see" substitute for the visual.
- "How it works" diagram (input JSON → segments → render): pointer to `docs/specs/segment-system.md` carries the same information for readers who want depth.

**Existing surfaces that didn't need changes:**
- Install section (already complete with all four installer methods, target triples, Gatekeeper note, attestation verify recipe).
- Why section (resource/correctness/plugin-API/onboarding gaps still apply).
- How fast / Documentation / Development sections.

**Cross-references (separate beads, unaddressed here):**
- lsm-lirz: privacy/no-telemetry section.
- lsm-xs8y: MSRV badge.
- lsm-c6h0: full docs/USAGE.md user-facing config + segment reference.

Validated through `mise run check` (markdownlint + prettier + cargo:check + clippy + fmt:check) plus pr-review-toolkit (code-reviewer + comment-analyzer) and Codex review. All Critical findings (4) addressed: rate_limit fictional ID corrected to rate_limit_5h, git_branch moved from v0.2 line into shipped defaults, segment list expanded honestly, OSC 8 claim rewritten to match actual emit behavior. Important + suggestion-grade items (powerline glyph, stale rhai claim) fixed; defensible omissions (capsule/flex keyword listing, padding:0 rationale, catppuccin row layout) acknowledged in review and skipped.
close_reason: README v0.1 polish: 'What you'll see' section with space + powerline render examples, [layout_options] block in the Configure TOML (color/separator/powerline_width), 11-theme table, honest segment list (defaults + opt-ins + pointer to docs/specs/segment-system.md for the full 20). Fixed factual gaps surfaced by review: rate_limit→rate_limit_5h, git_branch moved from v0.2 line into shipped defaults, OSC 8 description rewritten to match actual emit behavior (plugins today; built-ins for v0.2), powerline glyph corrected to U+E0B0, line-25 rhai claim tightened from 'roadmap' to 'scaffolding shipped'. Screenshots intentionally skipped.

title: Curated theme presets: Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night, Rose Pine + minimal/default
description:
Project vision (linesmith-project-vision memory) promises 6 popular curated themes + minimal/default presets as a v1 differentiator (#3). Today only Catppuccin (4 flavors) ships at crates/linesmith/src/theme/catppuccin.rs. Without the full pack, the v0.1 theme-picker screen (lsm-herx.21) and theme docs land mostly empty.

Acceptance:
- One module per theme under crates/linesmith/src/theme/{dracula,nord,gruvbox,tokyo_night,rose_pine,minimal,default}.rs
- Each registered in BUILT_INS in theme/mod.rs
- Each maps the full Role enum used by Catppuccin
- builtin_names() returns all flavors
- Snapshot test per theme via insta covering rendered example line
- Docs: docs/specs/themes.md (or section in existing) with palette tables
close_reason: Shipped 5 curated theme presets (Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night Storm, Rose Pine main) plus extracted default+minimal into modules. Each theme: pub(super) const, theme_colors() const fn, 5-6 unit tests. Pattern parity with catppuccin.rs; deferred insta in favor of the existing unit-test culture (rated equivalent regression coverage by test-analyzer). License attribution in module docs + new theming.md attributions section. 28 new tests including completeness pin. Verified all upstream licenses (4 MIT, 1 MIT/X11, 1 Apache 2.0).

title: TOML write-back via toml_edit + Ctrl+S save + dirty-check
description:
Persistence layer. toml_edit::DocumentMut held in the model; mutations applied on save. Atomic write (temp + rename) preserves comments/formatting on round-trip.

Ctrl+S writes immediately from any screen — no save dialog. Dirty-check via stringify diff against original. Confirm-on-quit when dirty.

MVP-critical.
close_reason: TOML write-back: LoadOutcome + Model::save via tempfile::persist atomic rename + Ctrl+S handler + AppScreen::ConfirmQuit modal gating dirty-quit. Save creates missing files, refuses on parse-error (no clobber), survives toml/toml_edit parser skew via save-disabled fallback, resolves to absolute path to dodge cwd-race, logs orphan temp on persist failure. 4 v0.2 follow-ups filed (lsm-iafp LoadOutcome enum, lsm-n1bw atomic_write hardening, lsm-mny2 transient save-status footer, lsm-1lfa boot-helper extraction).

title: Live-preview-as-header layout
description:
Preview pane anchored to top of every screen. Persistent across navigation. Renders the in-memory Config through layout::render_to_runs and maps StyledRun → ratatui Span. Updates on every state change. The accuracy guarantee comes free since preview = production rendering.

Holds last-valid output during transient invalid states (e.g., template editor mid-typing).

MVP-critical.
close_reason: Live-preview-as-header per ADR-0016: bordered preview block at top of every frame renders the user's config through the production layout engine and maps StyledRun → ratatui Span with theme-resolved color and decoration. Honors config.theme via XDG-resolved ThemeRegistry, color via [layout_options].color + Capability::detect (with NO_COLOR + terminal probing). Diagnostic stream from build_lines/render_to_runs surfaces below the preview body in dim italic. Preseeds DataContext.usage with NoCredentials so rate_limit_* segments hide without firing the live OAuth/Keychain/JSONL cascade. cwd set to current_dir so git_branch and workspace render against the editor's repo. 446 linesmith tests, 13 in preview module covering color/decoration mapping, capability downgrade, fg-vs-role precedence, AnsiColor brightness swap, plugin-warning surfacing, parse-fallback. 5 follow-ups filed: lsm-anib (P3 many-line affordance + plugin chip), lsm-pjht (P2 hold-last-valid for invalid edits), lsm-wyph (P1 lsm_warn!/lsm_error! sink threading for alt-screen safety), lsm-xd8n (P2 layout-decision events to caller), lsm-jygz (P2 thread CliEnv through tui::run for full color-policy parity).

title: Items editor screen (segment list, move-mode reorder, type picker, separator-as-item)
description:
Segment editor (image 2/3 in ccstatusline). Lists segments + separators as alternating positional items. Verb-letter keybindings: (a)dd via picker, (i)nsert via picker, (k)lone, (d)elete, (c)lear line, (r)aw value, (m)erge, Space edit separator, Enter move-mode toggle.

Type picker: horizontal scrollable widget invoked via ←→ from the cursor position. Reusable for add/insert/swap.

MVP-critical.
notes: Phase 3 in progress: simple verbs d/c/k (delete/clear/clone). No new widget needed; reuses existing array-mutation pattern + refresh_config.
close_reason: Items editor MVP closed. ADR-0024 ships per-boundary separator TOML (mixed string-or-inline-table segments array), LinePicker for multi-line configs, Space (insert separator) + m (toggle merge) verbs, r dispatching by entry kind for separator-character edits and segment-rename with inline-table field preservation. ItemsEditorPrev enum threads Esc back-nav to the right caller; zero-padded [line.01] keys resolve by parsed u32; doctor walks inline-table entries via shared classifier. 1791 tests, mise check clean. 11 follow-ups filed across 6 review iterations.

title: Main menu screen
description:
Top-level navigation screen (image 1 in ccstatusline). 7 menu items: Edit Lines, Edit Colors, Powerline Setup, Terminal Options, Global Overrides, Install to Claude Code, Exit. Uses ListScreen widget. Each entry routes to its dedicated screen; deferred screens (Powerline, Per-line) show a placeholder until their backing features ship.

MVP-critical.
close_reason: Main Menu screen with 7 rows (Edit Lines, Edit Colors, Powerline Setup, Terminal Options, Global Overrides, Install to Claude Code, Exit) driving the ListScreen widget. Adds ScreenOutcome enum + AppScreen::Placeholder variant + screen-specific Esc semantics (sub-screens back-nav, top quits) per ADR-0016. mem::take preserves cursor through Activate→Esc→Activate round-trip. 13 tests in main_menu, 3 in placeholder, 8 in app — full dispatch chain pinned. 1 follow-up filed: lsm-o83n (P3) for screen-stack architecture before depth-2+ navigation lands.

title: PropertyScreen reusable widget (labeled rows + per-row letter keys)
description:
Foundation for v0.2 screens that aren't list-shaped: Global Overrides, Powerline Setup, Terminal Options, Install to Claude Code, Color Level.

Behavior:
- Labeled rows; each row addressed by a per-row letter key (no list cursor).
- Row variants: Toggle (e.g., 'Global Bold: ✓ Enabled — Press (o) to toggle'), ValueCycle (e.g., 'Override FG Color: (none) - (f) cycle, (g) clear'), EditField (e.g., 'Default Padding: (none) - Press (p) to edit'), Drilldown (e.g., 'Terminal Width [drilldown]').
- Multi-paragraph 'Note:' footer with bullet definitions when configured.
- Status header for setup screens (e.g., Powerline shows 'Font Status: ✓ Installed').

Not on MVP — flat-properties screens land in v0.2.

title: ListScreen reusable widget (cursor + verb-letter actions)
description:
Foundation: extract the ccstatusline-style list-screen pattern into a reusable widget. Used by Main Menu, Items Editor, Color Editor, Theme Picker, Line Picker.

Behavior:
- ▶ cursor on the highlighted row.
- ↑↓ navigate; wraps at top/bottom (matches ccstatusline).
- Verb-letter dispatch: caller registers letter→action handlers; ListScreen routes keys.
- Bottom-of-screen description string pulled from the highlighted item.
- One-line help string from the caller.
- Move-mode toggle (only modal verb): Enter enters move-mode, ↑↓ swaps adjacent, Esc/Enter exits.

MVP-critical.
close_reason: Reusable ListScreen widget: pure handle_key + ratatui render, cursor with normal-mode wrap and move-mode swap, lowercase ASCII verb-letter dispatch, defensive cursor + move_mode clamps. 35 tests. 3 follow-ups filed: lsm-gniq (Windows KeyEventKind::Press filter), lsm-9x14 (MoveSwap + move-mode redispatch contract design, blocks lsm-herx.7), lsm-ls1q (render defense tests for long labels / unicode / multi-verb separator).

title: linesmith config subcommand + ratatui boot
description:
Foundation: add the linesmith config CLI subcommand that boots the ratatui TUI. Wires:
- New CLI subcommand (alongside existing render path).
- ratatui terminal setup (raw mode, alternate screen, cursor hide).
- Cleanup on exit (panic hook to restore terminal state).
- Main event loop (poll crossterm events, dispatch to screen state machine).
- Initial screen state = Main Menu.
- Loads the user's existing config file or creates a fresh in-memory Config if none exists.

MVP-critical. Pre-req for every TUI screen.

ADR: ratatui-for-tui-runtime (lsm-1qg8 — file ID will be assigned at filing time).
close_reason: linesmith config subcommand + ratatui boot scaffolding shipped per ADR-0015/16. Feature-gated behind config-ui (default-on); --no-default-features cleanly drops ratatui. tui module: terminal lifecycle (cleanup-complete on partial-state failure, both enter and leave), pre-enter panic hook, event loop with redraw-only-on-event + resize routing, AppScreen state machine, pure (Model, Event) -> Model update. Placeholder Main Menu confirms boot + config load. load_config uses from_str_validated so unknown-key warnings surface on stderr before alt-screen takeover. 17 tests added covering parse + load_config + screen routing + quit predicate. 2 follow-up beads filed (lsm-bwt0 EINTR retry, lsm-hr8r boot-stderr invariant test).

title: Separator-as-item refactor: Separator becomes a positional list element
description:
Architectural shift required by the TUI's Items editor (per ccstatusline's design): separators between segments become positional items in the same list, not a per-segment trailing config field. Today linesmith's Separator lives on SegmentDefaults.default_separator (segment owns its right-edge separator); the TUI shows separators as alternating items between segments and lets users edit each one individually.

Refactor scope:
- Move Separator out of SegmentDefaults into a sibling enum entry alongside segments.
- Layout: line.segments becomes Vec<LineItem> where LineItem = Segment(...) | Separator(SeparatorKind).
- Renderer walks the alternating list emitting segment + separator + segment + separator.
- Migration: existing configs that set per-segment separators auto-promote to inline Separator items at config-load time.

MVP-critical: the Items editor can't function without this. Without it, the editor would show one row per segment with no way to address separators between them.

Note: this is breaking against current spec language. May need a v0.7 spec bump to segment-system.md.
notes: Linked to lsm-1my (powerline separator MVP, shipped 2026-04-28). lsm-1my added [layout_options].separator with global modes 'space' / 'powerline' / arbitrary literals ('|', ' · ', etc.) plus powerline_width. That covers homogeneous-separator configs. The MIXED case (e.g., model | branch  cost) requires this separator-as-item refactor — only positional Separator items can carry per-boundary settings. Verified ccstatusline pattern via gh api on sirmalloc/ccstatusline: their segment list contains explicit { type: 'separator' } items, plus a separate PowerlineConfig object with separators[], separatorInvertBackground[], startCaps[], endCaps[], autoAlign. When implementing, migrate the global [layout_options].separator policy from lsm-1my (apply_layout_separator in segments/builder.rs) to inline Separator items, preserving back-compat for existing configs that use the global key.
close_reason: Separator-as-item refactor: LineItem enum (Segment | Separator) replaces SegmentDefaults::default_separator. Builder interleaves [layout_options].separator between adjacent segments; renderer walks the LineItem list directly with adjacency invariants in collect (separator survives only between two surviving segments) and drop (right-edge first, left-edge fallback). Plugin per-render override (RenderedSegment::with_separator) preserved and now beats inline at that one boundary, including post shrink_to_fit / reflow. Spec bumped v0.6 → v0.7, struck the 'separator ownership' open question. 1539 tests pass. 3 follow-up beads filed: lsm-q2t3 (Clone story; blocks lsm-herx.7), lsm-jaaq (perf short-circuit), lsm-ngwq (OverriddenSegment SemVer).

title: Layout engine: Vec<StyledRun> emit mode for TUI preview
description:
Foundation for the TUI's preview-as-header pane. Today the layout engine emits ANSI-encoded strings via render_with_warn. Add an alternative emit path that returns Vec<StyledRun> (segment text + Style for each run) so the TUI consumes the rich form directly without ansi-to-tui round-tripping.

Design notes:
- Internal: split render_with_warn into a render_to_runs core that returns the Vec<StyledRun> + a thin ANSI-formatting wrapper for stdout output.
- Existing render() / render_with_warn() callers keep the ANSI string output unchanged (back-compat).
- TUI calls render_to_runs and maps each StyledRun to a ratatui Span.

MVP-critical for the TUI epic. Foundation work; no user-visible change in isolation, but unblocks the live preview pane.

See lsm-herx for the broader epic.
close_reason: Layout engine: render_to_runs core returns Vec<StyledRun>; render_with_warn becomes thin runs_to_ansi wrapper. StyledRun added with #[non_exhaustive] + pub(crate) fields + new()/text()/style() accessors. 11 new tests including round-trip pin across capabilities and width pressure.

title: ADR: tui-screen-state-machine
description:
Decision: structure the TUI as a screen-state enum (ccstatusline-style — see their AppScreen union with 11 variants) with two reusable screen-template widgets:

- **ListScreen**: cursor (▶) + verb-letter actions (a/i/k/d/c/r/m). Used by Main Menu, Items Editor, Color Editor, Theme Picker, Line Picker.
- **PropertyScreen**: labeled rows, each addressed by a letter key, no list cursor. Used by Global Overrides, Powerline Setup, Terminal Options, Install to Claude Code.

Plus contracts:
- Preview as persistent header (re-renders on every state change).
- Ctrl+S saves immediately; no save dialog.
- Dirty-check via stringify diff; confirm-on-quit when dirty.
- Bottom-of-screen description for highlighted item.
- One-line help row under screen title.

Companion ADR: ratatui-for-tui-runtime.

Promote to docs/adrs/ when this lands.

title: ADR: ratatui-for-tui-runtime
description:
Decision: use ratatui v0.30 for the linesmith config TUI runtime, paired with tui-textarea for inputs. Capture the analysis behind:
- Pre-1.0 stability posture (pin minor, bump deliberately)
- Binary-size budget (~500KB-2MB stripped over a crossterm-only build; well under our cold-start performance ceiling)
- Elm Architecture (Model/Update/View) as the recommended state pattern
- Reference codebases: gitui (closest analogue), atuin, helix
- Span-emit decision: layout engine emits Vec<StyledRun> alongside ANSI so TUI preview consumes the rich form directly (avoids round-tripping ANSI via ansi-to-tui)
- Alternatives rejected: cursive (ncurses linkage / portability), crossterm-only (rebuilds layout/widgets), tui-rs (deprecated)

Companion ADR: tui-screen-state-machine.

Follow research already in this conversation thread; promote to docs/adrs/.
close_reason: ADR-0015 landed: ratatui v0.30 + tui-textarea, feature-gated behind config-ui (default-on); minor-version pinning pre-1.0; Vec<StyledRun> → ratatui Span mapping avoids ansi-to-tui.

title: Epic: linesmith config TUI (ccstatusline-parity)
description:
Goal: ship an interactive TUI for configuring linesmith, modeled on ccstatusline's UX (live preview as header, segment list with move-mode reorder, verb-letter keybindings, Ctrl+S save).

**v0.1 MVP critical path (7 beads, all shipped):**
1. Layout engine `Vec<StyledRun>` emit mode (clean preview without ANSI parsing) — lsm-herx.1
2. Separator-as-item architectural refactor (separators become positional list items) — lsm-herx.2
3. `linesmith config` subcommand + ratatui boot — lsm-herx.3
4. `ListScreen` reusable widget (cursor + verb-letter pattern) — lsm-herx.4
5. Main menu screen — lsm-herx.6
6. Items editor (segment list, move-mode reorder, type picker, separator-as-item, LinePicker) — lsm-herx.7 (rolled in lsm-herx.31)
7. `toml_edit` write-back + Ctrl+S save + dirty-check — lsm-herx.9

Plus live-preview-as-header (lsm-herx.8).

**v0.1 finalization (5 beads remaining):**
- Theme picker screen — lsm-herx.21
- User-theme discovery wiring — lsm-herx.22
- Install to Claude Code (folds lsm-5yd) — lsm-herx.28
- EnvironmentWarning widget — lsm-herx.34
- Snapshot tests via TestBackend + insta — lsm-herx.36

**v0.2+ parity work moved to lsm-hxtr** (PropertyScreen + per-segment editing, color editor, terminal/engine knobs, powerline setup, per-line config, free-text format editor, self-demo controls).

**Reference architecture from ccstatusline:**
- Preview anchored to top of every screen, re-renders on state change
- Two screen templates: ListScreen (cursor + verb-letter actions) and PropertyScreen (labeled rows + per-row letter keys — v0.2)
- Verb-letter keybindings: (a)dd, (i)nsert, (k)lone, (d)elete, (c)lear, (r)aw, (m)erge

title: Layout-pressure-aware segment compaction (shrink_to_fit trait extension)
description:
Codex review on lsm-z0ai surfaced a real UX gap: per-marker `hide_below_cells` thresholds key off `rc.terminal_width`, so they only fire when the terminal is narrow. The more common pressure case — wide terminal with a dense layout where neighboring segments consume the line — still drops affected segments whole via priority because the threshold never trips.

For `git_branch` specifically: a 200-cell terminal with 8 configured segments can still force the segment to overflow; `hide_below_cells` doesn't fire (terminal width >= threshold), so the segment drops whole and the user loses the branch name (the most signal-bearing piece).

Goal: extend the layout engine so segments can shed structured-tail content (`*`, `↑2 ↓1`) when they're about to be dropped due to **layout pressure**, not just terminal narrowness.

Three design options to evaluate:

1. **`shrink_to_fit(&self, target: u16) -> Option<RenderedSegment>` trait method.** When the engine's reflow loop is about to drop a non-truncatable segment, call `shrink_to_fit(remaining_budget)` first; if it returns Some, use the shrunk form. Cleanest API; third Segment-trait extension after `truncatable` (lsm-66k) and `RenderContext` (lsm-xdyp). Default impl returns None (current behavior preserved).

2. **Per-segment budget plumbing.** Engine pre-computes available cells per segment before calling `render`. Has chicken-and-egg ordering: budget depends on what other segments render, render decisions depend on budget.

3. **Two-pass rendering.** Render full once, measure overflow, re-render compact for segments that overflow. Doubles render cost; complicates the existing reflow loop.

Recommended starting point: option 1 (`shrink_to_fit`) — composes naturally with the existing reflow loop; segments opt in by overriding the default; `hide_below_cells` becomes a complementary user-preference knob.

For `git_branch` specifically, `shrink_to_fit` would re-emit `assemble` with dirty + ahead_behind suppressed — the same fallback shape lsm-z0ai already supports for narrow terminals, just triggered by layout pressure instead of terminal width.

Composes with the Starship-parity epic lsm-1o70: when the format template lands, `shrink_to_fit` becomes "render the same template with degraded variables."

Follow-up to lsm-z0ai.
notes: Post-review additions before commit: (1) `try_shrink` enforces a `[width.min, target]` range invariant on the shrunk render, matching `apply_width_bounds` and `try_reflow` parity (Codex review). (2) Contract violations (segment returns `width > target`) now surface through `lsm_warn!` so plugin authors see the misbehavior during development; engine still rejects and falls through to drop (pr-review). (3) Two extra OverriddenSegment tests pin the `user_style = None` shrink-passthrough path. Final test count: 1033 unit + 16 integration + 10 plugin = 1059 green. Spec § Layout algorithm step c, trait doc, and git_branch entry all reflect the [width.min, target] range contract.
close_reason: Layout-pressure-aware compaction shipped via `Segment::shrink_to_fit(&self, ctx, rc, target) -> Option<RenderedSegment>` (default `None`). The engine reflow loop now tries `shrink_to_fit` before falling back to `truncatable` end-ellipsis or drop, letting structured-tail segments shed decoration while keeping the signal-bearing prefix under any pressure — terminal narrowness or dense-layout overflow. `Item<'a>` carries a `&'a dyn Segment` back-ref so the engine can call back into the segment from the loop. `git_branch::shrink_to_fit` returns `assemble_compact` (icon + label + head, both markers suppressed). `OverriddenSegment::shrink_to_fit` forwards to inner with style merge. Spec segment-system.md v0.6 + git-segments.md (two-layer compaction story) + plugin-api.md (plugin support deferred). 8 new tests + 2 OverriddenSegment passthrough tests; 1027 unit + 16 integration + 10 plugin = 1053 total green. Plugin (rhai) shrink_to_fit support tracked separately as lsm-ns0l.

title: Pass RenderContext (terminal_width, …) into Segment::render
description:
Foundation for width-aware / dynamic segments.

Segment::render currently takes only `&DataContext`, which means a segment can't see the terminal budget when deciding how to render itself. The layout engine's reflow pass (lsm-66k) handles prose-like segments by trimming graphemes from the right, but composite segments (context_bar's `▰▰▰▰▱▱ 45%`, model's `Opus 4.7 (1M context)`) need to swap shape — drop the bar before the percent, drop the parenthetical before the name — which is segment-internal logic the engine can't do.

Proposed:
- Add `pub struct RenderContext { pub terminal_width: u16, … }` (room for line index, capability, neighbor info later).
- Change `Segment::render(&self, ctx: &DataContext) -> RenderResult` to `render(&self, data: &DataContext, render: &RenderContext)`. Keep `DataContext` separate — `RenderContext` is per-render layout state, `DataContext` is fetched data.
- Layout engine passes `RenderContext { terminal_width }` through `render_with_warn` → `collect_items_with` → segment.
- Update built-in and plugin segments. Plugin (rhai) bridge surfaces `render.terminal_width` to scripts per docs/specs/plugin-api.md.

Spec: docs/specs/segment-system.md §Segment trait + §Rendering pipeline.

Follow-up to lsm-66k. Unblocks segment-internal width-aware fallbacks (lsm-… context_bar, lsm-… model — children of this bead).
close_reason: Threaded `RenderContext` (currently `pub terminal_width: u16`, `#[non_exhaustive]`) into `Segment::render` as a second arg. Layout engine builds it once per render and passes through `collect_items_with`. Rhai plugin bridge surfaces `ctx.render.terminal_width` via `build_ctx` + a `build_render` helper. Spec segment-system.md v0.5 + plugin-api.md updated. 18 `Segment` impls updated; 991 unit tests + 14 integration + 10 plugin tests pass. Unblocks lsm-1no9 (context_bar fallback), lsm-rkxh (model compaction), lsm-z0ai (git_branch segment-aware fallback).

title: CI: cross-platform OS matrix on tests job
description:
linesmith ships 5 triples (mac x2, linux x2, win x1) but ci.yml only tests on ubuntu-latest. gix, terminal_size, supports-color, ANSI handling, and path separators all have OS-specific code paths — windows console / macOS Terminal.app bugs only surface on those runners.

Add a tests-os job (or matrix the existing tests job) with strategy.matrix.os: [macos-latest, windows-latest], fail-fast: false. Keep ubuntu as the primary fast-feedback gate; mark all three required for branch protection.

Cost: +6-10 min CI per PR (mac is 10x billable, win is 2x). Negligible for an oakoss public repo (free tier).

Surfaced during lsm-pud research on 2026-04-25.
close_reason: Tests job now matrixed across [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest] with fail-fast: false. Per-cell status surfaces in Actions UI; ci-summary table updated with '(per-cell status in Actions UI)' note since needs.X.result only exposes the rollup. lsm-j2o notes updated to recommend gating branch protection on the 'CI Summary' check name (single stable choke point that doesn't drift as future jobs are added).

title: Epic: implement ADR-0014 best-effort parse with segment-level isolation
description:
Implementation work for ADR-0014 (commit 4a7ea9d, status: proposed). Refactors linesmiths atomic parse into best-effort + per-segment Option-shaped contract per the ccstatusline pattern surveyed in parse-failure-isolation-survey (commit e39184a).

Architectural change in one paragraph: input::parse stays Result<StatusContext, ParseError> for catastrophic JSON-root failures only. Every nested field-level failure (missing field, null sub-field, type mismatch inside sub-objects) becomes Ok(None) for the affected field plus an lsm_warn! with full JSON path. StatusContext widens model and workspace from required to Option (matching the spec field set including session/vim/output_style/agent_name); ContextWindow leaves all become Option. Segments check None and elide.

**Sub-deliverables:**

1. input.rs: widen StatusContext.model and StatusContext.workspace to Option; widen ContextWindow leaves to Option (used, size, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens). Narrow ContextWindow.size from u64 back to u32 to resolve pre-existing source/spec drift the ADR Shape section calls out.
2. input.rs: rewrite parse_context_window / parse_cost / parse_effort / parse_model / parse_workspace to be best-effort — sub-field TypeMismatch / null becomes lsm_warn + Ok(None) for the whole sub-tree; only structural failures (e.g. cost field is a string not an object) remain Result::Err.
3. input.rs: update parse() entry point so only InvalidJson and root-level TypeMismatch remain in practice; ParseError variants stay declared (#[non_exhaustive], removing them is a breaking change).
4. ctx_mirror.rs: update plugin exposure for newly-Option fields (model, workspace) so plugins see () or a map matching the ADR contract.
5. Every segment that reads ctx.status.model / ctx.status.workspace: add None-handling (most should hide; check git_branch + workspace specifically).
6. Tests: regression test using the lsm-6z9e captured pre-first-API-call payload — model/git_branch/workspace render with context_window hidden. Synthetic test for malformed cost field — cost segment hides, others render, lsm_warn fires once with cost.total_cost_usd path. Empty-payload test: parse(b"{}").is_ok() with all top-level fields None.
7. docs/specs/input-schema.md: update §Edge cases to reflect the new contract (per-field nulls degrade to None + warn, not TypeMismatch).
8. docs/research/parse-failure-isolation-survey.md: when this epic ships, update the "synthesis recommends Option 1" section to past-tense "ADR-0014 chose Option 1; implemented in lsm-XXXX" referencing this beads ID.

**Coordination with lsm-6z9e:** lsm-6z9e ships the targeted null-handling quick fix in v0.1.2 (parse_context_window catches null sub-fields, returns Ok(None) for the whole field). This epic supersedes that quick fix architecturally — the same regression fixture serves as both the lsm-6z9e acceptance test and a confirmation criterion for this epic.

**Out of scope:** starship-style parallel rendering (per ADR-0012 each render is a fresh single-shot process; parallelism is N/A), ctx_mirror schema versioning for plugin breaking change (deferred until external plugin authors emerge per ADR-0014 Consequences).

**Acceptance:** all four ADR-0014 confirmation criteria pass (lsm-6z9e regression test, malformed cost test, parse(b"{}").is_ok(), full cargo test green with new partial-data tests added).
notes: Pass-2 review (Codex P2, 2026-04-28) of the lsm-yagj/edji/iy9z bundle landed unknown-enum-degrades-segment behavior for parse_vim early (input.rs:702-718): unknown vim.mode → lsm_warn + Ok(None), not ParseError. When this epic widens the parser, EXTEND the same rule to parse_effort (input.rs:644-648 still raises InvalidValue on unknown effort levels — symmetric fix is in scope). The asymmetry between the two parsers is a known wart documented in the comment at parse_vim's match arm; closing it is part of this epic's remit.
close_reason: ADR-0014 best-effort parse with segment-level isolation: implementation complete. All 10 sub-deliverables shipped across two commits — first delivered model/workspace/context_window per-leaf isolation + partial render; this commit extends to cost/effort/vim/output_style/version/agent. Only ParseError sites remaining are documented carve-outs: root-non-object (catastrophic) and used_percentage <0/NaN (undocumented CC state, surface loud).

title: Wire release-plz to cliff.toml so CHANGELOG.md filtering takes effect
description:
release-plz currently uses its built-in default cliff template (3-category Added/Fixed/Other split) instead of the project cliff.toml. The cliff.toml has correct commit_parsers (feat/fix/perf/refactor visible, docs/chore/test/ci skipped), but release-plz never consults it.

Diagnosis surfaced via PR #2 v0.1.1 changelog: 8 items in Other section that cliff.toml would skip (refactor/test/spec items) or relocate (refactor goes to its own Refactoring group). Spec docs/specs/release-process.md:141 already documents cliff.toml as the source of truth, so the current behavior contradicts the spec.

Fix: add changelog_config = "cliff.toml" to [workspace] in release-plz.toml. Single line, regenerates PR on next release-plz workflow run.

Acceptance: PR #2 CHANGELOG.md diff uses bold-scope format with SHA hyperlinks, refactor commits move to a Refactoring header, chore/test/docs commits drop entirely.
close_reason: Added changelog_config = 'cliff.toml' to release-plz.toml [workspace]. Project's cliff.toml commit_parsers (skip docs/chore/test/ci, group feat/fix/perf/refactor) now apply to release-plz's PR-generated CHANGELOG.md. The next release-plz workflow run will refresh PR #2 with the cleaned-up format.

title: Catppuccin Role::Muted remapped from overlay0 to subtext0 (live-capture readability fix)
description:
Surfaced via lsm-mdd7 live-capture session on 2026-04-24. `Role::Muted` previously mapped to `overlay0` (Catppuccin UI-chrome grey meant for borders/dividers). Cost and effort segments render with `Muted`, so on Catppuccin dark flavors (Mocha at `#6c7086`) they sat too dim to read on dark terminal backgrounds.

**Fix:** remapped `Role::Muted` to `subtext0` in `crates/linesmith/src/theme/catppuccin.rs` for all four flavors. Mocha now renders Muted at `#a6adc8` — `subtext0`, Catppuccin's canonical "secondary text that still reads clearly."

**Rationale:** `overlay0` is the correct role for `Border`, not for text. Catppuccin semantics: `text` > `subtext1` > `subtext0` for text; `overlay2/1/0` and `surface2/1/0` for UI chrome. Our `Border` role already maps to `surface2`, so users who wanted the chrome-grey have it via that role.

**Test coverage:** existing palette-drift tests pass; no new test needed for a color mapping (the `every_flavor_maps_every_base_role` test guards against unmapping).

**Acceptance:** live statusline under Claude Code shows `$21.12` and `xhigh` in a clearly readable grey (`#a6adc8`) instead of the near-invisible `#6c7086`.

This issue exists mainly to give the commit for the remap a bead to close per AGENTS.md's "close before staging" convention.
close_reason: Role::Muted remapped from Catppuccin overlay0 to subtext0 across all four flavors. overlay0 is the UI-overlay/border grey (Mocha #6c7086); subtext0 is the canonical secondary-text role (Mocha #a6adc8), readable against dark backgrounds. Cost and effort segments (both Role::Muted) now render clearly without changing any segment code.

title: Extend ContextWindow to parse current_usage from stdin (prereq for tokens segments)
description:
Prerequisite for lsm-ua8 (tokens segments) and lsm-inpf/lsm-r1w follow-ups that need per-turn token counts.

Currently `crates/linesmith/src/input.rs` captures only `used`, `size`, `total_input_tokens`, `total_output_tokens` on `ContextWindow`. Claude Code's stdin also carries:

```json
"context_window": {
    ...
    "current_usage": {
      "input_tokens": 2000,
      "output_tokens": 500,
      "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
      "cache_read_input_tokens": 500
    }
}
```

This is `null` before the first API call in a session and present afterward.

**Scope:**
- Add `pub struct CurrentUsage` with the four `u64` fields.
- Extend `ContextWindow` with `pub current_usage: Option<CurrentUsage>`.
- Update `parse_context_window` to parse the object when present, map `null` to `None`, and return a `TypeMismatch` when the value is a non-object / non-null.
- Mirror `current_usage` to plugins via `ctx_mirror.rs` as `ctx.status.context_window.current_usage` — either a map with the four keys or rhai `()` when None.
- Update `docs/specs/plugin-api.md` §ctx.status.context_window shape to document the field.
- Tests: present-case parse, null-case parse, missing-case parse (current_usage key absent — treat same as null), type-mismatch error, plugin mirror for both None and Some.

**Acceptance:** parsing + mirror + spec match the stdin contract documented at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline. `cargo test -p linesmith` green after extending the input fixture suites.

**Blocks:** lsm-ua8 (tokens segments depend on this struct shape). Also unblocks future `context_usable` segment work per lsm-4wb research.
close_reason: TurnUsage struct added (#[non_exhaustive], Debug+Clone+Copy+Eq). ContextWindow gains Option<TurnUsage> current_usage; parse_current_usage handles absent/null → None and surfaces full nested paths on TypeMismatch/MissingField. ctx_mirror.rs emits ctx.status.context_window.current_usage as map-or-unit via build_turn_usage (destructured to fail compile on new fields). docs/specs/plugin-api.md updated to document the 4 leaf fields — previous one-line reference was aspirational; spec drift closed. 6 unit tests + 1 plugin-mirror test (absent, null, happy-path, non-object TypeMismatch, nested-path TypeMismatch provenance, missing-inner MissingField). Unblocks lsm-ua8 tokens segments.

title: Live-capture context_window stdin across 5 edge cases + fill research test matrix
description:
Follow-up from lsm-4wb. The research note at `docs/research/context-window-correctness.md` has a Test matrix section with pass/fail rows for 5 scenarios (200k baseline, post-`/compact`, post-`/resume`, 429, 1M-context). Those rows need live-capture data from real Claude Code sessions before the research is complete.

**Scope:**
1. Write a small shell wrapper that `tee`s linesmith's stdin to a timestamped JSONL file while passing through to linesmith unchanged.
2. Point Claude Code's `statusLine.command` at the wrapper.
3. Hit each of the 5 scenarios during normal Claude Code usage (no dedicated session required; opportunistic is fine).
4. At each state, capture `/context` output inside Claude Code to establish ground truth.
5. Fill in the research note's test matrix with pass/fail + delta between stdin `used_percentage` and `/context` reality.
6. File per-failure follow-up beads for any row where Claude Code's stdin diverges from visible reality.

**Acceptance:** Test matrix (~line 54 of the research note) has Pass/Fail + specific values for all 5 rows. Observed-failures section populated (or confirmed empty). Any failures filed as individual beads linked back to this one.

**Context:** Previous hypothesis (that used_percentage was broken in all 5 scenarios) weakened significantly after ccstatusline-source research showed they trust used_percentage verbatim with no compensation. Live tests will confirm or reject this newer baseline.
close_reason: Test matrix complete: rows 1/2/5 Pass (delta=0 on Sonnet 4.6 200k, post-compact, Opus 4.7 1M), row 3 Pass (session_id unchanged across /resume; pct=24 matched /context exactly), row 4 N/A (statusline not invoked during 429 retry). No failures; no follow-up beads needed.

title: Widen Percent::from_f64 to clamp used_percentage instead of rejecting >100
description:
Per lsm-4wb research: `Percent::from_f64` at `crates/linesmith/src/input.rs:~555` rejects any value outside `0.0..=100.0` as `ParseError::InvalidValue`. For `context_window.used_percentage` specifically, this collapses the whole stdin parse and degrades the statusline to `?` (driver.rs:719-730).

Claude Code has been observed emitting values >100 post-`/compact` (Anthropic #37163). When that happens linesmith goes marker-state instead of showing a percentage. ccstatusline handles the same case via `clampPercentage(0, 100)` — a bounded display of 100% is better UX than a bare `?` marker.

**Fix sketch:**
- Either widen the `Percent::from_f64` range (accept 0..=200 and let callers clamp) or — cleaner — add a `Percent::from_f64_clamped` constructor and use it in `parse_context_window`. Emit an `lsm_warn!` on clamp so the signal is still visible to users debugging weird percentages.
- Preserve the strict constructor for other callers (`UsageBucket.utilization`, `ContextWindow.used` in rate-limit buckets where 0..=100 is a real contract).
- Test: seed a stdin payload with `used_percentage: 101.3`, assert the segment renders 100% with a warn, not `?`.

**v0.1 significance:** fixes a severe-but-narrow failure mode observed upstream. The defensive parse is cheap and independent of the live-test investigation tracked separately.
close_reason: Percent::from_f64_clamped added; parse_context_window asymmetric: clamp above 100 (known upstream drift per claude-code#37163) with lsm_warn, reject below 0 (undocumented state, preserves corrupted-payload signal). 5 tests (1 unit + 4 integration) cover happy path, fractional overshoot, NaN, and negative-reject. Codex called out the symmetry regression during review; asymmetric design lands the fix without silently masking corrupted inputs. Follow-ups filed: lsm-g3im (tolerance filter on the warn, needs live-test data to calibrate), lsm-inpf ((Percent, Clamp) enum return for compile-time clamp awareness).

title: plugins: cap unknown_buckets size and JSON depth in ctx_mirror
description:
ctx_mirror::build_unknown_buckets iterates a server-controlled HashMap with no size cap. rhai's MAX_MAP_SIZE (256) only gates script-side growth; it does not reject a host-constructed Map with >256 entries. A malicious or buggy /api/oauth/usage response with thousands of keys flows straight through.

Related: json_to_dynamic recurses into arbitrary-depth nested JSON with no depth guard. rhai's MAX_EXPR_DEPTH gates script parsing, not host-side recursion — a nested-object bomb could blow the stack.

Fix: enforce MAX_MAP_SIZE + a key-length cap at the mirror boundary with a lsm_warn! on overshoot. Add a depth limit to json_to_dynamic (recursion counter param or iteration limit).

Found in lsm-xhu silent-failure review #5.
notes: Shipped: CapPosture {Strict, EscapeHatch} split — ctx.status.raw preserves escape-hatch round-trip (depth cap only for stack safety); server-controlled payloads (unknown_buckets values) get full caps (depth, map/array breadth, string size, key size). ConversionLimits aggregates per-category counts into one lsm_warn per top-level call. Deterministic sort on unknown_buckets truncation. docs/specs/plugin-api.md updated. 17 boundary/behavior tests covering exact boundaries, UTF-8 char-boundary truncation, per-entry depth reset, and posture asymmetry. Follow-ups: lsm-p5sx (ctx.meta.truncated sentinel, ADR-sized), lsm-860n (logger test sink).
close_reason: ctx_mirror: cap unknown_buckets at MAX_MAP_SIZE, drop oversize keys (>MAX_STRING_SIZE), and bound json_to_dynamic recursion at MAX_JSON_DEPTH=32 with lsm_warn on overshoot. 3 tests added.

title: rate-limit: 401 + active-lock serves stale endpoint data (pre-existing)
description:
Sequence: invocation A writes a failure lock on 401 (no cache update, intentional per the spec). Invocation B within the 30s error TTL sees the active lock and stale cache, enters the lock-active branch, and serves the stale endpoint data — violating the '401 does not serve stale' policy via the lock-active path.

Pre-existing bug surfaced during lsm-xhu review (silent-failure-hunter #A). Covered only for invocation A by endpoint_401_does_not_serve_stale_cache; no test covers the A→B sequence.

Fix sketch: in the lock-active branch, check entry.error == Some('Unauthorized') and fall through to JSONL (now that JSONL is wired) instead of serving stale data.
close_reason: lock-active branch now skips entry.data when lock.error == Unauthorized, closing the A→B stale-serve path. 3 tests added (A→B with empty JSONL, A→B with JSONL fallback, isolated guard). 401 handler intentionally keeps cache untouched — caching the Unauthorized tag would outlive the 30s lock TTL and mask a subsequent unrelated lock (Codex-flagged state leak).

title: Structured logger + doctor integration for silent Ok(None) paths
description:
Rate-limit segments (lsm-7po) and the usage cascade (lsm-wwd) have multiple `Ok(None)` hide paths and `let _ = write(...)` persistence drops that are currently invisible to users debugging 'why does my statusline look wrong?'.

Scope:
- Wire a `tracing`/`log`-style facade crate-wide with a `RUST_LOG`-ish env gate
- At every rate-limit `Ok(None)` site (bucket absent, resets_at missing, resets_at past, is_enabled=false, format_extra_usage returns None): emit a `debug!` with the gating condition
- At every cascade `write_cache`/`write_lock` failure site (currently `debug_assert!` + TODO(lsm-logger)): promote to a structured `warn!` that `linesmith doctor` can surface
- Wire `linesmith doctor` to read buffered traces and reformat into actionable remediation output
- Drop every `TODO(lsm-logger)` anchor comment in cascade.rs once landed

Blast radius: cascade.rs (6 anchor sites), 5 rate-limit segments (~8 Ok(None) paths total).

title: JSONL → UsageBucket mapping for rate-limit segments
description:
Cascade v0.1 (lsm-wwd) returns `Err(original)` whenever the endpoint fails, even when the JSONL aggregator has data, because `UsageBucket.utilization` requires a Percent we can't derive without tier detection (ADR-0011 is explicit that v0.1 skips tier detection).

Follow-up to ship actual JSONL-backed rendering. Options outlined in `docs/specs/jsonl-aggregation.md` §Open questions:

1. Hardcoded conservative tier-ceiling assumption (compute % against Max-tier caps; under-reports for Pro/Free)
2. Distinct `UsageData::Jsonl { tokens: JsonlTokens }` variant (biggest design change; type-design-analyzer's preferred approach)
3. Extend `UsageBucket` with an `Option<u64>` token-count side channel alongside the required utilization

Includes: update `jsonl-aggregation.md` §Open questions with resolution, update `rate-limit-segments.md` §JSONL-fallback display with concrete render for the chosen option, land the cascade code + tests.
close_reason: Cascade returns Ok(UsageData::Jsonl(...)) on every endpoint-failure path (NoCredentials, Timeout, NetworkError, RateLimited, Unauthorized) when the aggregator produces data. Ships the enum UsageData { Endpoint(EndpointUsage) | Jsonl(JsonlUsage) } shape per ADR-0013, deletes UsageSource, wires FiveHourWindow.ends_at into rate_limit_5h_reset, hides rate_limit_7d_reset and extra_usage under JSONL. Spec rate-limit-segments.md bumped to v0.2.1.

title: linesmith doctor: usage/credentials/cache diagnostics
description:
Per doctor.md spec (peek before implementation). Reports actionable diagnostics for the y6m data pipeline so users can self-serve before filing issues.

Ships: credential source report (MacosKeychainPrimary / MacosKeychainMultiAccount / EnvDir / XdgConfig / ClaudeLegacy + path/service detail; token REDACTED); cache file report (presence, cached_at, schema_version, TTL remaining, parse-ok); lock file report (presence, blocked_until, TTL remaining); endpoint reachability probe (single request with current credentials; report HTTP status + response-time); JSONL source report (project-root discovery result + entry count; no token/message-content exposure); exit code 0 on healthy / 1 on degraded / 2 on broken.
design: Read doctor.md before implementation to align report structure + exit-code conventions. Reuse DataContext rather than reimplementing fetch logic — doctor IS a client of the cascade. Do NOT mutate cache state during doctor run: probe endpoint with a dry_run=true flag that bypasses write-on-success path in slice 6.
acceptance_criteria: linesmith doctor runs with no arguments, prints report, exits cleanly. Token redaction: format! inspection confirms no bearer token bytes in output. Degraded cases: expired cache, active lock, credentials but no network all produce distinct messages. --json flag outputs structured report (machine-readable for CI).

description: Phase 6 of lsm-ewa. title: Phase 5: Wallclock timeout, log rate-limit, doctor surfacing for plugin runtime
description: Phase 5 of lsm-ewa. Three deliverables: (1) wallclock timeout per render via Engine::on_progress callback that checks an Instant and aborts past 50ms (rhai has no native timeout); (2) per-plugin log() rate-limit so a chatty plugin can't flood stderr (1 line per plugin per process for v0.1); (3) expose PluginRegistry load errors via a public method so a future linesmith doctor can surface them (the errors are already returned from PluginRegistry::load; need an API that lets external code query them post-construction). Acceptance: a timeout.rhai fixture (infinite loop) drops within ~50ms with no process hang; a chatty plugin emits at most one log line per render even if it calls log() 100 times; PluginRegistry exposes load_errors() or similar.

RenderState RAII guard cleans thread-locals + debug-asserts no leak from prior render.

title: release.yml workflow_dispatch dry-run path
description:
Wire the dry-run path through `release.yml` so `workflow_dispatch` builds all cargo-dist targets + generates SLSA attestations as workflow artifacts without creating a GitHub Release, publishing to crates.io, or pushing to the homebrew tap.

**Shipped scope:**
- Compute an ephemeral tag (`v0.0.0-dry-run-<short-sha>`) on dispatch and thread it via `dist build`'s `--tag` for artifact naming. Nothing is pushed to git. Unknown event types fail fast with `::error::` rather than silently emitting an empty tag-flag.
- Gate `publishing` on `github.event_name == 'push'` so `host` / `publish-homebrew-formula` / `announce` auto-skip on dispatch.
- Widen `build-local-artifacts` `if:` to admit `workflow_dispatch` — without this clause the existing `publishing == 'true' || pr_run_mode == 'upload'` gate evaluates false on dispatch (publishing is push-only; `dist-workspace.toml` pins `pr-run-mode = "skip"`), and the entire build matrix gets skipped.
- Add explicit `publishing == 'true'` to `publish-homebrew-formula` for defense-in-depth on top of `needs: host`.
- 7-day retention on workflow artifacts uploaded during dispatch; 90-day default preserved for real releases.

**Out of scope (split out):**
- `cargo publish --dry-run` integration: lives in `release-plz.yml`, not `release.yml`. release-plz has no dry-run path today; pipeline-validating crates.io changes still requires a local `cargo publish --dry-run` or a real `v0.0.x` patch release.
- `allow_dirty` input threading: cargo-dist 0.31's `--allow-dirty` is a boolean flag covering only "CI scripts out of date," already permanently allowed via the toml's `allow-dirty = ["ci"]`. No source-tree-dirty toggle exists in 0.31 to thread to, and CI checkouts are always clean. The placeholder input added in lsm-2xd was removed.
- Auto-trigger on PRs touching release infra → lsm-2bei.

**Constraints:**
- `release.yml` is cargo-dist-generated but protected by `allow-dirty = ["ci"]` in `dist-workspace.toml`, so hand-edits survive regeneration.
- Tag-push trigger unchanged so real releases still work the same way.

**Validation:** verified actionlint clean (only pre-existing autogen'd shellcheck warnings), prettier + markdownlint pass. Real validation requires a `workflow_dispatch` invocation against a branch after merge — that's the whole point of the feature.

Spec: `docs/specs/release-process.md` §Dry-run workflow.
close_reason: workflow_dispatch path threads through release.yml: ephemeral tag (v0.0.0-dry-run-<short-sha>), publishing flag gated to push events, build-local-artifacts gate widened so dispatch actually builds, publish-homebrew-formula given an explicit publishing gate for defense-in-depth, 7-day retention on dispatch artifacts, fail-fast on unknown event types. allow_dirty input removed (cargo-dist 0.31 has no source-dirty toggle to thread to). cargo publish dry-run remains TODO in release-plz.yml. PR auto-trigger filed as lsm-2bei.

title: Update plugin-api.md to describe rhai plugin data_deps declaration
description:
Follow-up from segment-system.md v0.3 update (lsm-thm). The canonical Segment trait now requires `data_deps() -> &'static [DataDep]` so the runtime can prefetch only declared sources. Rhai plugins are wrapped via RhaiSegment, which means plugins need a script-side mechanism to declare their deps — otherwise every plugin falls through to the default `[Status]` and non-stdin sources (usage, credentials, claude_json, jsonl) never get prefetched. Plugin authors calling `ctx.usage()` would trigger blocking lazy-init on the hot render path.

Proposed syntax: a script-header comment like `// @data_deps = ["usage", "claude_json"]` parsed by the RhaiSegment loader at config-load time. Alternative: a `.linesmith.toml` sibling file per plugin.

Acceptance:
- plugin-api.md bumps to v0.2 (or whatever aligns with its version cadence)
- Adds a §Data dependencies section describing the metadata syntax
- Shows an example rhai script with the declaration header
- Documents how DataContext fields are exposed to rhai (rhai needs binding for each source type)
- Links to data-fetching.md's DataDep enum for the full list
- Notes any dep-validation errors (unknown dep name, malformed header)
notes: Filed from lsm-thm / segment-system.md v0.3 review. Without this, rhai plugins cannot correctly consume non-stdin data sources.
close_reason: docs/specs/plugin-api.md bumped to v0.2. Adds @data_deps script-header declaration with valid dep-name table mapping to DataDep enum variants. ctx shape now mirrors DataContext: ctx.status exposes parsed stdin (StatusContext), ctx.usage/credentials/claude_json/jsonl/git/etc. populated when declared. Result-shaped accessors use tagged #{ kind: 'ok' | 'error', data | error } convention. Existing v0.1 scripts migrate via one-time ctx.X → ctx.status.X rename. RhaiSegment wrapper updated to match segment-system.md v0.3 (declared_deps field + data_deps() method + &DataContext render). New edge cases for UnknownDataDep / MalformedDataDeps startup errors and undeclared-dep accessor behavior. Closes the consistency gap opened by segment-system v0.3 — rhai plugins can now declare non-stdin data dependencies and the runtime's lazy-load prefetch honors them.

title: Update segment-system.md to v0.3: absorb data_deps() + StatusContext.data
description:
Update segment-system.md from v0.2 to v0.3 to match the three rate-limit-lane specs:

1. Change the Segment trait's render signature from `render(&self, ctx: &StatusContext) -> RenderResult` to `render(&self, ctx: &DataContext) -> RenderResult`. DataContext owns StatusContext as a field (ctx.status), so segments that only need stdin data lose nothing.
2. Add a `data_deps(&self) -> &'static [DataDep]` method to the trait with default `&[DataDep::Status]`. See docs/specs/data-fetching.md §Segment dependency declaration for semantics.
3. Verify plugin-api.md's rhai binding story still works — rhai segments will need to declare deps via script metadata (e.g., a `deps = ['usage']` preamble in the .rhai file).

Why this is a v0.3 bump (not v0.2 amendment): signature change is breaking. Any segment code in segment-system.md v0.2's examples will need updating.

title: Research: JSON parser + cache serialization stack due-diligence
description:
Before writing Rust code for the data-fetching layer (lsm-y6m + supporting beads), survey the actual parser/serialization landscape with real benchmarks. Outputs decision matrix per source.

Context: docs/research/data-fetching-strategy.md §Parsing efficiency claims serde_json + partial structs is fastest pragmatic choice. Need due-diligence to either validate or refute that claim with real numbers, not estimates.

Acceptance:
- Survey current Rust JSON parsers: serde_json, simd-json, sonic-rs, json-rust, plus anything else relevant
- Real benchmark numbers for our workloads: small <10KB (settings.json, sessions/*.json, OAuth response), medium ~125KB (~/.claude.json), JSONL streaming (MB+)
- Crate maturity signals: last commit, downloads/month, open issues, MSRV, transitive dep count + binary size impact
- What comparable Rust CLIs use for hot-path JSON: ripgrep, fd, bat, gitui, jujutsu, eza, dust, hyperfine — pull their Cargo.tomls
- Memory mapping (memmap2 vs read-into-Vec): edge cases, JSONL append-during-read, Windows quirks
- Internal cache serialization options: bincode vs rkyv vs postcard vs JSON. Decode speed, schema-migration story, inspectability
- JSONL-specialized libraries (jsonl crate, etc.) — anything purpose-built we're missing
- Decision matrix: per data source, recommended parser + format with explicit tradeoff
- Output: docs/research/json-parsing-stack.md (then promote relevant decisions to an ADR slice)

Why now: This is the last research gap before implementation begins on the data-fetching layer. Locking in parser choices speculatively (rather than measuring) creates churn later.
notes: Promoted from a conversation about whether serde_json is fast enough. User flagged: 'I just want to make sure we do our due diligence before starting it.'
close_reason: serde_json + partial structs is the validated v0.1 choice. 9 of 13 surveyed Rust CLIs use serde_json on hot paths; zero use simd-json or sonic-rs. Partial-struct deserialization drops ~/.claude.json parse cost 80%+ — bigger win than swapping parsers. Cache stays JSON (pretty + schema_version) for inspectability; binary saves negligible time at 1KB. JSONL incremental tail via BufReader::read_line + byte offset; mmap contraindicated due to SIGBUS-on-rotation. simd-json deferred behind --features fast-json flag, promotion only on benchmarked >2ms p50 win. bincode upstream archived 2025-08-15 — flagged for future binary-cache decisions. Full doc: docs/research/json-parsing-stack.md.

title: Investigate: does context_window percentage stay correct across 1M / post-compact / post-resume / 429s?
description:
Spike, not a feature. docs/ideas/0001-feature-parity-matrix.md tags 'Context window percentage correct across 1M / compact / resume / 429s' as a v0.1 differentiator.

**Competitor finding:** ccstatusline has TWO distinct context widgets — ContextPercentage AND ContextPercentageUsable. The split strongly suggests that after /compact the raw percentage from Claude Code's stdin payload doesn't reflect usable budget. That's likely the edge case we need to measure + reproduce.

**Scope (investigation only, no code change this bead):**
- Read Claude Code statusline JSON payload docs + latest Code release notes
- Test by running linesmith against: (a) a 200k-context session pre-compact, (b) same session post-compact, (c) post-/resume, (d) during a 429 response, (e) in 1M-context (Claude Opus 4.7 1M variant)
- Inspect ccstatusline's ContextPercentage vs ContextPercentageUsable implementations — that's the target behavior
- For each case, verify: used_percentage matches visible reality, context_window_size reflects the actual model cap, no misleading 0% or 100% glitches
- Document findings in docs/research/context-window-correctness.md
- If issues found: file per-issue beads; likely need a ContextPercentageUsable-style companion segment + possibly an ADR on how we compute 'usable' (subtract system prompt + compact overhead?)
- If no issues found: close with 'investigated; no gaps for v0.1'

**Prior art:**
- sirmalloc/ccstatusline widgets/ContextPercentage.ts + ContextPercentageUsable.ts

**Acceptance:** research note exists with a pass/fail for each of the 5 edge cases + documents the ContextPercentageUsable distinction. Follow-up beads filed for any failures.
close_reason: Research note shipped at docs/research/context-window-correctness.md. Key shift from original hypothesis: ccstatusline trusts used_percentage verbatim — zero compact/resume/429 compensation code. title: context_bar segment: visual bar for context-window fill (v0.1 differentiator)
description:
v0.1 differentiator per docs/ideas/0001-feature-parity-matrix.md: 'Context window bar (visual) — size configurable'. claude-powerline + claude-hud + ccstatusline all ship it; we don't.

**Competitor finding:** ccstatusline's ContextBar widget is the reference. Width configurable, three-color threshold ramp (green/yellow/red). Same shape as our proposed design.

**Scope:**
- New segments/context_bar.rs implementing Segment trait
- Renders as Unicode block-char bar: '████▓░░░░░' or similar, with color ramp green → yellow → red as fill approaches 100%
- Configurable via [segments.context_bar]:
  - width (default 10 cells)
  - thresholds (e.g., green <50%, yellow <80%, red ≤100%)
  - characters (full/partial/empty block set — allow Nerd Font swap)
- Source: context_window.used_percentage (already in StatusContext)
- Returns None when context_window is missing
- Narrow-terminal behavior: bar drops under width pressure via normal priority system
- **Differentiator:** ccstatusline's bar is fixed width in the UI. Ours exposes width configurably so users pick 5-cell compact vs 20-cell expansive.
- Tests: 0%, 50%, 100%, boundary thresholds, different widths, NoColor fallback (swap colored blocks for high/med/low ASCII chars)

**Related work:** the lsm-4wb spike may surface a 'ContextPercentageUsable' style distinction — if we add a usable-variant, the bar should key off the same computation to stay consistent.

**Prior art:** sirmalloc/ccstatusline widgets/ContextBar.ts

**Acceptance:** 'context_bar' renders a visual fill bar colored by threshold; width configurable; hidden when context_window is None.
close_reason: Add context_bar segment: Unicode block-char bar (defaults to width 10 cells, '█▓░' glyphs) colored by green/yellow/red threshold ramp via Role::Success/Warning/Error. Configured under [segments.context_bar] with cells, thresholds.{green,yellow}, and characters.{full,partial,empty}. Thresholds are pair-validated (monotonic by Thresholds::new); bar pct is round-ties-to-even to match the textual context_window's banker's rounding so text and bar agree at every boundary. Glyphs constrained to single-cell to preserve RenderedSegment::width()==cfg.width. Hidden when context_window absent.

title: tokens segment: total input / output / cache tokens (v0.1 parity)
description:
v0.1 parity item per docs/ideas/0001-feature-parity-matrix.md (Token / Context section).

**Competitor finding:** ccstatusline splits this into **4 widgets** — TokensInput, TokensOutput, TokensCached, TokensTotal. Rather than a single 'tokens' segment with config toggles, consider matching their split: gives users fine-grained layout control (e.g., show only input+output, or only total) without a config forest.

**Scope (recommended split):**
- 4 segments: tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_cached, tokens_total
- Each reads the corresponding field from context_window.current_usage
- Each returns None when current_usage is missing (pre-first-API-call)
- Defaults priority: lower than context_window, same bucket as cost — spec TBD
- Formatting: 'k' / 'M' suffix for >1000 / >1M
- Add to built_in_by_id (NOT DEFAULT_SEGMENT_IDS — all opt-in)
- Add 'power-user' preset to include tokens_total (others available to users who want them)

**Alternative:** single 'tokens' segment with config like [segments.tokens.show] = ['input', 'output'] — simpler mental model but locks users into one display shape.

**Decision point (in the spec or inline during implementation):** prefer the 4-segment split per ccstatusline; users compose via config.line.segments, which matches how powerline-style statuslines work.

**Prior art:** sirmalloc/ccstatusline widgets/TokensInput.ts / TokensOutput.ts / TokensCached.ts / TokensTotal.ts

**Acceptance:** tokens_input / tokens_output / tokens_cached / tokens_total segments render from stdin current_usage fields; all hidden when current_usage is None; covered by unit tests.

title: GitHub repo settings: branch protection, auto-delete, squash-merge, Discussions, security
description:
User-side GitHub UI settings (no code change). Needed before CI (lsm-pud) can be a required gate on merges.

**Scope (all via Settings → ... on github.com/oakoss/linesmith):**

**Branch protection on 'main':**
- Require a pull request before merging
- Require status checks: static-analysis + tests (from lsm-pud)
- Require branches to be up to date before merging
- Require conversation resolution before merging
- Dismiss stale approvals on new commits (optional)

**Merge settings:**
- Enable: Squash merging (default — matches atomic-commit discipline per AGENTS.md)
- Disable: Merge commits (optional — forces squash)
- Disable: Rebase merging (optional)
- Enable: Automatically delete head branches

**General:**
- Enable: Discussions (referenced by .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml from lsm-ref)
- Verify: Dependabot alerts enabled (default on for public repos)
- Verify: Dependabot security updates enabled (probably conflicts with Renovate — disable Dependabot security if Renovate picks up advisories)
- Verify: Secret scanning enabled (default)
- Verify: Secret scanning push protection enabled
- Verify: Private vulnerability reporting enabled (per oakoss/.github/SECURITY.md)

**Depends on:** lsm-pud (CI workflow must exist before setting it as a required check).

**Acceptance:** merging to main requires a passing CI run; head branches auto-delete on merge; Discussions tab is visible; Dependabot alerts + Renovate don't conflict.
notes:
Per lsm-h9ys (cross-platform OS matrix): branch protection should gate on the 'CI Summary' check name as the single choke point. Reasoning:

- 'CI Summary' is one stable name that doesn't drift as we add matrix cells (lsm-h9ys) or new jobs (lsm-fbar MSRV, lsm-vj7 cargo-deny).
- It already calls fail_unless_success against every needs.X.result — so it goes red iff any required job goes red.
- Alternative is enumerating each individual check ('Static Analysis', 'Tests (ubuntu-latest)', 'Tests (macos-latest)', 'Tests (windows-latest)', '...'). That works but requires updating branch protection every time we add or rename a job, which is the kind of drift that bites silently.

If you want per-job granularity in branch protection too (e.g. for finer-grained 'this job is allowed to fail' configurations), require both 'CI Summary' AND the individual names. But the minimum-viable safe gate is 'CI Summary' alone.
close_reason: GitHub repo settings: project ruleset 'Required CI Checks' (id 15551225) requires CI Summary status check + strict up-to-date with main, stacking on top of org ruleset 'Main Branch - Org' (id 10195660) which already enforces PR + squash-only + linear history + signed commits + no force-push/deletion. Discussions enabled. Rebase merge disabled (org ruleset already blocked it; UI cleanup). Pre-existing settings already correct: squash merge enabled, merge commits disabled, auto-delete head branches, dependabot alerts enabled (security-updates correctly disabled — Renovate will replace), secret scanning + push protection + non-provider patterns + validity checks all enabled, private vulnerability reporting enabled, squash commit title=PR_TITLE + message=COMMIT_MESSAGES (preserves carefully-written commit messages verbatim).

title: Write docs/specs/doctor.md (or extend config.md §Doctor)
description:
Unblocks lsm-l35 (doctor command). Specs the contract for each health check.

title: linesmith doctor command (env + config + terminal health check)
description:
'linesmith doctor' subcommand per docs/specs/doctor.md (v0.1, landed). Diagnostic CLI that inspects environment, config, Claude Code integration, credentials, cache, plugins, git, and self-version — reports each check as PASS/WARN/FAIL/SKIP with remediation hints.

**Epic; sliced into lsm-l35.1 through lsm-l35.8.**

**Scope (per doctor.md §Check catalog):**
- CLI surface: linesmith doctor [--plain] (no --full; all checks always run — see doctor.md change log 2026-04-29)
- Severity levels: PASS / WARN / FAIL / SKIP with Unicode + ASCII glyphs
- Exit codes: any FAIL → 1; WARN-only or all-PASS → 0; usage error → 2
- I/O failures during render → reported to stderr, exit code from report (matches cli_main convention)
- Default output: grouped tree by category with colors + Unicode
- --plain: ASCII glyphs + ASCII separators; renderer-emitted strings only (user-supplied label/hint pass through verbatim)
- Check catalog across 8 categories: Environment, Config, Claude Code, Credentials, Cache, Rate-limit endpoint, Plugins, Git, Self
- Network probes (rate-limit endpoint + GitHub update check) run unconditionally; transport-level errors → WARN, not FAIL
- Short-circuit propagation ($HOME missing → skip file-based; config parse fail → skip segment checks; OAuth token missing → skip endpoint probe)
- Non-interactive tty / piped stdout → WARN (not FAIL) so --plain CI use doesn't gate exit-1
- NO_COLOR is a PASS (user preference, not degradation)
- Panic handling: release profile is panic=abort per ADR-0007; panicking check terminates whole run. Checks written defensively so panics indicate doctor bugs
- linesmith init auto-runs doctor unless --no-doctor passed (slice .7)

**Deferred to v0.2+ per spec:**
- --json machine-readable output (id field already populated in v0.1; serializer is the only remaining work)
- --verbose / -v detail level (separate follow-up bead)
- --offline opt-out (separate follow-up bead)
- doctor fix auto-remediation

**Acceptance:** every 'linesmith doctor can inspect this' hook from the data-fetching lane specs is covered; catches mistyped theme, missing config, OAuth token issues, Claude Code not installed; --plain produces CI-friendly output; offline runs exit 0 (network errors are WARN, not FAIL); tree rendering wraps cleanly at 40+ cells.

title: Add ahead/behind counters to git_branch segment
description:
