title: Write docs/specs/git-segments.md
description:
Unblocks lsm-8jl (git epic). Specs the contract for every git-derived segment.

**Scope:**
- Crate choice: gix vs. git2 (cite ADR-0001; gix is in the stated stack but if it can't discover worktrees cleanly, document the alternative)
- Data sources per segment:
  - git_branch: HEAD ref resolution; detached-HEAD fallback to short SHA
  - dirty: staged / unstaged / untracked; display as single-char indicators or counts; configurable
  - ahead/behind: compare HEAD to upstream; handle no-upstream gracefully

- Platform notes: Windows path separators, case-insensitive FS

description:

- .github/workflows/ci.yml — static-analysis (fmt + lint:md + cargo fmt + clippy + check) + tests + summary job; runs on PR + push to main (oakterm shape)
- .github/workflows/codeql.yml — scans GitHub Actions only (Rust not supported by CodeQL; cargo-audit/deny covers Rust)
- .github/workflows/audit.yml + deny.toml — cargo-deny check (dependency security, license policy, duplicates, advisory feed)
- .github/renovate.json — Renovate config mirroring oakoss/oakterm pattern (config:recommended, group:allNonMajor, helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests, schedule:earlyMondays, semantic-commit chore, automerge, cargo enabled, rangeStrategy=bump, prConcurrentLimit=5)

**Reference configs:**
- jbabin91/autocomplete-rs (full audit + deny setup)
- oakoss/oakterm (minimal CI + CodeQL + Renovate baseline)

**Why separate from release pipeline:** CI benefits every PR today, not just at release time. Also unblocks trust in auto-merging Renovate PRs.

**Acceptance:** every PR runs CI + CodeQL + audit and must pass before merge. Renovate proposes dep updates weekly, auto-merges non-major ones that pass CI. Branch protection rules updated to require CI green.

Sub-tasks filed as dependent beads.

title: Cut v0.1.0-rc1 dry-run release and verify pipeline end-to-end
description:
Part of lsm-c2i epic. First actual release cut — validates the pipeline before we tag an actual v0.1.0.

**Scope:**
- Bump Cargo.toml version to 0.1.0-rc.1
- git tag v0.1.0-rc.1 and push
- Monitor cargo-dist workflow: all 6 targets build, artifacts upload, GH pre-release created with binaries + checksums
- Verify Homebrew formula appears in oakoss/homebrew-tap
- Verify CHANGELOG.md appears / updates
- Do NOT publish to crates.io on RC (set 'publish = false' in Cargo.toml for the RC, or use a prerelease-aware workflow)
- Download each platform binary and smoke-test: binary runs, prints --version, accepts stdin JSON
- If all green, plan the real v0.1.0 tag (depends on lsm-5yd init + git_branch epic + doctor being done first)

**Depends on:** lsm-2xd (configs), lsm-b6z (prereqs).

**Acceptance:** v0.1.0-rc.1 GH pre-release exists with 6 binaries; installer script works end-to-end on at least one mac + one linux machine; brew tap has a working formula; no crates.io publish.

Plan deviated from RC-first because the bootstrap publish already put linesmith 0.1.0 on crates.io — RC for an already-published version would be contradictory. Instead: tagged v0.1.0 directly on HEAD, release.yml built all 7 targets (fixed 2 issues along the way: missing [profile.dist] in Cargo.toml; empty oakoss/homebrew-tap needed initial main-branch commit). title: linesmith init: interactive onboarding + Claude Code settings snippet
description:
Part B of the original lsm-kb6 split. Builds on lsm-kb6 (presets list/apply + embedded TOMLs).

**Scope:**
- 'linesmith init' interactive prompts via dialoguer: preset (from the list registered in lsm-kb6), theme (from lsm-qp5's ThemeRegistry), tool (claude-code / qwen-code / auto)
- Resolve config path via existing XDG resolver; create directories as needed (0755); write config.toml
- After write, emit the Claude Code settings.json snippet to stdout for copy-paste:
    "statusLine": {
      "type": "command",
      "command": "linesmith",
      "padding": 0
    }
- Offer (y/n prompt) to run 'linesmith doctor' — if doctor subcommand isn't ready yet, print 'linesmith doctor coming soon' and skip the offer (file a placeholder then)
- New dep: dialoguer
- Tests: init_creates_valid_config_round_trips_parse, init_writes_to_resolved_xdg_path, init_emits_settings_snippet
- If the resolved config path already has a file, fall through to the same overwrite/backup behavior as 'presets apply' (share that helper from lsm-kb6)

**Why split from lsm-kb6:** Part A ('presets list'/'apply') is non-interactive, testable via pure file I/O, no new deps. Part B adds dialoguer + interactive flow + TTY concerns. Separating lets Part A ship standalone.

**Acceptance:** 'linesmith init' with no existing config writes a valid starter config and emits the Claude Code snippet. Running the resulting config round-trips through Config::from_str without errors.
close_reason: linesmith init: dialoguer prompts for preset+theme, writes config.toml to the resolved path with theme injected, prints a Claude Code settings.json snippet that honors --config and LINESMITH_CONFIG, warns on shell-quoting hazards (spaces, metacharacters, leading dash, non-UTF-8). Spec docs/specs/config.md §init updated to v0.1.2. Two follow-ups filed: lsm-w0kx (dialoguer bypasses cli_main's injected stdin), lsm-9ll1 (rename-after-clobber breadcrumb test gap).

title: Style string syntax + [segments.<id>].style config overrides
description:
Follow-up to lsm-qp5 (user themes). Splits the style-syntax concern out because it's independent of theme-file loading: users can restyle individual segments even without authoring a full theme.

**Scope:**
- Parse style strings per docs/specs/theming.md §Style syntax:
  - `role:<name>` → Style.role = Some(Role::X) where <name> is case-insensitive match to Role variants
  - `fg:<color>` → Style.fg = Some(Color::X) where <color> is hex / named / rgb() (shares color parser with lsm-qp5's theme TOML loader)
  - Decorations: `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `dim` (case-insensitive)
  - Empty string / whitespace only → Style::default()
  - Whitespace-separated tokens, order doesn't matter
- Surface parse errors at config-load via validate_keys companion: invalid role name / invalid color spec warn + fall back to default style
- Wire Style into config: extend SegmentOverride with `style: Option<String>` (keep as raw string in config, parse at apply_override time) — or `style: Option<Style>` via serde with_from_str pattern
- Wire through apply_override in segments/builder.rs: if style is set, the RenderedSegment's style gets overridden
- Resolution precedence (already spec'd in theming.md): user style overrides segment's declared role
- Tests: all syntax variants, invalid-role warn, invalid-color warn, override wins over segment role

**Depends on:** lsm-qp5 (shared color-parsing helpers — hex/named/rgb() parsers can be extracted from the theme TOML loader)

**Acceptance:** `[segments.model] style = "role:primary bold"` in config.toml renders model with Primary role + bold. `style = "fg:#ff00ff italic"` uses an explicit color that outranks the segment's declared role.
close_reason: Style-string parser (role:/fg:/bold/italic/underline/dim) with paren-aware tokenizer for rgb(r, g, b). SegmentOverride.style wired through apply_override with warn-and-skip on invalid input; empty/whitespace-only styles are no-ops. Seven-variant StyleParseError with offending input. One follow-up filed (lsm-7nl).

title: [layout_options].separator styles: powerline (MVP), capsule, flex
description:
Add `[layout_options].separator` config knob with reserved keywords, arbitrary-literal fallback, and a `[layout_options].powerline_width` companion knob.

**Shipped scope (v0.1):**
- Reserved keywords: `space` (default), `powerline` (Nerd Font U+E0B0 chevron), `capsule` / `flex` (warn + fall back to `space`; reserved for v0.2+), `""` (truly empty → `Separator::None`).
- Arbitrary literal fallback: anything not a reserved keyword renders verbatim. `separator = " | "` and `separator = " · "` reach ccstatusline parity for homogeneous-separator configs.
- Whitespace-vs-empty distinction: `""` → no separator; `"   "` → 3-space literal. The truly-empty bypass runs *before* the keyword `trim().to_ascii_lowercase()` pass, so user-meaningful whitespace literals survive.
- `powerline_width = 1 | 2`: cell-count knob for fonts where U+E0B0 renders as 2 cells. Validated at the config boundary into a typed `PowerlineWidth { One, Two }` enum so downstream layout math can never see an invalid width.
- Padded chevron rendering: `Powerline.text()` emits ` ▶ ` (single-space pad each side) so the chevron has breathing room without bg fill; `width()` reports `chevron_cells + 2`.
- `Role::Muted` chevron styling. `Role::Border` was tried first and rejected — too dim against dark themes (surface2 ≈ background on catppuccin-mocha).
- `OverriddenSegment` rewrites both the segment's `default_separator` AND any per-render `right_separator: Some(Space|Theme)` so plugin segments returning the implicit Space can't bypass the global layout-options choice.
- Test coverage: parser keyword/literal/whitespace decision tree, builder wrap policy (Space/Theme replace, Literal/None/Powerline preserve), `apply_separator_override` branches (5), priority-drop with powerline budget, end-to-end `render_with_warn` plumbing, boundary `powerline_width` validation, padded-chevron total_width math.

**Out of scope (split out):**
- True bg-transition powerline (chevron with previous-segment bg + next-segment fg): blocked on `Style.bg` infra → lsm-aivt.
- Powerline-passthrough gap (segments hardcoding `Powerline { width: One }` ignoring user's `powerline_width = 2`): pinned today as deliberate behavior → lsm-5azz.
- `did_you_mean` warning for typo'd keywords (`"powereline"` silently emits as a literal): pinned by test as deliberate → lsm-edce.
- Mixed per-segment separators (some boundaries powerline, some pipe, some space): requires the separator-as-item refactor → lsm-herx.2.

Spec: `docs/specs/config.md` §layout_options.
notes: Shipped 2026-04-29 after multiple review rounds (pr-review-toolkit + Codex). Notable design decisions captured in code: (a) PowerlineWidth { One, Two } enum at the type layer makes invalid widths unrepresentable downstream; (b) Role::Muted over Role::Border for chevron color (dark-theme legibility); (c) padded chevron rendering compensates for absent bg fill until lsm-aivt lands; (d) apply_separator_override handles plugin runtime separators alongside default_separator overrides. Follow-ups filed: lsm-aivt (bg-transition), lsm-5azz (passthrough gap), lsm-edce (did_you_mean). lsm-t6sq closed as obsolete — its powerline_width knob shipped here. Migration path to lsm-herx.2: when separator-as-item lands, port apply_layout_separator's wrap policy to inline Separator items, preserving back-compat for existing [layout_options].separator configs.
close_reason: [layout_options].separator (keywords + arbitrary literal) + powerline_width knob (typed PowerlineWidth { One, Two }). Padded ▶ chevron, Role::Muted styling. OverriddenSegment also rewrites plugin runtime right_separator.

title: RFC: Extract CLI driver + segment builder from lib.rs
description:
## Problem

lib.rs is ~1300 lines and co-hosts five concerns: the render façade (`run`, `run_with_width`, `run_with_segments_and_width`, `run_with_context`, `RenderContext`), width detection, segment assembly with override validation, the CLI driver (`CliEnv`, `cli_main`, `run_cli`, `load_config`, `check_config`, `resolve_theme`), and ~740 lines of tests across two inline modules. Navigating any single concern requires understanding the whole file; adding tests to one domain requires reading the others. The render façade legitimately belongs at the crate root, but the CLI orchestration and segment assembly are implementation details that leak into the public-API file.

## Proposed Interface

Two new modules, each with a minimal surface. All existing `linesmith::*` paths preserved via re-exports; `main.rs` and `tests/integration.rs` do not change.

### `crate::driver` (new file `src/driver.rs`)

Public surface — two items:

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct CliEnv {
    pub linesmith_config: Option<String>,
    pub xdg_config_home: Option<String>,
    pub home: Option<String>,
    pub terminal_width: Option<u16>,
    pub color_capability: Option<crate::theme::Capability>,
}

impl CliEnv {
    pub fn from_process() -> Self;  // snapshot real env
    pub fn for_tests() -> Self;     // None paths, width=Some(200), capability=Some(None)
    pub fn empty() -> Self;         // all None — for tests asserting on lazy detection
}

pub fn cli_main<A>(
    args: A,
    stdin: impl std::io::Read,
    stdout: &mut dyn std::io::Write,
    stderr: &mut dyn std::io::Write,
    env: &CliEnv,
) -> u8
where A: IntoIterator, A::Item: Into<std::ffi::OsString>;
```

Crate-private: `run_cli`, `load_config`, `check_config`, `resolve_theme` become `fn` (no `pub`).

### `crate::segments::builder` (new file `src/segments/builder.rs`)

Public surface — two items:

```rust
pub fn build(config: Option<&crate::config::Config>, warn: impl FnMut(&str)) -> Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>;
pub fn build_default() -> Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>;
```

Crate-private: `apply_override`.

### Crate-root re-exports (in `lib.rs`)

```rust
pub use driver::{cli_main, CliEnv};
pub use segments::builder::{build as build_segments, build_default as build_default_segments};
```

Rename-on-re-export preserves integration-test call sites.

## Dependency Strategy

**In-process** — all logic is pure plus thin I/O wrappers. Nothing crosses a network/process boundary. No new traits or adapters introduced; external-crate wrappers (`supports-color`, `terminal-size`, `toml`, `serde_json`) already live as single-function seams that can be swapped in place.

## Testing Strategy

**Test relocation** — replace, don't layer:

- `cli_main_tests` module (15 tests, ~540 lines) moves from `lib.rs` → `driver.rs`
- `build_segments_*` tests (~8 tests, plus `StubWithWidth` + `width_merge_*` = 12 tests total, ~200 lines) move from `lib.rs::tests` → `segments/builder.rs::tests`
- Width detection tests + `resolve_terminal_width` tests stay in `lib.rs`
- Render-path tests (`malformed_json_renders_marker_and_succeeds`, `minimal_payload_renders_model_then_workspace`, `full_payload_renders_model_context_workspace`) stay in `lib.rs`
- Integration tests at `tests/integration.rs` untouched

**No new tests added** — this is a move refactor. Test count stays at 240 lib + 7 integration.

**New `CliEnv::for_tests()` constructor** replaces the duplicated `fn empty_env()` helper inside `cli_main_tests`. Net LOC reduction ~10 lines of test setup.

## Implementation Recommendations

### What `driver` owns

- Args → exit code (the full CLI lifecycle)
- Config path resolution, load, validation
- `--check-config` exit-code contract (0 ok / 1 invalid)
- Lazy width + capability detection on render path only
- Theme name resolution with unknown-name warning + fallback
- IO wiring through injected stdin/stdout/stderr sinks

### What `driver` hides

- That arg parsing goes through `lexopt` via `cli::parse`
- That config loading is a two-step resolve-then-read
- That `--check-config` has four failure modes (no-path / invalid-parse / no-file-implicit / valid-with-warnings)
- The specific env vars (`LINESMITH_CONFIG`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HOME`) and their precedence

### What `driver` exposes

- `CliEnv` as the sole input struct for ambient process state
- `cli_main` as the sole orchestration entry point
- `u8` exit code (callers wrap in `ExitCode` at the binary boundary)

### What `segments::builder` owns

- `Config` → `Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>` transformation
- Validation: unknown IDs warn + skip, duplicates keep-first, empty-list warning, inverted-bounds drop with warning
- Override application: priority + width-with-inherit-from-inner-default

### What `segments::builder` hides

- The `DEFAULT_SEGMENT_IDS` canonical order
- The `OverriddenSegment` wrapper (applied internally when a `[segments.<id>]` table exists)
- Width-bounds merge algorithm (caller supplies half-specified bounds; builder inherits the other half from the segment's built-in default)

### What `segments::builder` exposes

- Two free functions keyed on `Option<&Config>` + warn callback
- Return type `Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>` unchanged from today

### Migration

- `main.rs` and `tests/integration.rs` keep working unchanged — re-exports handle the path shift
- `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `lib.rs` loses its width + build_segments blocks but keeps render tests
- No public API deletions; no breaking changes

## Scope boundary

Explicitly NOT in this refactor:
- Extension traits for plugin runtime (`lsm-ewa` owns that design)
- Theme registry trait for user-loaded themes (`lsm-qp5` owns that)
- External-crate leak tightening (separate bead — tighten `lexopt::Error` / `toml::de::Error` surfaces out of public API)
- `cli_main_from_process()` convenience wrapper (net-zero move, adds surface for no gain)
- `theme::catppuccin` sketch (belongs in `lsm-b7u`)

## Expected impact

- `lib.rs`: ~1300 → ~400 lines (render façade + width + re-exports + render tests)
- `driver.rs`: new, ~250 lines + ~540 test lines
- `segments/builder.rs`: new, ~90 lines + ~210 test lines
- Public API: zero surface change
- Test count: unchanged (240 lib + 7 integration)
- Follow-ups enabled: any future module deepening can happen inside `driver` or `builder` without touching `lib.rs`
close_reason: Extracted CLI driver into crate::driver and segment assembly into crate::segments::builder. lib.rs: 1206 → 273 lines (77% reduction). Both new modules pub(crate) so re-exports at crate root (linesmith::cli_main, linesmith::CliEnv, linesmith::build_segments, linesmith::build_default_segments) are the canonical paths. Added CliEnv::for_tests() named constructor replacing the anonymous empty_env() helper. Test count unchanged (240 lib + 7 integration). No public API change. Codex review + 5-agent review pass confirmed byte-identical behavior.

title: Slice 7c: User theme TOML loading + themes list subcommand
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn. Lets users drop a theme file into `~/.config/linesmith/themes/` and reference it from config.

**Scope:**
- Theme TOML file format parser (per docs/specs/theming.md §Theme file format): required `name`, `[roles]` base table, optional `[roles.extended]` table, optional `[separators]` table (for lsm-1my forward-compat)
- Color parsing in theme files: hex (`"#rgb"`, `"#rrggbb"`), named 16-color (`"red"`), RGB (`"rgb(r, g, b)"`) — normalized to `Color::TrueColor` or `Color::Palette16`
- User theme discovery: walk `~/.config/linesmith/themes/*.toml` at startup, XDG-compliant
- Name-collision handling: user theme wins over built-in of same name; stderr warning
- Parse error handling: one rejected theme doesn't abort startup; warn with file path + row/col, fall back to `default` if the config asks for the rejected theme
- `linesmith themes list` CLI subcommand: enumerate built-ins + user themes with source annotation (`built-in` vs `~/.config/linesmith/themes/mocha.toml`)

**Out of scope (separate bead):**
- Style string syntax (`"role:success bold"`, `"fg:#ff8800 underline"`) — orthogonal to theme files
- Per-segment style overrides via `[segments.<id>] style = "..."` in config.toml
- Catppuccin conformance tests against user-authored theme files (ships with lsm-b7u already)

**Acceptance:** drop a `mytheme.toml` in `~/.config/linesmith/themes/`, reference it via `theme = "mytheme"` in config.toml, see it render. `linesmith themes list` shows both built-in and user themes with source paths. Name collision with a built-in shows a warning and the user theme wins.
close_reason: User theme TOML loading + themes list subcommand. Users drop files in ~/.config/linesmith/themes/*.toml (XDG-aware); merged into a ThemeRegistry alongside built-ins. Color parsing supports hex (#rgb / #rrggbb), named 16-color, rgb(r,g,b), and 'none'. Two-phase parse with validate_theme_file_keys catches typos at top-level, [roles], [roles.extended], and [separators] with file-path-prefixed warnings. First-user-found wins on collision per spec §Edge cases; user always wins over built-in. New cli::Action::ThemesList subcommand prints registered themes with source annotation. 329 lib + 7 integration tests (up from 290).

title: Slice 7b: Catppuccin flavors (Latte/Frappé/Macchiato/Mocha)
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (MVP theme engine). Ships the 4 Catppuccin flavors against the MVP theme registry so linesmith qualifies for the Catppuccin integration list (github.com/catppuccin/catppuccin#portlist).

Scope:
- Depend on `catppuccin` crate (~20KB) OR embed 4 TOML palettes via include_str!. Decision point during implementation; crate is leaner for palette drift detection.
- Register 4 flavors in the built-in theme registry: catppuccin-latte, catppuccin-frappe, catppuccin-macchiato, catppuccin-mocha
- Map all 9 base roles to Catppuccin palette colors per flavor
- Map all 7 extended roles to flavor-appropriate dim/surface/border variants
- Snapshot tests: render a canonical status-line through each flavor, assert expected bytes
- Palette-sync CI check: detect upstream Catppuccin palette changes

Acceptance: `theme = "catppuccin-mocha"` in config.toml renders with the Mocha palette; 4 flavors all recognized; snapshot tests lock the output per flavor.
close_reason: Catppuccin flavors (Latte/Frappé/Macchiato/Mocha) shipped against the lsm-7kn theme engine. Palette values sourced from the catppuccin crate (v2) so upstream drift is caught by dep bumps. Role mapping follows ecosystem convention: mauve=Primary, blue=Accent, green/yellow/red/teal=state roles, surface0/surface2 for Surface/Border. Dim variants left unset for Catppuccin's single-shade-per-hue identity. 9 new tests including per-flavor mauve drift alarm with canonical RGB values. 290 lib + 7 integration.

title: Make main.rs run() and check_config() testable via pure inner fn
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) review: main.rs has ~100 lines of orchestration (arg error paths, load/fallback logic, --check-config branches) with zero direct tests. Integration tests hit linesmith::run_* which bypasses main entirely.

Extract pure inner function: fn run_inner(args, stdin, stdout, stderr, env) -> ExitCode. Then main.rs becomes a thin wrapper that reads env + delegates. Tests spawn the inner function with fake IO and assert exit codes + byte output.

Alternative: use assert_cmd / std::process::Command to spawn the built binary against fixture configs. Simpler but slower and less portable.

Closing the gap matters because --check-config's exit codes (0 for ok, 1 for invalid) are the CI/editor-integration contract per docs/specs/config.md:245. Today a regression that flips those codes ships green.
notes: Expanded scope post-Codex review: also threaded stderr through run_with_segments_and_width + layout::render (superseded lsm-v3e), and changed terminal_width to Option<u16> so meta commands don't probe TTY.
close_reason: Extracted cli_main(args, stdin, stdout, stderr, env) -> u8 into lib.rs; main.rs shrinks to a 10-line ExitCode wrapper. 12 new tests lock --check-config exit codes (0 ok / 1 no-path / 1 malformed / 0 missing-explicit), help/version output, bad-arg hint, and CliEnv plumbing (HOME/XDG precedence). Follow-up filed for run_with_segments_and_width stderr plumbing.

title: Warn on unknown keys in config.toml (not just silently ignore)
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) review: spec (docs/specs/config.md §Validation rules §1/§6) says unknown top-level keys should WARN and be ignored, and unknown keys in [segments.<id>] blocks should WARN and be ignored. The current impl silently ignores all unknown keys (no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] anywhere) because deny_unknown_fields rejected spec-valid forward-compat keys like 'theme', '$schema', 'layout'.

Correct fix requires a two-phase parse: first parse into a tolerant struct for backwards/forwards compat, then validate the raw toml::Value tree against a known-key allow-list and emit warnings. That's more work than this slice needed.

User impact today: typos like 'priorty = 10' silently drop instead of warning. Matters more once --check-config becomes a CI gate.
close_reason: Unknown-key warnings via two-phase parse (toml::Value → validate_keys → try_into). Allow-lists: top-level (implemented + spec-documented forward-compat), [layout_options] fields, per-segment schema that tightly gates built-ins while skipping unknown ids so plugins own their own schema. Warnings surface on render stderr and count toward --check-config summary. 17 new tests (281 lib + 7 integration).

title: Multi-line layout: [line.N] sections + layout="multi-line"
description:
Support multi-line status lines per docs/specs/config.md §Multi-line layouts.

Config shape:
- layout = "multi-line" at top level
- [line.1] segments = [...]
- [line.2] segments = [...]
Each line runs the layout algorithm independently, emits its own newline-terminated string.

Edge cases (from spec edge-case table):
- layout = "multi-line" with no [line.N] sections → treat as single-line, warn
- layout = "single-line" with [line.N] sections present → info log, use [line] for rendering
- [line] AND [line.N] both present → document precedence

Depends on lsm-u8u (config parser) and lsm-aql (layout engine — already shipped).
close_reason: Multi-line layout: top-level layout = "single-line" | "multi-line" selector + [line.N] numbered sub-tables. Each line independently runs the layout engine with the full terminal width. New build_lines + run_lines_with_context entry points; build_segments stays for single-line embedders with a fallback to line 1 + warning when called against a multi-line config. power-user preset converted to two-line layout. Edge cases all warn-and-recover: missing layout key auto-promotes when [line].segments is empty, unknown scalar siblings under [line] honor the forward-compat contract, non-numeric numbered keys drop, integer keys sort numerically (so [line.10] follows [line.2]). Cross-line plugin reuse v0.1-limited with specific 'rendered on an earlier line' diagnostic. Spec docs/specs/config.md updated to v0.1.4. Three follow-ups filed: lsm-4yjs (Arc-shared CompiledPlugin for cross-line plugin reuse, v0.2+), plus the prior lsm-w0kx and lsm-9ll1 from the earlier review cycles still apply.

title: Color policy: --no-color / --force-color + NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR + [layout_options]
description:
Wire color emission through CLI flags, env vars, and config.

**Precedence (first match wins):**
1. `--no-color` or `--force-color` CLI flag
2. `NO_COLOR` env var (per no-color.org, any non-empty value)
3. `FORCE_COLOR` env var (any non-empty value)
4. `[layout_options].color = "auto"|"always"|"never"` in config
5. Default "auto" (TTY detection via supports-color)

**Also in this slice:**
- `[layout_options].claude_padding` — factored into width calc before handing to layout

**Out of scope (filed as follow-up):**
- `[layout_options].separator` styles (`powerline`, `capsule`, `flex`). Powerline needs Nerd Font glyph emission and affects layout-engine width math; capsule + flex are v0.2+ per spec. Separate bead.

Depends on lsm-u8u (config parser) and lsm-7kn (theme system — both shipped).
close_reason: Color policy precedence chain (CLI --no-color/--force-color > NO_COLOR env > FORCE_COLOR env > [layout_options].color > auto) + claude_padding width calc. FORCE_COLOR parses 0/false/off as 'absent' per npm/chalk convention. ColorPolicy, ColorOverride, LayoutOptions marked #[non_exhaustive]; LayoutOptions fields flattened (no redundant Option wrappers). 18 new tests (262 lib + 7 integration). Separator styles filed as lsm-1my (powerline needs Nerd Font emission; out of scope here).

title: Publish config.schema.json via schemars + CI drift check
description:
Derive a JSON Schema from the config.toml Rust types using schemars; commit config.schema.json at the repo root and embed via include_str! for offline editor integrations. CI fails when the committed schema is stale relative to the types (regenerate-and-diff check).

Editor integrations (taplo, VS Code, Zed) pick up the schema via the '$schema' key in the user's config, written by 'linesmith init' and 'linesmith presets apply'.

Depends on lsm-u8u (for the Config types to derive from). Dep: schemars.
close_reason: Published config.schema.json at repo root via schemars 1.x. Generator: dedicated gen-config-schema bin printing to stdout. Mise tasks schema:update / schema:check (both atomic via tempfile + set -e); CI drift step in static-analysis. linesmith init + presets apply prepend #:schema URL directive to written configs; URL pinned to env!(CARGO_PKG_VERSION) tag form. Closed-shape structs (Config, LayoutOptions, WidthBoundsConfig) get additionalProperties: false in the schema via schemars(extend(...)) without breaking serde's permissive runtime. Forward-compat top-level keys (preset, plugins, \) now real Config fields with JsonSchema; plugins typed as BTreeMap<String, toml::Value> so non-table values fail at parse. Tests: schema validity (round-trip + property keys present), TOML round-trip of wrapped body (separator + position pinned), forward-compat field deserialization. Spec docs/specs/config.md JSON Schema section rewritten. .prettierignore excludes generated schema. Follow-ups: lsm-xru2 (A→C hybrid + release-pipeline schema commit), lsm-qs9e (per-segment + [line.N] sub-schemas, Codex round-7 P2), lsm-eao3 (schemastore.org submission).

title: linesmith presets list + presets apply + 5 embedded presets
description:
Part A of the original lsm-kb6 split (Part B = lsm-5yd for 'linesmith init' interactive onboarding).

**Scope:**
- 'linesmith presets list' — prints embedded preset names, one per line, in stable order
- 'linesmith presets apply <name>' — writes the preset's TOML body to the resolved config path:
  - If file exists: prompt 'overwrite config.toml? [y/N]' on stderr; on yes, back up existing as config.toml.bak (overwrite prior .bak if present); on no, abort with exit 1
  - '--force' flag skips prompt; still writes backup
  - If name is unknown: fail fast listing valid names, exit non-zero
  - Create parent directories as needed (0755)
- Unknown subcommand under 'presets' → clear error per the existing 'themes' dispatch pattern in cli.rs
- 5 embedded presets (include_str!) per docs/specs/config.md §Presets:
  - minimal: model + context_window
  - developer: model + workspace + git + context_window + cost + rate_limit_5h + rate_limit_7d
  - power-user: everything v0.1 supports (defer multi-line to lsm-bvu)
  - cost-focused: model + context_window + cost + rate_limit_5h + rate_limit_7d
  - worktree-heavy: model + workspace + git + context_window
  - (Note: git_branch segment isn't built yet — include TODO comment in affected presets; filed separately if needed)
- Tests:
  - Every embedded preset parses via Config::from_str without warnings
  - Every embedded preset produces a non-empty segment list via build_segments
  - 'presets list' prints all 5 names
  - 'presets apply <name>' to a temp path writes expected bytes; with existing file creates .bak
  - Unknown preset name errors with list
  - --force skips prompt (driver-level test with stdin closed)

**Depends on:** lsm-u8u (config core, already done — parser + registry + XDG resolver)

**Acceptance:** 'linesmith presets list' prints the 5 names. 'linesmith presets apply developer' writes a valid config.toml to the XDG path. Re-running with file present prompts, backs up to .bak, and writes new content on confirm. '--force' skips prompt. Resulting config round-trips through Config::from_str and produces the expected segment list.
close_reason: Presets list/apply subcommands + 5 embedded TOMLs (minimal, developer, power-user, cost-focused, worktree-heavy). --force confirms overwrite skip; existing .bak refused unless --force (Windows-safe pre-remove). --config threads through to the target path. Prompt + backup notifications on stderr, only final success on stdout. Two follow-ups filed (lsm-rd7 broken-pipe exit code, lsm-9j7 rename permission test).

title: Truncate highest-priority segment before dropping under width pressure
description:
From slice-4 Codex review: the layout engine drops segments whole once total_width exceeds terminal_width, even when a single over-wide segment (e.g. a long workspace name) could be truncated to fit. Result: `linesmith/very-long-feature-branch-name` on a 30-40 col terminal disappears rather than showing a truncated location.

Current design: width.max is an absolute cap applied in collect_items, unconditional on terminal width. That helps when a segment is pathologically wide but doesn't address "terminal is narrower than natural segment width."

Proposed: before dropping the currently-selected-to-drop segment, attempt to truncate it to (segment_width - (total_width - terminal_width)) cells. Only drop when truncation fails (e.g. resulting width below width.min, or segment has no truncatable text).

Requires spec update to docs/specs/segment-system.md §Layout algorithm. Likely needs a per-segment "truncatable: bool" or "min_useful_width" hint so segments like model/cost that shouldn't truncate opt out.

Once this lands, revisit whether built-in segments (workspace especially) should declare width.max at all — they may not need to.
notes:
Final state (post-commit drift fix): only `workspace` opted in. `git_branch` reverted after Codex review caught that generic right-edge end-ellipsis truncation cuts dirty/ahead-behind markers (e.g. `feat/long * ↑…`); structured-tail segments need a segment-aware fallback instead, tracked as lsm-z0ai once lsm-xdyp lands.

Follow-ups (7 total):
- lsm-byrv: expose `truncatable` via `[segments.<id>]` TOML override
- lsm-vla9: revisit `width.max` declarations on built-ins after reflow
- lsm-xdyp: `RenderContext` plumbing into `Segment::render` (foundation for dynamic segments)
- lsm-1no9: `context_bar` width-aware fallback (consumer of lsm-xdyp)
- lsm-rkxh: `model` width-aware compaction (consumer of lsm-xdyp)
- lsm-z0ai: `git_branch` segment-aware fallback (consumer of lsm-xdyp)
- lsm-s2yk: `TruncationPolicy` enum + type-level floor on `SegmentDefaults`
close_reason: Layout reflow pass: SegmentDefaults.truncatable opt-in lets prose-like segments (workspace, git_branch) shrink to (cur_width - overflow) cells with floor max(width.min, 2) before the engine drops them under width pressure. Spec §Layout algorithm updated; 6 new tests cover happy path, floor enforcement, drop-on-too-tight, multi-pass loop, priority-zero immunity. Two follow-ups filed: lsm-byrv (TOML override), lsm-vla9 (revisit width.max on built-ins).

title: Consider Segment::render -> Result<Option<RenderedSegment>, SegmentError>
description: From slice-4 type-design review: current Segment::render returns Option<RenderedSegment> where None means 'hide.' A plugin that fails to render (rhai error, missing field, arithmetic overflow) has no distinct signal — it vanishes indistinguishably from intentional hiding. Evaluate changing the trait to return Result so runtime errors propagate separately. This is a breaking change the moment a real plugin implements the trait, so decide before the plugin slice ships.
close_reason: Shipped in b36a638: Segment::render returns RenderResult = Result<Option<RenderedSegment>, SegmentError>; errors log to stderr and hide. 135 tests green.

title: Lock down RenderedSegment and SegmentDefaults public fields before plugin API
description: From slice-4 type-design review: RenderedSegment has pub text/width/right_separator; the invariant width == text_width(text) is load-bearing but only enforced at construction. Mutating .text silently desyncs width. Same concern on SegmentDefaults's pub fields — currently no builder beyond with_priority so plugin authors needing to set width/default_separator must use struct literal, blocked by #[non_exhaustive]. Options: make fields pub(crate) + add accessors, or add with_width/with_default_separator chainable builders. Decide before plugin runtime ships.
close_reason: Shipped in 3388b2a: RenderedSegment fields pub(crate) with getters, SegmentDefaults gains with_width/with_default_separator chainable builders.

title: Strip control characters from segment output to prevent terminal injection
description: From slice-4 silent-failure review: segment text can contain control chars (ESC, bell, etc.) which `UnicodeWidthChar::width` reports as 0 cells but are pushed into output verbatim. A malicious project dir at `~/work/evil\x1b[2J/` could blank the user terminal on every statusline render. Strip or escape control characters in RenderedSegment::new and/or text_width.
close_reason: Strip char::is_control() chars in RenderedSegment::new and with_separator. Fast no-alloc path when text is clean. Integration-level tests lock hostile project_dir and worktree name cases against regression.

title: Slice 5: File-based cache layer
description: Implement cache layer per docs/specs/segment-system.md. CachePolicy enum: AlwaysFresh, Ttl(Duration), Invalidated{any_of: Vec<CacheInvalidator>, ttl: Option<Duration>}. CacheInvalidator variants: FileChanged(PathBuf) via mtime, ContextFieldChanged(&'static str) via hash, SessionChanged. Storage: one file per segment under XDG_CACHE_HOME/linesmith/ with atomic temp-rename writes. Unlocks rate-limit scraping without blowing the <20ms budget.

title: Slice 3b: Tool detection heuristic + per-tool normalizer split
description: Split the inline claude module in input.rs into crates/linesmith/src/input/normalizers/{mod.rs,claude.rs,qwen.rs,other.rs}. Implement heuristic detection per input-schema.md (QwenCode if 'version' field present; ClaudeCode if 'cost.total_api_duration_ms' present; default ClaudeCode). Also lands the path_tail two-arg refactor from lsm-coc since the split multiplies the footgun.

title: Slice 3: CostMetrics + cost segment
description: Add CostMetrics{total_cost_usd: f64, total_duration_ms, total_api_duration_ms, total_lines_added, total_lines_removed} to StatusContext per ADR-0008. Implement cost segment rendering '$X.XX' using host-side format_cost_usd helper (per plugin-api.md contract). Claude normalizer maps 'cost' JSON object.
close_reason: Closed

title: Slice 3: Effort segment
description: Add EffortLevel enum (Low/Medium/High/Max/XHigh) parsed from 'effort' field. Implement effort segment that renders the current /effort level when present. Claude Code doesn't emit this live today (per docs/research/user-demand.md ccstatusline#239) so the segment will be hidden in practice until Claude Code ships the re-emit; document this explicitly in the segment's doc comment.
close_reason: Closed

title: Address Codex review: spec contract inconsistencies
description: 3 P2 inconsistencies: (1) format_cost_usd takes cents but ctx.cost.total_cost_usd is f64 dollars; (2) config.md visible_if uses nil but plugin-api says () is the sentinel; (3) plugin discovery precedence contradicts between plugin-api.md (plugin_dirs first) and config.md open question (default first).
close_reason: Codex review feedback applied: (1) format_cost_usd now documented as taking f64 dollars (matching ctx.cost.total_cost_usd), not cents; format_duration/format_tokens/format_countdown_until types also made explicit. (2) config.md visible_if example uses () (rhai unit) instead of nil, matching plugin-api.md's documented sentinel. (3) Plugin discovery precedence unified: plugin_dirs scanned first (project-local wins), default XDG scanned last. Documented in both the top-level config.toml example and as a resolved Open Question. Lint + format clean on 29 files.

title: Add docs/research/README.md index
description: Write docs/research/README.md with a date-sorted table of all research docs + one-line summaries. Cross-link from docs/README.md's Folders section so discoverability is one hop.
close_reason: Wrote docs/research/README.md with date-sorted table of all 5 research docs + one-line summaries and conventions section. Cross-linked from docs/README.md Folders table. Prettier + markdownlint clean.

title: Add docs workflow + source-of-truth callout to AGENTS.md
description: AGENTS.md has a Pipeline diagram and pointer to docs/README.md but lacks operational docs workflow (when to write which doc type, mechanics of copying template + numbering, promotion flow, ADR immutability). Also needs explicit callout that AGENTS.md is the source of truth and CLAUDE.md imports via @AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Added (1) source-of-truth callout at top of AGENTS.md explicitly stating AGENTS.md is the canonical file and CLAUDE.md only imports it, and (2) Docs Workflow section covering when to write each doc type (table), mechanics (template + numbering + cross-linking), promotion flow (idea→ADR→spec→beads), and ADR immutability rule. Prettier + markdownlint pass clean.

title: Consolidate CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md to single source of truth
description: Currently bd init created both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with duplicate content. Goal: one source of truth with @import. Approach to evaluate: make AGENTS.md the source of truth (tool-agnostic convention) and have CLAUDE.md just @import it. Complication: bd auto-maintains a BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION block inside CLAUDE.md — need to confirm whether bd can be pointed at AGENTS.md instead, or if we keep the bd block in CLAUDE.md and import the rest from AGENTS.md. Defer until after docs/ backfill complete.
close_reason: Consolidated: AGENTS.md is source of truth with project content (pipeline, tooling, non-interactive shell, architecture, task tracking, rules, commits, session completion). CLAUDE.md reduced to @AGENTS.md import. Removed bd auto-injection markers — bd does not re-inject on bd stats/remember/forget (likely because core.hooksPath was unset for lefthook, so bd hooks don't trigger refresh). If bd ever re-injects, run 'bd init --agents-file AGENTS.md' to redirect.

title: Theme picker: reload-on-save user theme files mid-session
description: Today the picker snapshots the ThemeRegistry at boot via Model.theme_registry. Adding or editing a TOML in ~/.config/linesmith/themes/ requires quitting and reopening to see it. The richer UX is mid-session reload: file-watcher (notify) on the user themes dir, debounced, that rebuilds the registry and refreshes the picker's themes vec on the next render. Implementation needs (1) a notify watcher set up at boot, (2) channel/event wiring through the event loop, (3) registry rebuild that preserves picker cursor across the swap when possible, (4) tests covering add / modify / delete, (5) decision on whether to invalidate any cached preview output. Flagged on lsm-herx.22 — the original spec mentioned reload-on-save semantics but v0.1 shipped the simpler boot-time snapshot.

title: Theme picker: per-row inline mini-previews
description: The theme picker today renders each row as theme.name() + a cursor-only 'press Enter' hint. The cursor-driven global preview at the top swaps theme on Up/Down so the user can see each theme's effect, but they walk through entries serially. The richer UX is per-row inline mini-previews — each row shows a miniature rendered statusline at that theme so the user can compare themes at a glance. Implementation requires (1) per-theme segment rendering for every visible row (cap to visible-window only), (2) new picker view shape since ListScreenView only supports label + description, (3) layout decisions on truncation, color budget per row, and scroll behavior, (4) tests for rendering correctness and performance budget. Flagged by Codex round-4 as a feature-completeness gap on lsm-herx.21.

title: Theme picker live-preview test: render via TestBackend instead of mirroring app::view's match arm
description: The current test `theme_picker_preview_override_uses_cursor_theme_not_committed_theme` (in app.rs) re-implements the same `match &m.screen { ThemePicker(state) => state.cursor_theme(), _ => m.theme.name() }` selector inline as the production view path. A regression that drops the match arm in app::view would still pass this test because the test fabricates the correct value locally. Render via `ratatui::backend::TestBackend`, draw the frame, and assert SGR bytes (or Buffer cells) reflect the cursor's theme color rather than the committed theme's. Flagged by pr-test-analyzer (round 2, severity 7) on the herx.21/.22 review pass.

title: Epic: linesmith config TUI v0.2 — ccstatusline parity continuation
description:
Continuation of lsm-herx for v0.2 parity scope. The v0.1 MVP shipped under herx (items editor, LinePicker, live preview, save, theme picker, install screen, environment warnings, snapshot tests). This epic tracks the post-MVP ccstatusline-parity work that didn't make the v0.1 cut.

Scope groups:

- **PropertyScreen + per-segment editing** — PropertyScreen reusable widget (P2 foundation), 5 editor templates (format-enum / threshold / boolean+string / composite / plugin-free-text), 5 wiring beads pairing each segment family with its template, Global Overrides screen.
- **Color editor** — single-screen, row-IS-preview, all segments at once.
- **Terminal + engine knobs** — Terminal Options screen (Color Level + Terminal Width sub-screen), Inherit Colors / Minimalist Mode / Global Bold knobs.
- **Powerline Setup + Nerd Font detection** — discovery wiring + screen.
- **Per-line config + free-text format-template editor** — multi-line color overrides, format string editor with live validation.
- **TUI polish** — self-demonstrating controls (color swatches, theme mini-previews).

Reference architecture and ADR pointers carry over from lsm-herx (ratatui-for-tui-runtime + tui-screen-state-machine + ADR-0024 per-boundary separator TOML).

title: LinePicker: full driver-level chain round-trip test
description: Per pr-test-analyzer review of lsm-herx.7 (round 2). enter_carries_picker_state_so_esc_back_nav_returns_to_picker pins one hop (Picker -> Editor's prev = LinePicker). The full chain MainMenu -> LinePicker -> ItemsEditor -> Esc -> LinePicker -> Esc -> MainMenu, with cursor preservation at every level, is not asserted as one driver-level test (cursor_preserved_across_activate_esc_activate_round_trip in main_menu.rs covers the MainMenu side; an analog for the three-deep chain would catch a regression that resets the picker cursor when its prev-MainMenu fires mem::take). Add a test using app::update + Event::Key transitions.
notes: Surfacing review: pr-test-analyzer (lsm-herx.7 PR review round 2).

title: Doctor: include array index in malformed-line warnings
description: Per silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-herx.7 (round 2). The KindlessTable and WrongShape variants in check_config_segments emit warnings naming the array (e.g. '[line.1].segments has an inline-table entry without a type field') but not the offending entry index. For a 5-entry array with one buried integer, the user re-reads the whole array. Add the index: '[line.{key}].segments[{idx}] is neither a string nor an inline table'. One enumerate() call. Apply to both classified-entry warns in doctor::check_config_segments.
notes: Surfacing review: silent-failure-hunter (lsm-herx.7 PR review round 2).

title: LineKey numbered-key resolution: extract single helper
description: Per type-design-analyzer review of lsm-herx.7 (round 2). LineKey::Numbered(NonZeroU32) requires walking the [line] table to match by parsed u32 (zero-padded  support per ADR-0024). Today four sites duplicate the same 4-line filter chain: items_editor::numbered_line_key, line_picker::line_entry_counts, line_picker::add_empty_line_outcome's duplicate check, line_picker::delete_line. Extract a single fn find_numbered_key(table: &Table, n: NonZeroU32) -> Option<&str> and route all four through it. Collapses ~30 lines of duplication, keeps LineKey: Copy (no String cascade), and gives the typed-handle ADR follow-up a clean swap point.
notes: Surfacing review: type-design-analyzer (lsm-herx.7 PR review round 2).

title: ItemsEditorPrev: drop Default impl, use explicit mem::replace at call sites
description: Per type-design-analyzer review of lsm-herx.7 (round 2). ItemsEditorPrev's Default goes to MainMenu(MainMenuState::default()), which is a value-level lie: it claims MainMenu is the safe placeholder for unknown prev, defeating the variant's purpose of distinguishing single-line vs multi-line callers. Today's single call site (back_nav_to_prev) take-and-dispatches in one expression so this is theoretical; a future caller that mem::takes prev for some other reason and forgets to restore silently nukes the LinePicker round-trip with no compile-time signal. Drop the Default impl and use mem::replace(&mut state.prev, ItemsEditorPrev::MainMenu(...)) at the single call site with a comment naming the placeholder choice.
notes: Surfacing review: type-design-analyzer (lsm-herx.7 PR review round 2).

title: Doctor: warn on duplicate-by-value numeric [line.N] keys
description: Per Codex review of lsm-herx.7 (post-fix iteration). A hand-edited config can carry both [line.1] and [line.01]; both parse to NonZeroU32(1). The renderer sees two distinct sub-tables and produces two segment lists for line 1 (BTreeMap iteration order). The TUI picker dedups for usability (only one row shows), and lookups target the first parsed-numeric match. This means the shadow line stays in the document, accumulates non-editing diffs, but is silently inaccessible. Doctor should detect this case (multiple [line.N] keys parsing to the same u32) and surface a malformed-line warning so the user knows to delete the duplicate.
notes: Surfacing review: codex (lsm-herx.7 PR review iteration 4). The dedup in line_picker::numbered_lines is the editor-side workaround; doctor should be the diagnostic surface.

title: Items editor: render-output integration tests for merge-flag adjacency
description: Per pr-test-analyzer review of lsm-herx.7. The new TUI tests pin toml_edit shape (the array structure after Space/m verbs) but not what the renderer actually produces. The merge flag's interaction with the renderer's adjacency-prune pass — particularly when a merging segment drops under width pressure — is not directly tested at the render-output level. Add 1-2 tests using crate::layout::render_with_warn that build a Vec<LineItem> from a config with merge=true and assert the rendered string shape (e.g., 'merged segment + dropped neighbor' produces the expected width).
notes: Surfacing review: pr-test-analyzer (lsm-herx.7 PR review). The pattern exists in builder/tests.rs near line 435 (RawSeg helpers).

title: InsertTarget: collapse Before/After to InsertAt(usize)
description: Per type-design-analyzer review of lsm-herx.7. InsertTarget::Before(usize) | After(usize) — every consumer destructures to a single resolved usize. The Before/After distinction does no useful work after picker selection; the items-editor screen could pre-compute the insert position (cursor for i, cursor+1 for a, 0 for Space-on-empty, cursor+1 for Space-on-non-empty) and pass a single InsertAt(usize) to the picker. Cleaner type, fewer destructures, and the saturating clamp in insert_segment/insert_separator already handles out-of-range values gracefully.
notes: Surfacing review: type-design-analyzer (lsm-herx.7 PR review).

title: extract_line_segments: targeted regression tests for shape errors
description: Per silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-herx.7. extract_line_segments uses toml::Value::try_into::<LineEntryItem>() as a catch-all that swallows every shape mismatch with a generic 'inline table didn't parse ({e})'. The error display IS useful today, but a future serde upgrade or LineEntryItem field rename could degrade it silently. Add regression tests pinning the exact warn text shape for { type = 42 }, { merge = "yes" }, { character = 7 } so CI catches degradation.
notes: Surfacing review: silent-failure-hunter (lsm-herx.7 PR review).

title: LinePicker: structured AddLineError for distinguishable warnings
description: Per silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-herx.7. add_empty_line returns bool, conflating two failure modes: (1) [line] is a non-table (rare, hand-edited config), and (2) line N already exists (hits saturation when last is u32::MAX). The single 'could not add [line.N]; document not editable' warn message is wrong for case (2) — the document IS editable, line numbers are exhausted. Replace bool with Result<(), AddLineError> and emit distinct warns per variant ('NonTable: document [line] is a non-table' vs 'Duplicate: line numbers exhausted').
notes: Surfacing review: silent-failure-hunter (lsm-herx.7 PR review).

title: Validator pass for [line].segments inline-table entries
description: Per ADR-0024 + comment-analyzer review of lsm-herx.7. The existing validate_keys pass in linesmith-core walks top-level / [layout_options] / [segments.<id>] shapes only — it does NOT descend into [line].segments array entries. A typo'd inline-table key like { tpye = "separator" } silently lands in LineEntryItem.extra and only surfaces at builder time as a generic 'kindless inline table' warning rather than a per-key 'unknown key tpye in line entry' diagnostic. Extend validate_keys to walk each LineEntry::Item entry under [line].segments and [line.N].segments, warning on keys outside the typed set + character/merge appropriateness rules.
notes: Mentioned in ADR-0024 §Decision Outcome (Bad bullet) and the LineEntry doc-comment as deferred. Surfacing review: comment-analyzer (lsm-herx.7 PR review).

title: Items editor: typed-handle/wire-shape split for LineEntry
description: Per type-design-analyzer review of lsm-herx.7. Today LineEntry is an untagged enum directly deserialized from TOML, with LineEntryItem.kind: Option<String> permitting illegal post-parse states (kindless inline tables, merge-on-separator). The validator + builder warn-and-drop these at use sites. Cleaner: keep a private RawLineEntry for serde (current shape), expose a public LineEntry with exhaustive variants (Segment { id, merge, extra } | Separator { character, extra } | Malformed { extra }), normalizing illegal states at construct time. Also collapses tui::items_editor::EntryKind + linesmith_core::config::LineEntry::kind() into one canonical classifier. Substantial refactor — multiple call sites in builder/dispatch.rs, items_editor.rs, line_picker.rs.
notes: Surfacing review: type-design-analyzer (lsm-herx.7 PR review). Captures the typed-handle vs wire-shape pattern. Apply only when a v0.2 feature (per-instance config, color overrides) actually makes the loose typing painful.

title: Items editor type picker: source candidates from PluginRegistry, not just built-ins
description:
The Phase 4 type picker (lsm-herx.7) hard-codes BUILT_IN_SEGMENT_IDS as its candidate set. Plugin-backed configurations lose the ability to add/insert plugin segments through the UI:

- After 'c' clear, plugin IDs disappear from the document and become un-recoverable through the picker.
- Plugin IDs the user has never used can't be added at all.

Full fix requires plumbing PluginRegistry through tui::run → Model → TypePickerState. Today the TUI's preview path (preview::render_lines) doesn't take a plugin registry — needs design work for:
- Where the registry lives (Model field? Lazy-loaded?).
- When it's rebuilt (boot? On config.plugin_dirs change?).
- Lifetime story: candidates need to be owned strings (Vec<String>) rather than &'static, since plugin IDs aren't static.

Possible partial fix as an intermediate step: scan the document for plugin IDs already in any segments array, union with BUILT_IN_SEGMENT_IDS. Doesn't cover 'add a plugin you've never used' or 'recreate a cleared plugin segment', but covers the 'reorder/duplicate existing plugin entries' subset.

Filed during lsm-herx.7 Phase 4 codex review (codex P2).

title: Items editor: pin cursor-preservation through Esc back-nav (uncatchable today)
description:
When ItemsEditor is reachable from a non-row-0 menu entry (LinePicker), add a model-level test that walks main_menu cursor to a non-default position, opens ItemsEditor, hits Esc, and asserts the restored MainMenuState carries that cursor.

Currently uncatchable because:
- ItemsEditor only routes from MainMenuItem::EditLines (row 0)
- MainMenuState's list field is private, no public surface for non-default construction
- Round-trip tests can only check cursor==0, which matches MainMenuState::default() — a regression that swaps mem::take for default() would silently pass

Becomes catchable when LinePicker (a separate bead) introduces a non-row-0 entry into the items editor flow, OR when a multi-line config's [line.N] entries become editable through MainMenu.

Filed during lsm-herx.7 Phase 2 review (pr-test-analyzer Critical Gap #1).

title: Extract testable boot-path helper from tui::run
description:
Surfaced by lsm-herx.9 pr-test-analyzer review (finding 6).

`crates/linesmith/src/tui/mod.rs::run` is dominated by terminal I/O and not unit-testable in isolation. Extract a mid-level helper that returns the constructed `Model` + parse warnings without entering the alt-screen:

```rust
fn build_model(
    config_path: Option<&Path>,
    stderr: &mut dyn Write,
) -> io::Result<(Model, Option<String>)>;
```

Lets us assert end-to-end:
- Load a malformed TOML, observe `save_target` is `None`
- Trigger Ctrl+S through `update`, observe `apply_save` fires NoTarget warn through the captured sink
- Round-trip a clean parse → mutate document → save → reload → verify the bytes match

Today we get partial coverage via `Model::save`'s direct tests + `load_config`'s direct tests, but the integration between them isn't pinned. A future refactor could break the wiring without any test failing.

Defer until items editor lands so the integration becomes load-bearing.

title: Transient save-status footer for visible Ctrl+S feedback
description:
Surfaced by lsm-herx.9 silent-failure-hunter review (finding 5).

At default `LINESMITH_LOG=warn`, both `SaveOutcome::Saved` (`lsm_debug!`) and `SaveOutcome::Clean` (silent) produce zero visible feedback. The user can't distinguish three states with very different next actions:
- Saved successfully
- Nothing to save (no edits)
- Ctrl+S didn't register (modal ate it, terminal swallowed Ctrl, etc.)

A user retries, sees nothing, and either force-quits (potentially losing edits if the dirty bit was wrongly clean) or assumes save is broken.

Add a transient status footer that surfaces 'saved /path/foo.toml' or 'no changes to save' for ~1s after Ctrl+S, then fades. Doesn't pollute the warnings panel (which is for diagnostic / error output) but is visible at default verbosity.

Implementation sketch:
- Add `Model.last_action: Option<(Instant, String)>`
- `apply_save` populates it on every outcome
- `render_preview` renders the footer message if `last_action` is recent
- Event loop ticks redraw when the footer's TTL expires

Defer until items editor (lsm-herx.7) lands and the user actually has something to save.

title: atomic_write parent-dir sync_all + permission hardening
description:
Surfaced by lsm-herx.9 silent-failure-hunter review (findings 4 + 11).

Two crash-durability + permissions hardening tasks for `crates/linesmith/src/tui/mod.rs::atomic_write`:

1. **Sync the parent directory after rename.** `sync_all()` on the temp file flushes its data + metadata, but `tempfile::persist` doesn't fsync the directory entry. On a hard crash between persist and the next directory-fsync, the rename can be lost on ext4 with `data=writeback` or older XFS configs (the classic 'rename-but-don't-fsync-the-directory' hole). The function name says 'atomic' and crash-durability is part of that contract for many users. Open the parent dir + sync_all after persist returns.

2. **`create_dir_all` uses default umask.** When the user's first save creates `~/.config/linesmith/`, the new subdir gets default umask permissions (typically 0755). On a system where the user's `~/.config` is 0700, the new subdir is more permissive than its parent — silent visibility widening. linesmith config can contain auth tokens for plugins (per spec roadmap); silently widening visibility to other users on multi-user hosts is a real leak. At minimum: emit `lsm_debug!('created directory {parent}')` so the action is auditable. Better: `DirBuilder::mode(0o700)` on Unix when creating a new config root.

Defer until v0.2; bounded relevance (hard-crash window for #1, multi-user hosts for #2).

title: linesmith-plugin eprintln! fallback bypasses LogSink
description:
Surfaced by lsm-wyph code-reviewer review.

`crates/linesmith-plugin/src/engine.rs` (around the warn-emitter install) falls back to `eprintln!("linesmith [warn] {msg}")` when no host emitter is installed. The fallback bypasses the new `LogSink` machinery and writes raw to stderr — exactly the failure mode lsm-wyph is meant to prevent for the alt-screen.

Currently inert: `linesmith-core::plugins::build_engine` always installs a host emitter that routes through `crate::logging::emit` (the LogSink path), and `tests/log_bridge.rs` pins the install. Any future entry point that builds a plugin engine WITHOUT going through `linesmith-core::plugins::build_engine` would re-open the hole.

Fix options:
- Move the fallback into linesmith-core where it can use the LogSink path directly
- Make `build_engine` mandatory by sealing or removing the public construction path in linesmith-plugin
- Add a clippy disallowed_method lint forbidding direct `eprintln!` outside the logging facade

Relevant code: crates/linesmith-plugin/src/engine.rs (emit_warn fallback).

title: Preview pane: many-line height affordance and plugin-segment indicator
description:
Surfaced by review of lsm-herx.8. Two related v0.2 polish items deferred from the v0.1 preview implementation.

1. Many-line height truncation has no affordance. The preview cap is 16 rows total (2 borders + ~14 content), so a config with 14+ lines silently loses lines. Add a '+N more' indicator on the last visible row, or make the preview pane scrollable.

2. Plugin segments hide silently. The preview passes plugins = None to keep the editor independent of the rhai runtime, so segments configured to run plugin scripts produce 'unknown segment id' warnings. The warning surfaces in the warnings panel below the preview body (see lsm-herx.8), but the preview line itself doesn't show where the plugin segment WOULD render. Two options:
   - Render a placeholder chip ('[plugin: <id>]') in dim italic at the segment's position so users see their layout.
   - Build with plugins enabled in the TUI (heavier; means TUI carries the rhai runtime).

Both are deferred until v0.2 — the v0.1 preview shows a complete picture for built-in segments, which is the dominant case.

title: Screen-stack architecture for back-navigation across depth-2+
description:
Surfaced by type-design review of lsm-herx.6 Main Menu work. Should be settled before the second sub-screen depth lands.

Today, back-navigation works because PlaceholderState carries prev: MainMenuState. Each Placeholder remembers exactly its parent. This works for the v0.1 two-level tree (Main Menu → Placeholder, Esc returns).

The pattern doesn't generalize past depth 2:

- If EditLines opens ColorEditor opens ThemePicker, each intermediate screen has to box the previous, doubling memory.
- Each child screen ties itself to a specific parent type. ThemePicker can't be opened from both EditColors AND from a hypothetical PluginConfig screen without becoming generic over a parent enum.
- ADR-0016's 'small ceremony cost per screen-to-screen handoff' is exactly this cost made concrete.

Options to consider:

1. Vec<AppScreen> stack on Model. Any screen pops without knowing its parent. Esc on a non-root screen pops; Esc on the root quits. Cleanest semantics, well-trodden TUI pattern. Needs care around the 'screen owns its state' principle — popping discards state by default; an explicit save would need to lift state to the stack frame.

2. Parent-pointer in each screen's state struct, generic over AppScreen. More uniform than today's MainMenuState-specific prev, but the generic-over-enum shape is verbose in Rust and causes Box dependencies.

3. Defer entirely until a third screen depth actually lands. v0.1 only adds Main Menu + Placeholder + (eventually) Items Editor — none nest. Risk: if v0.2 adds a sub-screen of EditLines, the cleanup is done under deadline pressure.

Recommend (1) — the stack model matches user mental models (Esc = back) without coupling sibling screens.

Blocks: any bead that introduces a screen reachable through more than one parent (most likely lsm-herx.21 ThemePicker or lsm-herx.20 ColorEditor).

title: ListScreen render defense tests: long labels, unicode width, multi-verb separator
description:
Render-side hardening tests for the lsm-herx.4 ListScreen widget. The contract is pinned by 32 unit + smoke tests today; these are edge-case defenses for render scenarios the contract doesn't speak to but that real users will hit.

1. Long label: a label whose width exceeds the available column count must render without panicking. ratatui's List truncates by default — pin that.

2. Unicode width: a 2-cell-wide grapheme (e.g. CJK character or emoji) in a label must render at the correct cell width without breaking the cursor symbol layout. Today's TestBackend dump uses .symbol().chars().next().unwrap_or(' ') which silently swallows multi-codepoint graphemes — a more careful dump is needed.

3. Multi-verb separator: render tests assert dump.contains("a add") but don't pin the · separator between multiple verbs. A regression to , or dropping the separator entirely would still pass. Add a test with verbs = [{a,add}, {d,delete}] asserting dump.contains("a add · d delete").

Lives in crates/linesmith/src/tui/list_screen.rs tests module.

title: Pin the TUI boot-time stderr-before-alt-screen invariant in tests
description:
Test gap surfaced in the lsm-herx.3 review pipeline (pr-test-analyzer round 2, rating 7). Deferred from `.3` because the test requires extracting a prelude helper from `tui::run` — out of scope for the boot-bead.

Today's `tui::run` writes the parse-warning to its `stderr: &mut dyn Write` sink *before* calling `enter_terminal`. That ordering is the actual user-facing invariant of the round-1 silent-failure fix: a malformed config has to be visible to the user before alt-screen takes over the terminal.

Only `load_config`'s output (the warning string) is pinned by tests. The `run` ordering — "warning lands on the buffer before any terminal escape" — is not. A future refactor that reorders `enter_terminal()` ahead of the warning write would regress the invariant silently.

Fix shape: extract `(load_config + warning emit)` from `run` into a small `prepare_boot(stderr, config_path) -> Result<Model, ...>` helper. Test feeds it a malformed-TOML path + a `Vec<u8>` stderr sink, asserts the buffer contains "parse error" + the path basename + "opening with defaults" before any terminal-escape bytes (or just before the function returns at all, since `prepare_boot` doesn't touch the terminal).

Cheap once the helper is extracted; defer until lsm-herx.6 lands and the boot path picks up real preview/init steps that justify the helper for code-quality reasons.

title: TUI event loop: retry on EINTR + recoverable I/O blips instead of aborting
description:
Follow-up from the lsm-herx.3 review pipeline (silent-failure-hunter).

Today, the `linesmith config` event loop in `crates/linesmith/src/tui/mod.rs::run_loop` propagates any `?` failure out as a hard abort:

- `cevent::poll(...)?` — a SIGWINCH-induced EINTR kills the editor.
- `cevent::read()?` — same.
- `terminal.draw(...)?` — a single transient stdout backpressure event aborts the session.

Better behavior: distinguish recoverable from fatal I/O errors. For `poll`/`read`, retry on `ErrorKind::Interrupted`. For `draw`, log + retry once before bailing.

Defer to a follow-up bead because it requires a small wrapper that classifies io::Error kinds and a test seam (mock crossterm? inject errors?) — out of scope for `.3`'s "boot the TUI, prove the placeholder renders" contract.

Triggered by: a real user hitting Ctrl+L (which generates SIGWINCH on some terminals) or backgrounding `linesmith config` and resuming. Without retry, both paths can drop the user out of the editor.

title: OverriddenSegment: add #[non_exhaustive] for SemVer growth
description:
Pre-existing issue surfaced during the lsm-herx.2 type-design review (round 1) but unrelated to that bead's scope.

OverriddenSegment is pub (segments/mod.rs) but lacks #[non_exhaustive], unlike its sibling pub types in the same module (Separator, RenderedSegment, SegmentDefaults, RenderContext, SegmentError, LineItem all carry the attribute).

Either:
(a) Narrow visibility to pub(crate) if embedders aren't expected to construct it directly. Today it's only used inside segments/builder/plugins.rs's apply_override.
(b) Keep pub and add #[non_exhaustive] per ADR-0021 rule 10.

Recommendation: (a) — it's an engine-internal wrapper for [segments.<id>] override application. Narrowing to pub(crate) is the right move for a v0.x scaffolding type with no embedder use case.

Trivial change; verify via cargo check that no out-of-tree consumer breaks (none expected).

title: apply_runtime_separator_overrides: short-circuit when no segment sets a runtime override
description:
Performance follow-up from the lsm-herx.2 review pipeline (code-reviewer rounds 1 + 2).

Today, layout::collect_items_with unconditionally walks the LayoutItem list to apply runtime separator overrides, even when no segment has RenderedSegment::right_separator: Some(_) — the dominant case (no built-in segment uses with_separator).

Fix: short-circuit the loop with a single any() pre-pass:

```rust
if items.iter().any(|it| matches!(it, LayoutItem::Segment(s) if s.rendered.right_separator.is_some())) {
    for i in 0..items.len() { apply_override_at(items, i); }
}
```

OR fold the override read into collect_items_with's main loop by tracking the previous segment's right_separator across iterations.

Before applying: benchmark the bench/render.rs default-config render before/after to confirm the overhead is measurable. The clone is shallow (Cow::Borrowed for Literal, trivial for Space/Theme/None) so the win may be sub-microsecond.

Defer until after benchmarks justify the change.

title: Add edge-case tests for rhai_format_countdown_until
description:
lsm-3912 rewrote rhai_format_countdown_until to use as_second() arithmetic instead of chrono's num_minutes/num_days. The existing test (engine_format_countdown_until_handles_future_timestamp) is shape-only (asserts != "?" && != "now" && !is_empty). Add tests for: (a) sub-minute future → 'now', (b) multi-day future → '5d', (c) round-hour future → '3h' (no '0m' tail).

Pre-req: lsm-3912 landed.

title: is_fresh: log negative cached_at→now duration via lsm_debug
description:
cascade::is_fresh silently treats negative ages (cached_at > now) as 'stale' and returns false, forcing a refetch. Comment claims clock-skew is filtered by CacheStore::read, but resolve_usage takes an injected now() callback so the read-time filter doesn't catch in-call drift. Add lsm_debug! when the negative-age branch fires so misconfigured test clocks or production drift become observable.

Surfaced by silent-failure-hunter during lsm-3912 review (pre-existing parity issue, not a migration regression).

title: Add JSONL timestamp parser strictness pinning tests
description:
The chrono → jiff migration in lsm-3912 made the timestamp parser stricter. jiff Timestamp::FromStr rejects naive datetimes (no Z/offset), leading whitespace, and >9 subsec digits — chrono accepted all three (truncating subseconds). Claude Code transcripts unlikely to emit these shapes, but pinning the rejection contract documents the upstream requirement.

Acceptance: tests in jsonl/tests.rs that assert (a) ms/ns precision parses, (b) naive datetime is rejected, (c) >9 subsec digits is rejected. Reference jiff 0.2 parser semantics.

title: Add nanosecond-precision wire-compat test for chrono-era cache files
description:
The cache_reads_rfc3339_z_suffix_serde_format test (added in lsm-3912) only covers zero-subsec round-trip. Real chrono-era usage.json files carry nanosecond precision (e.g. `2026-04-19T12:00:00.123456789Z`). Add a parallel test that asserts a fixture with non-zero subseconds round-trips correctly under jiff so a future jiff bump that truncates precision fails loudly instead of silently corrupting upgrade-from-chrono caches.

Pre-req: lsm-3912 landed.
Acceptance: new test in crates/linesmith-core/src/data_context/cache.rs asserting cached_at.subsec_nanosecond() and to_string() round-trip on `.123456789Z` input.

title: Migrate chrono → jiff across the workspace
description:
lsm-15xg added `jiff` as a new dep for IANA tz handling on the rate-limit reset segments (jiff reads system /usr/share/zoneinfo/* on Unix → ~0KB tzdata cost vs chrono-tz's ~250-400KB embedded DB). chrono is still used for parsing upstream ISO timestamps and DateTime<Utc> arithmetic in 8+ files. Maintaining two datetime libraries is a workspace-bloat smell and a long-term maintenance tax.

Migration scope (rough order):
- Audit all chrono usages: `grep -rn 'use chrono\|chrono::' crates/` — likely cluster: data_context (cascade, jsonl, fetcher), segments (session_duration, rate_limit/window). Most are DateTime<Utc> + Duration arithmetic and ISO 8601 parsing.
- Add jiff equivalents: chrono::DateTime<Utc> → jiff::Timestamp; chrono::Duration → jiff::SignedDuration; chrono::Utc::now() → Timestamp::now(); ISO parsing via jiff::Timestamp::from_str.
- Drop chrono dep, drop chrono-tz if it ever lands.
- Verify binary size delta (~150KB chrono dropped, ~0KB net since jiff replaces it).

Pre-reqs: lsm-15xg lands first (gets jiff into the workspace and proves the API patterns).

Acceptance: chrono removed from Cargo.toml workspace dependencies; cargo tree shows no chrono in linesmith/linesmith-core/linesmith-plugin; mise run check + test green; binary size ≤ pre-migration.
close_reason: Migrated chrono → jiff across the workspace. 12 files, 29 chrono refs replaced. Type mapping: DateTime<Utc> → jiff::Timestamp, Duration → jiff::SignedDuration, Utc::now() → Timestamp::now(), parse_from_rfc3339 → s.parse::<Timestamp>(), signed_duration_since → duration_since, DurationRound::duration_trunc replaced with custom floor_to_grain / floor_to_hour helpers using as_second() arithmetic, TimeZone::with_ymd_and_hms test fixtures → civil::date(y,m,d).at(...).in_tz('UTC')?.timestamp(). chrono dep removed from workspace + all 3 per-crate Cargo.toml. New cache_reads_rfc3339_z_suffix_serde_format test pins on-disk wire compatibility (chrono-version usage.json files still parse under jiff). On-disk schema unchanged: chrono and jiff both default-serialize as RFC 3339 with Z suffix. Public API path unchanged: external callers still get crate::data_context::CachedUsage, FiveHourBlock, etc. with same shapes. mise run check + 1542 tests + bench all green; binary 4.20MB (was 4.22MB, −16KB net since jiff replaces both chrono and jiff coexistence). Closes the bead filed as a follow-up to lsm-15xg.

title: Add real-bytes regression test for EnvVarState→XdgEnv→resolve_config_path pipeline
description:
Test-coverage follow-up from lsm-0a4e review. The new code path (\`var_os\` → \`CliEnv\`/\`EnvVarState\` → \`nonempty_os()\` → \`XdgEnv\`) is not exercised by any test using actual non-UTF-8 bytes. Existing tests:

- The \`non_utf8_for_test\` helper synthesizes \`raw\` from a UTF-8 \`String\` — round-trip equals UTF-8.
- All \`CliEnv\` tests use \`path.as_os_str().to_owned()\` from \`tempdir()\` paths — UTF-8 in practice.

The only real-bytes coverage lives at \`linesmith-core/src/data_context/xdg.rs:191\` (the \`preserves_non_utf8_xdg_cache_home\` test on \`XdgEnv\` directly), one layer below \`EnvVarState\`.

Add \`#[cfg(unix)]\` regression tests that:

1. Construct \`EnvVarState::NonUtf8 { lossy, raw }\` with \`raw\` from \`std::os::unix::ffi::OsStringExt::from_vec(b"/srv/caf\\xe9-bin".to_vec())\` and assert \`state.nonempty_os().unwrap().as_encoded_bytes()\` retains the \`\\xe9\` byte.
2. Wire that \`EnvVarState\` through to \`runtime_xdg_env\` and \`resolve_config_path\`; assert the resolved \`PathBuf\` ancestor preserves the bytes.
3. (Optional) Construct \`CliEnv\` with \`xdg_config_home: Some(OsString::from_vec(...))\`; pass through \`run_cli\`-style entry; assert the cascade preserves bytes.

Acceptance: doctor's \`runtime_xdg_env\` build, the cache cascade (\`derive_cache_root\`), and the Claude-home snapshot all have at least one real-bytes test.

Driven by silent-failure-hunter + type-design-analyzer findings on lsm-0a4e (2026-05-03).

title: Refactor EnvVarState::NonUtf8 from { lossy, raw } to NonUtf8(OsString)
description:
Type-design follow-up from lsm-0a4e review. Three reviewers (type-design-analyzer, code-reviewer, comment-analyzer) flagged the dual-storage shape as denormalized.

Current shape (post-lsm-0a4e):
\`\`\`
NonUtf8 {
    lossy: String,         // for hint output
    raw: std::ffi::OsString, // for plumbing through OsStr APIs
}
\`\`\`

Issues:
- \`lossy\` is derivable from \`raw\` via \`raw.to_string_lossy().into_owned()\`. Storing both creates a representable-but-illegal state where \`lossy != raw.to_string_lossy()\`.
- The \`non_utf8_for_test\` helper synthesizes \`raw\` from a UTF-8 \`String\` (\`OsString::from(&lossy)\`), so tests against this variant don't exercise true non-UTF-8 byte handling.
- Two field accesses at every match site (\`{ lossy, .. }\` for display, \`{ raw, .. }\` for plumbing) — slightly noisy.

Proposed shape:
\`\`\`
NonUtf8(std::ffi::OsString)
// + a private/public method:
fn lossy(&self) -> std::borrow::Cow<'_, str>
\`\`\`

Eliminates the redundancy. Display sites become \`raw.to_string_lossy()\` (one extra call per warn/fail render in doctor — irrelevant at doctor frequency). The \`non_utf8_for_test\` helper becomes trivial: \`NonUtf8(OsString::from(s))\` with no synthesized invariant.

Acceptance: \`EnvVarState::NonUtf8\` is single-field; \`lossy()\` method on the enum returns the lossy form on demand; all match sites updated; \`non_utf8_for_test\` simplified or replaced; \`mise run check\` green; existing 1036+ tests pass.

Driven by code-review findings on lsm-0a4e (2026-05-03).

title: CI check: linesmith-plugin's inline-duplicated lints stay in sync with [workspace.lints]
description:
ADR-0021 rule 6 mechanizes visibility-ladder enforcement via `[workspace.lints]`. linesmith-plugin can't use `[lints] workspace = true` because it has a per-crate `disallowed_methods = "allow"` carve-out (the plugin crate is the home of the disallowed method). Stable Cargo (1.94 verified) doesn't support per-lint workspace inheritance, so the plugin's Cargo.toml inline-duplicates `[workspace.lints.rust]` + `[workspace.lints.clippy]` then layers the override.

The duplication has a "Keep in sync with the root" comment but no mechanical enforcement. Drift is silent: future workspace lints added to `[workspace.lints]` won't apply to linesmith-plugin unless someone manually mirrors them.

Two options for mechanical enforcement (pick during work):

1. **Shell/CI grep gate.** A small step in CI (or `mise run check`) that diffs the lint set between Cargo.toml's `[workspace.lints.*]` and crates/linesmith-plugin/Cargo.toml's `[lints.*]` (modulo the documented `disallowed_methods = "allow"` carve-out). Cheap, declarative, fails loudly. Example sketch (refine during work):
   ```sh
   diff <(awk '/\[workspace\.lints/,/^$/' Cargo.toml | grep -E '"(forbid|warn|deny|allow)"') \
   ```
