   ```sh
        <(awk '/\[lints/,/^$/' crates/linesmith-plugin/Cargo.toml | grep -E '"(forbid|warn|deny|allow)"' | grep -v disallowed_methods)
   ```
2. **Tiny custom Rust binary.** ~30 LOC reading both manifests via `toml`, asserting set equality (with the carve-out as an explicit allowlist).

Resolves automatically if stable Cargo gains per-lint workspace inheritance — the inline duplication and this CI check both go away.

Acceptance: drift between the two lint blocks is detected before merge; the carve-out documented in the check itself.

Driven by code-reviewer finding on bead lsm-v1ec (2026-05-02 review).

title: #[non_exhaustive] audit pass against ADR-0021 rule 10
description:
ADR-0021 rule 10 narrows \`#[non_exhaustive]\` to: error enums **whose variants you expect to grow**, public config structs with all-pub fields, and other enums expected to grow. Closed-set types fixed by domain don't get the attribute (forces wildcard arms downstream where they're semantically wrong).

This bead audits every \`#[non_exhaustive]\` site in the workspace against the rule:

1. \`grep -rn "non_exhaustive" crates/\` — enumerate all marked types.
2. For each marked type: classify as growth-prone (keep), closed-set-by-domain (drop), or ambiguous (consult the type's domain).
3. \`grep -rn "^pub enum\\|^pub struct" crates/\` — enumerate unmarked public types; flag any that *should* be marked (rare but worth the sweep).

Known starting state (from ADR drafting): \`UsageError\`, \`GitError\`, \`CredentialError\` and their sister types in \`data_context/errors.rs\` are all marked, all growth-prone — these stay. The rate-limit segment configs (\`RateLimit5hSegment\`, etc.) are marked — they're public config structs with all-pub fields and the rule keeps them marked too.

Suspicious candidates (not pre-decided; classify during the audit):
- \`PercentFormat\` / \`DurationFormat\` / \`ExtraUsageFormat\` enums in rate_limit_format.rs — currently marked? probably closed-set
- Any 2-variant enum carrying \`#[non_exhaustive]\` is a likely drop candidate

Acceptance: each \`#[non_exhaustive]\` site has a justification (either inline comment, or this bead's close reason documents the classification). Closed-set marks are removed. \`mise run check\` is green. No SemVer breakage exposed (linesmith-core / linesmith-plugin are still \`0.1.x\`-line per ADR-0019, so over-restrictive un-marking is acceptable here, but worth being deliberate).

Driven by ADR-0021 follow-up #7.

title: Plugin LOG_LINES_PER_PLUGIN rate-limit integration coverage
description:
Per pr-test-analyzer on lsm-65r7, the plugin host's per-process LOG_LINES_PER_PLUGIN rate-limit (in linesmith-plugin/src/engine.rs:284-307) has no integration coverage. The single-render subprocess approach in log_bridge.rs can never trigger the rate-limit since each subprocess gets a fresh process. A regression that inverts the comparison (> vs >=) or drops the increment would not surface in any existing test.

Cheap fix: add a multi-render unit test inside linesmith-plugin's own tests module that calls rhai_log directly with set_current_plugin_id, asserting that LOG_EMITTED stays capped at LOG_LINES_PER_PLUGIN regardless of how many calls are made. Subprocess isolation isn't needed because the rate-limit lives in linesmith-plugin (this crate's tests already have the [lints.clippy] disallowed_methods=allow carve-out for direct build_engine calls).

Source: pr-review-toolkit pr-test-analyzer on lsm-65r7.

title: Subprocess timeout watchdog for log_bridge tests
description:
Per silent-failure-hunter on lsm-65r7, the integration tests in crates/linesmith/tests/log_bridge.rs use child.wait_with_output() with no wallclock guard. If the linesmith binary hangs (infinite loop in a plugin, deadlock somewhere in startup), the test stalls indefinitely until cargo's outer timeout fires (hours, not seconds) — silent-stall failure mode without diagnosis.

Add a wallclock guard around the subprocess call: either pull in the wait_timeout crate as a dev-dep, or spawn a watchdog thread that kills the child after N seconds (e.g., 30s) and panics with 'linesmith hung; killed after N seconds'. Same fix could apply to any other subprocess-style integration tests we add later.

Source: pr-review-toolkit silent-failure-hunter on lsm-65r7.

title: ADR: record bridge-stays-in-core deviation from ADR-0018
description:
ADR-0018 (workspace split) and its supersession ADR-0019 both describe a three-crate split into 'linesmith-core', 'linesmith-plugin', and 'linesmith-cli'. The lsm-v2o3 implementation diverged from this in two ways:

1. CLI stays as 'linesmith', not renamed to 'linesmith-cli' — the binary was already published to crates.io as 'linesmith' (cargo install linesmith), and the rename would have broken the documented install path. ADR-0019 already mentions this in its context (binary 'packaged at crates/linesmith to keep the published crate name linesmith'), but the explicit decision-to-not-rename isn't recorded as a discrete decision. lsm-494l (the rename bead) closed wontfix.

2. Bridge stays in linesmith-core, not linesmith-plugin. ADR-0018 listed 'rhai plugin engine + caps + dep-gated context + error classification' as living in linesmith-plugin. The implementation kept ctx_mirror (DataContext → rhai::Map mirror) and the RhaiSegment / output adapters in linesmith-core, since moving them would have cascaded segment.rs and core::segments::builder out of core too. linesmith-plugin holds engine/discovery/registry/header/errors only — pure rhai host with no linesmith domain types in its public surface.

Per AGENTS.md, accepted ADRs are immutable. Write a new ADR (or addendum-as-superseder) that records both deviations and their rationale so future readers can find the actual architecture without grepping commit history. Mark ADR-0018 (and possibly ADR-0019) as superseded by [new-ADR] for the relevant sections.

Source: post-extraction review pass, type-design + comment-analyzer agents corroborated 'consumer-side bridge' framing.
close_reason: ADR-0020 records the two crate-partition deviations from ADR-0018 (cli stays as 'linesmith'; ctx_mirror + RhaiSegment + output bridge layer in core, not cli). Updated ADR-0018 status to flag dual supersession by 0019 (publish) and 0020 (partition).

title: DepName newtype at the linesmith-plugin/core seam
description:
Per type-design review on lsm-v2o3, the plugin/core seam currently uses Vec<String> for declared deps with a panic in linesmith-core::plugins::segment::dep_from_token if a name doesn't map to DataDep. Drift is now caught at build time by the round-trip test added in this bead, but the type system doesn't carry the invariant — Vec<String> admits any string at the seam.

Introduce a transparent newtype DepName in linesmith-plugin with a crate-only ctor (new_validated, called only from header parsing). Header parser returns Vec<DepName>, CompiledPluginParts.declared_deps becomes Vec<DepName>, dep_from_token takes &DepName. The seam stays string-shaped on the wire but type-shaped in code; the plugin crate's invariant becomes type-enforced.

Defer until v0.2 / publish-decision time per ADR-0019. Source: pr-review-toolkit type-design-analyzer report on lsm-v2o3.

title: cli: wire explicit fallback labels for non_exhaustive enum match arms
description:
Five fallback _ => arms in cli return generic placeholder text for #[non_exhaustive] enums from linesmith-core:
- driver.rs themes_list ThemeSource → 'unknown source'
- doctor/mod.rs source_label CredentialSource → 'unknown credential source'
- doctor/mod.rs Head → 'HEAD (unrecognized)'
- doctor/mod.rs RepoKind → 'RepoKind: unrecognized'
- driver.rs ColorPolicy → from_terminal() (silent auto-detect fallback)

These are correct degradation today — they let cli + core roll forward independently — but they're perpetual deferrals: when a new variant lands in linesmith-core, the cli will keep rendering 'unknown ...' until someone notices. This bead tracks the rollup work of wiring explicit labels each time linesmith-core adds a variant.

Two related sites have already been hardened with explicit handling and are NOT part of this rollup:
- driver.rs load_config ConfigLoadOutcome _ arm now writes a stderr 'cli/core version skew' warning before falling back to defaults
- doctor/snapshot.rs read_config_at ConfigLoadOutcome _ arm now routes to ConfigReadOutcome::IoError (FAIL row) instead of Unresolved (SKIP)
- doctor/snapshot.rs snapshot_credentials CredentialError _ arm uses .code() to safely render variant tag without leaking token bytes
- doctor/mod.rs check_plugins_compile renders unexpected PluginError variants via .kind() (added in linesmith-core/src/plugins/errors.rs) to avoid leaking author-controlled message strings
- doctor/mod.rs PluginError classifier already routes well-known variants across plugins.compile / plugins.deps_valid / plugins.no_id_collisions / plugins.no_builtin_collisions check rows; only the catch-all _ arm remains as deferral

Process: when adding a #[non_exhaustive] enum variant in linesmith-core that any cli match site touches, also add the matching arm in cli before merging the core change. Document in CONTRIBUTING.md / AGENTS.md as a release checklist item.

Filed during lsm-1nh0 review by comment-analyzer (deferral arms with no per-arm bead). Single rollup bead instead of per-arm beads to keep the workflow lightweight.

title: ci: add cargo test -p linesmith-core isolation step
description:
mise run cargo:test invokes cargo test --locked --workspace which runs every crate's tests but does not prove cargo test -p linesmith-core passes in isolation. Since linesmith-core is now a publishable crate (per ADR-0018), a sneaky dev-dep leak — a core test that accidentally imports something only linesmith (cli) brings transitively — would pass --workspace while breaking crates.io consumers.

Add a CI step alongside the existing workspace test:
- cargo test --locked -p linesmith-core
- (when applicable) cargo test --locked -p linesmith-plugin (after lsm-v2o3)
- (when applicable) cargo check --locked -p linesmith-core --no-default-features (if features land)

Filed during lsm-1nh0 review by pr-test-analyzer. Low-priority because no leak today, but prevents one entire class of cross-crate regressions before the workspace publishes.

title: tests: sweep driver.rs path-construction sites for Windows separator-mismatch fragility
description:
The XDG cascade refactor (lsm-vsab) changed path construction from PathBuf::from(h).join(".config/linesmith/themes") (single join, mixed separators on Windows) to chained .join("...").join("...").join("...") (backslash-normalized). The OS treats both equivalently, but they're different strings.

Most existing tests use the old single-join pattern for filesystem setup only — fine, since create_dir_all/write/etc handle either form. But any test that compares a built path to cascade-rendered output via substring/equality will break on Windows.

Found because themes_list_includes_user_themes_with_source_path (driver.rs:1937) failed CI on the lsm-vsab push (run 25199244299). Spot-fix landed in the lsm-e4m1 commit. ~10 other sites identified in driver.rs that use the same single-join pattern (lines 1437, 1457, 1816, 1841, 1842, 1862, 1884, 1903) but they only do filesystem ops, not string comparison.

Acceptance:
- Audit every test site using .join("a/b") or .join("a\\b") for path construction
- For sites that compare against cascade output: convert to chained .join calls
- For sites that only do filesystem ops: leave alone (no fix needed; the pattern is harmless there)
- Document the gotcha in test conventions

title: runtime: refactor ConfigLoadOutcome toward deletion (collapse to Result)
description:
Type-design-analyzer review of lsm-e4m1 rates ConfigLoadOutcome 3/5 encapsulation, 2/5 invariant expression, 2/5 usefulness. Both consumers (driver's 3-tuple, doctor's ConfigReadOutcome) re-map every variant 1:1, so the type is a pass-through translation layer earning no compile-time leverage.

Proposed refactor:
1. Drop the Unresolved variant — load_config(resolved: &ConfigPath) and let Option handling happen at call sites (where the Option already lives)
2. Tighten source typing: IoError { source: io::Error } and ParseError { source: toml::de::Error } instead of the broad ConfigError. Outer path becomes unambiguously authoritative because the inner type doesn't carry one.
3. Promote warnings to Vec<UnknownKey { path: String, key: String }> so the future doctor surfacing (lsm-8sus) gets structure for free.
4. Drop #[non_exhaustive] on the pub(crate) type — the compiler will tell every caller to update on a new variant, which is what we want.
5. Final shape collapses to Result<Loaded, LoadError>.

Verify deletion test: would complexity vanish or reappear distributed across the 2 callers? Type-design-analyzer's read says single-call-site mapping makes this a clean refactor.

Defer to v0.2 — the lsm-e4m1 round closed the parity gap (warnings now flow on ParseError per Codex review fix), so this is polish, not correctness.

title: doctor: surface Plugin load_errors in Plugins category snapshot
description:
The runtime predicate runtime::plugins::load_plugins returns a PluginRegistry whose load_errors() the driver writes to stderr but the doctor currently discards. This is a parity gap parallel to lsm-q7ee (themes) and lsm-8sus (config warnings): doctor's Plugins category PASSes silently when plugins fail to compile.

Acceptance:
- snapshot_plugins folds registry.load_errors() into DoctorPluginsSnapshot
- 'All plugins compile' check renders WARN (not skipped) when load_errors is non-empty
- Existing doctor parity rule lsm-efmu audit finds no new mirror

Background: filed during lsm-e4m1 review pass after the runtime/plugins.rs doc claim 'doctor folds them into the Plugins category snapshot' was found stale and corrected to mention this follow-up.
close_reason: Already wired. Doctor's snapshot.rs:30-55 surfaces registry.load_errors().to_vec() into PluginsRegistrySummary.errors, and doctor/mod.rs:2185-2235 classifies them across plugins.compile, plugins.no_id_collisions, plugins.no_builtin_collisions, and plugins.no_invalid_deps check rows. Bead was filed during lsm-e4m1 review based on a stale runtime/plugins.rs doc claim that has now been corrected.

title: doctor: surface theme-loader diagnostics (malformed files, collisions, unreadable dirs)
description:
Parallel parity gap to lsm-8sus (which surfaces unknown-key warnings from Config::load_validated). After lsm-e4m1 lifted theme loading into runtime::themes::build_theme_registry with an on_warn callback, doctor still passes |_| {} as the warn-sink — discarding diagnostics for malformed theme files, name collisions (built-in override, duplicate user theme), and unreadable directory entries.

Result: a user with a malformed ~/.config/linesmith/themes/oops.toml runs 'linesmith doctor' and the Themes category PASSes silently. Same parity-gap class as the discarded Config warnings.

Proposed fix:
1. Add a counter or Vec<String> field to the doctor's themes-related snapshot (currently just known_theme_names: BTreeSet<String>).
2. Pass a real on_warn callback in collect_known_theme_names that accumulates into the counter / Vec.
3. Add a doctor check 'themes.no_loader_warnings' (or similar) that PASSes when count is 0, WARNs when > 0 with hint listing first 3 file paths.

Acceptance: a user with one malformed theme file gets a WARN line on 'linesmith doctor' instead of a silent PASS.

References:
- crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs::collect_known_theme_names (the |_| {} warn-sink)
- crates/linesmith/src/runtime/themes.rs::build_theme_registry (the on_warn parameter)
- crates/linesmith/src/theme/user.rs::with_user_themes (the original warn callback site)
- Mirrors lsm-8sus pattern (config unknown-key warnings)

title: doctor's Config check should mirror Config::load_validated unknown-key warnings
description:
Surfaced during lsm-2it2 parity audit of doctor snapshot helpers.

Current state: read_config_at in crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs uses bare toml::from_str::<Config>, which silently accepts unknown keys (typos like [segmnts.echo] instead of [segments.echo]).

Runtime state: driver.rs:1026 uses Config::load_validated which emits one warning per unknown key (top-level, [layout_options], [segments.<id>]) via the KNOWN_TOP_LEVEL / KNOWN_LAYOUT_OPTIONS allow-list.

The gap: a user with a typo in their config gets:
- linesmith run: a warning to stderr ('unknown key segmnts.echo')
- linesmith doctor: 'Config parses' renders PASS
The user's segment isn't loaded, but doctor doesn't surface the cause.

Proposed fix:
1. Switch read_config_at to call Config::load_validated, capturing warnings into a Vec<String>.
2. Add ConfigReadOutcome::LoadedWithWarnings { path, config: Box<Config>, warnings: Vec<String> } variant.
3. Add a new check 'config.no_unknown_keys' that PASSes on Loaded, WARNs on LoadedWithWarnings (label naming the count, hint suggesting the user check the config for typos and listing the first 3 keys).
4. Plain-mode coverage entry for the WARN.

Acceptance: a config with [segmnts.echo] WARNs on the new check; a clean config PASSes; the existing 'Config parses' check is unaffected (still PASS for both since they DO parse).

References:
- crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs:140 (read_config_at)
- crates/linesmith/src/config.rs:277 (Config::load_validated)
- crates/linesmith/src/driver.rs:1026 (runtime caller)

title: Test snapshot_update_probe HTTP/proxy branches with a fake transport
description:
Coverage gap surfaced in lsm-l35.9 review. snapshot_update_probe in crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs (~line 712) has three non-trivial branches that are only exercised by smoke testing the live binary:

1. Non-2xx HTTP classification (404, 403 rate-limit, 5xx incident → TransportError)
2. read_to_end I/O error path (connection drop mid-body)
3. Proxy detection from env (HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY parsing)

The proxy branch is the highest regression risk: it mirrors the pattern from commit 4cab952 ('feat(data): honor HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY for OAuth fetcher'). A refactor that drops the ureq::Proxy::try_from_env() call would silently make doctor unreachable behind corporate proxies with no test signal.

Approach options:
1. Inject a transport trait (similar to UsageTransport in data_context::fetcher) so snapshot_update_probe takes &dyn UpdateTransport. Tests pass a FakeTransport; production passes UreqTransport. Most thorough — also enables future probe-target customization.
2. Add wiremock-rs or mockito as a dev-dep and spin up a local HTTP server in the test (binds 127.0.0.1:0). Heavier setup, more end-to-end. Catches real ureq behavior changes.
3. Refactor snapshot_update_probe into smaller pure helpers (build_request, classify_response, etc.) so each one is unit-testable without I/O. Lighter than option 1 but more code restructuring.

Recommended: option 1. The classifier is already extracted (classify_update_response_inner); transport injection is the natural complement, and matches the pattern established in data_context::fetcher.

Defer trigger: file when one of these branches breaks in real use (most likely the proxy branch) — at that point the cost of writing the test pays for itself immediately.

References:
- crates/linesmith/src/doctor/snapshot.rs::snapshot_update_probe (~line 712)
- crates/linesmith/src/data_context/fetcher.rs::UsageTransport (the trait pattern to mirror)
- Review thread: pr-test-analyzer finding #2 from lsm-l35.9 review round

title: Hermetic from_process test seam: env-overridable DoctorEnv builder
description:
pr-test-analyzer's lsm-l35.4 review flagged that no test exercises the from_process → DoctorEnv wire-up for the Claude Code snapshot's home_state. The naive fix (set_var(HOME, tempdir) in a test) races with parallel test execution and is unsound under modern Rust's std::env::set_var safety model.

Refactor: extend DoctorEnv::from_process (or add a sibling fn) to accept env overrides as parameters, mirroring the cli_config_override that already exists. Tests then construct an override-driven snapshot deterministically without mutating process env.

Acceptance: a from_process_with_env(home_override, xdg_override, path_override, ...) helper exists and is used by at least one driver-level integration test that asserts ~/.claude/sessions/ count surfaces in stdout when $HOME points at a tempdir.

title: Doctor Self category: GitHub update probe with always-run network call
description:
Implement the Self/update-available check per docs/specs/doctor.md §Self.

Spec rules:
- Always-run (per 2026-04-29 spec edit; --full was dropped)
- Probe github releases API for the latest linesmith release
- 2s timeout (matches the rate-limit endpoint timeout convention)
- PASS if running on latest release
- WARN if newer release available
- WARN on transport-level errors (no network, DNS failure, timeout) — offline isn't a setup problem
- Reuse ureq workspace dep (no new dependency)

Why deferred from lsm-l35.2: that slice shipped Environment + Self/version + Self/binary-path (all in-process). The GitHub probe is a substantial standalone piece (HTTP client config + GitHub releases API JSON parsing + semver comparison + error-to-WARN mapping) that deserves its own slice rather than tacking onto lsm-l35.2's PR.

Suggested ID: self.update_available

Implementation hints:
- Add an injectable probe function on DoctorEnv (e.g. update_check: Box<dyn Fn() -> UpdateStatus>) so tests can stub it
- Production wiring: DoctorEnv::from_process() supplies the real probe; tests use a closure returning Latest / Outdated / Transport(err)
- Spec edit candidate: clarify in §Self what user-agent string to send (linesmith/<version>)

References:
- docs/specs/doctor.md §Self (lines 244-247)
- crates/linesmith/src/doctor/mod.rs (DoctorEnv, self_category)
- lsm-l35.2 (slice that intentionally deferred this)
close_reason: Self/update_available check landed. New DoctorUpdateProbe enum (Latest | Newer{latest} | TransportError{message} | ParseError{message}); update_probe field on DoctorEnv; check_self_update_available reading the snapshot in self_category. Probe lives in snapshot.rs::snapshot_update_probe — direct ureq Agent (not UsageTransport since GitHub is unauthenticated), 2s timeout, 32 KiB body cap, 'linesmith/<version>' User-Agent, honors HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY via ureq::Proxy::try_from_env. Pure classifier classify_update_response splits JSON parsing + tag-name extraction + version comparison from the network call. parse_three_part_version strips a leading 'v', truncates pre-release/build suffixes at first non-digit. Fallback for non-semver tags: equality → Latest, anything else → Newer with verbatim tag (so date-based or monorepo-prefixed releases still surface). All non-Latest outcomes WARN per spec §Self always-run rule (offline / GitHub outage doesn't gate exit-1). Tests: 8 classifier tests + 4 check_self_update_available tests + 3 plain_mode_coverage_envs entries (1443 lib tests, was 1431). Spec change-log entry added. mise run check + test green.

title: CLI: subcommands silently drop global flags (--no-color, --force-color, --check-config)
description:
Codex P2 finding during slice 1 (lsm-l35.1) revealed a class bug: when a subcommand dispatches in cli::parse, the populated CliArgs is discarded and only args.config is manually re-threaded into specific Action variants. Other CliArgs fields (color_override, check_config) silently vanish for every subcommand.

Confirmed silent drops today:
- linesmith --no-color init -- color override discarded; init prompts use ColorfulTheme regardless
- linesmith --no-color themes list -- discarded (output is plain anyway, but the contract is wrong)
- linesmith --no-color presets list -- discarded
- linesmith --no-color presets apply NAME -- discarded
- linesmith --check-config init / themes / presets -- check_config bool dropped silently (no-op)

Slice 1 closed the doctor instances:
- doctor --config X warns and degrades on stderr (driver.rs::doctor_action)
- doctor --no-color / --force-color rejected at parse time (cli.rs)

This bead handles the broader pattern. Two paths:

Path A (parser-level rejection): mirror the doctor pattern — reject --no-color / --force-color / --check-config when paired with any subcommand that doesn't consume them. Cleanest, consistent with the --plain rejection precedent. Risk: noisier for users who set NO_COLOR=1 globally and run a subcommand. Mitigation: NO_COLOR env var path is distinct from --no-color flag path and stays untouched.

Path B (thread through every Action variant): add color_override / check_config to ThemesList, PresetsList, PresetsApply, Init action variants. Heavier; each consumer must decide what to do with the override. Likely overkill for check_config (init/themes/presets don't have a check semantic).

Recommendation: Path A for color overrides (parser rejection); Path A for check_config too (it's Run-only by design). File a single follow-up issue with both fixes bundled if scope feels right.

References:
- crates/linesmith/src/cli.rs::parse (the dispatch flow that drops args)
- crates/linesmith/src/cli.rs::Action variants
- Codex review pass 3 (P2 finding that spawned this)
- lsm-l35.1 (where doctor's instances were fixed)

title: Doctor §Rate-limit endpoint spec: cover TLS handshake + captive portal in WARN/FAIL boundary
description:
docs/specs/doctor.md §Rate-limit endpoint demotes 'transport-level errors (DNS / connect / read timeout)' to WARN, but two real failure modes aren't addressed:

**1. TLS handshake failure on a working network.** DNS resolves, TCP connects, then TLS fails (cert expired, cipher mismatch, MITM proxy). User's network works, but trust store / system clock is broken. Currently ambiguous which row this falls under — likely silently classified as FAIL by an implementer reading the WARN enumeration literally.

**Fix:** add 'TLS handshake' to the WARN row enumeration with a hint suggesting 'check your system clock or proxy CA'.

**2. Captive portal returning 200 OK with HTML body.** TCP+TLS succeed, HTTP returns 200, but body is the airport WiFi splash page (text/html, not JSON). The current PASS row matches on status code alone ('returns 200'); the JSON deserialize then fails and falls into the next row's 'Endpoint returns expected shape → FAIL: missing required fields'. So the captive portal flips to FAIL with hint 'report a linesmith issue; Anthropic changed the API' — a misleading actionable hint.

**Fix:** add a Content-Type sniff before deserialize. Non-application/json + 200 → WARN with 'captive portal or proxy interception detected — check your network'.

**Trigger:** when slice .5 (Credentials + Cache + Rate-limit endpoint) lands and implements the actual probe. Both cases are spec-only edits today; the implementation can land at the same time.

**References:**
- docs/specs/doctor.md §Rate-limit endpoint (lines 213-225 area)
- Silent-failure-hunter pass 2 NEW-4, pass 3 carryover #4
- lsm-l35.5 (slice that consumes this spec edit)

title: Doctor v0.2 JSON: audit id/severity catalog mapping + decide id() public-API stability
description:
Two audits to pair with the v0.2 --json work for linesmith doctor (currently CheckResult populates a stable 'id' field per docs/specs/doctor.md §JSON output but no consumer ships).

**Audit 1 — id/severity catalog mapping:**
The CheckResult constructors (pass/warn/fail/skip) accept any &static str id — there's no compile-time guard preventing CheckResult::fail('env.stdout_tty.skip', ...) from being constructed. Today this is theoretical (slice 1 has one PASS check). Once slices .2-.6 each wire 5+ checks across 8 categories, accidental misuse will compile and only surface at JSON-consumer time.

Add a #[cfg(test)] catalog audit when --json ships: walk every check producer at runtime and assert each id appears in a single allowed-severities map (e.g. 'env.stdout_tty' may be PASS/WARN/SKIP but never FAIL). Cheap to add now while the catalog has one entry; expensive once eight categories exist.

**Audit 2 — id() / label() / hint() pub stability:**
These accessors are pub on a #[non_exhaustive] CheckResult with no in-tree consumer beyond tests. When --json lands, decide whether they remain pub (full external read surface) or become pub(crate) (only the serializer reads them, written to a stable JSON contract). Document the choice in the spec's §JSON output section.

**Trigger:** Concurrent with v0.2 JSON serializer work.

**References:**
- crates/linesmith/src/doctor/mod.rs (CheckResult constructors + accessors)
- docs/specs/doctor.md §JSON output
- Silent-failure-hunter pass 2 NEW-1, pass 3 NEW-3.1

title: ADR: linesmith doctor CLI shape — no scope flags, network-by-default
description:
Capture the v0.1 doctor CLI-shape decision in an ADR per AGENTS.md ('Decisions go in ADRs').

**Decision summary:**
- 'linesmith doctor' has one optional flag: --plain (ASCII output)
- All checks (including network probes: rate-limit endpoint, GitHub update check) run unconditionally
- No --full opt-in; --offline opt-out is on the table but unfiled
- --verbose / -v reserved for future detail-level work
- Transport-level network errors → WARN, not FAIL (offline isn't a setup problem)
- Auto-runs at end of 'linesmith init' (opt out via --no-doctor)

**Why an ADR is warranted:** This shape constrains every future check slice (.2-.6) and the v0.2 --json work. Future contributors will second-guess 'why no --full?' and 'why network by default?' without a written record.

**Driving discussion:** the slice 1 review pass on 2026-04-29 (5-agent code review + Codex review) surfaced the --full design tension; resolved by dropping it from the v0.1 surface (see docs/specs/doctor.md change log).

**Action:** copy docs/adrs/0000-template.md to docs/adrs/0008-doctor-cli-shape.md, fill in considered options ('always run', 'opt-in --full', 'opt-out --offline', 'tiered subcommands like quick/full'), document the chosen path + rationale, link from docs/specs/doctor.md.

title: Add --verbose / -v flag to linesmith doctor once first verbose-worthy data lands
description:
Diagnostic detail level for doctor (per docs/specs/doctor.md §Open questions). Defer until at least one check category produces data worth surfacing only on demand.

**Likely candidates per category:**
- Self: target triple, build profile, rustc version, full version metadata
- Environment: full $TERM / $COLORTERM / $LANG dump, OS version
- Config: all paths tried (not just resolved), parser source span on errors
- Credentials: full keychain service / file path (token still REDACTED)
- Cache: cached_at as ISO timestamp + bytes + schema version
- Plugins: each plugin's declared roles + dep list + file size
- Git: HEAD sha, upstream URL, .git path
- Endpoint probe: response headers + redirect chain
- Update check: changelog URL diff

**CLI shape:**
- --verbose / -v (universal short-flag pairing per cargo, flutter, mise, git)
- Orthogonal to --plain (both should compose; --plain --verbose is valid)
- Don't claim -v on Action::Doctor until this lands — keep it free

**Trigger:** When slice .2 (Environment + Self) lands and reveals what's actually worth gating behind verbose, or when a user asks for more detail than default.

title: Add --offline opt-out to linesmith doctor if network probes become friction
description:
Doctor's network checks (rate-limit endpoint probe, GitHub update check) run unconditionally per the v0.1 surface decision (see docs/specs/doctor.md §Open questions and the 2026-04-29 change log).

**Trigger to act:** First user reports of friction with the always-on probes — corporate air-gapped, captive portals, ultra-tight CI loops, or measurable doctor-runtime complaints.

**Scope when triggered:**
- Add --offline flag (long-only; no short)
- Skip Rate-limit endpoint category and the GitHub update check in the Self category when --offline is set
- Both skipped checks render as SKIP (not WARN) with reason 'skipped (--offline)'
- Document in doctor.md §CLI surface and §Edge cases

**Why opt-out, not opt-in:** opt-out for stated need is appropriate; opt-in would force users to remember a flag to get the diagnosis they came for. See doctor.md §CLI surface rationale.

title: fetcher: refactor resolve_proxy_from_env for warn-asserting tests
description: lsm-5rfy added resolve_proxy_from_env() with a warn-on-unparseable-URL path that's currently testable only via process-global env mutation (racy in parallel tests) or end-to-end manual verification. Fix shape (depends on lsm-8mbh's warn-sink injection): extract env-reading into a pure function resolve_proxy(get_env) so a fake getter drives all three branches; once lsm-8mbh lands, assert the warn fires with the expected variable name and the message contains 'falling back to direct connection'. Specifically pin that the URL value is NOT in the message (Codex flagged credential-leak risk; redaction is load-bearing). Covered today: smoke test that UreqTransport::new() is infallible. Flagged by pr-test-analyzer + silent-failure-hunter during lsm-5rfy review.

title: Tighten config.schema.json: per-segment + [line.N] sub-schemas
description:
Codex round 7 P2 #3: the published config.schema.json maps LineConfig.numbered and SegmentOverride.extra to serde_json::Value, producing additionalProperties: true on [line] and [segments.*] blocks. Editor tooling cannot catch typos like 'segmnts', 'lable', or invalid per-segment knobs that the loader DOES warn about (KNOWN_LAYOUT_OPTIONS, validated_segment_keys allowlists per segment id).

Fix path:
- Per-segment-id sub-schemas: [segments.context_window] gets a tighter schema than [segments.<plugin-id>]. Either oneOf branches keyed by segment id, or a separate map in the Config schema.
- [line.N] sub-tables: validate keys are positive-integer strings, values are LineConfig-shaped (segments array).

Likely needs custom JsonSchema impls or a manually-curated schema fragment merged into the schemars output. Schemars' flatten + serde_json::Value remap can't express this fidelity.

Deferred from lsm-gao because the v0.1 ship needs the basic schema published; users get top-level + per-segment-known-key validation immediately, even if plugin-extras and [line.N] internals stay open. Filed for v0.2.

title: Submit linesmith config.schema to schemastore.org
description:
Once the schema shape is stable post-v0.1, submit the JSON Schema to schemastore.org so VS Code, taplo, and IntelliJ pick it up automatically without users needing to write a #:schema directive in their config.toml.

Process: open a PR to https://github.com/SchemaStore/schemastore adding a fileMatch entry for linesmith config files (/linesmith/config.toml and similar paths). Schemastore pulls from the upstream URL on a schedule.

Deferred from lsm-gao because the schema needs to stabilize first; submitting before v0.1 ships could lock in a shape we'd want to evolve. Reasonable trigger: after v0.1.0 stable release.

title: Switch config.schema.json URL to version-pinned tag
description:
lsm-gao initially shipped a version-pinned tag URL per Codex round-8 P2 #2; reverted to main-pinned URL based on industry-pattern survey: bacon, starship, dprint all use single canonical URL with main pinning. The biome pattern (versioned + self-hosted) is the destination but premature without project website infrastructure.

## Decision rationale

Codex's concern (main schema may describe fields the user's binary doesn't have) is theoretical:
- Schema evolves forward-compatibly by convention (fields added, not removed).
- Editors validate 'field allowed by schema,' not 'binary recognizes field.'
- A schema slightly ahead loosens validation rather than tightens it.
- bacon and starship ship this exact pattern in production.

Reverting eliminates the dev-build 404 problem entirely (URL always resolves on main) and aligns with schemastore.org submission (lsm-eao3) which expects a single canonical URL per project.

## v0.2 reactivation criteria

Move to versioned + self-hosted (biome pattern) once two pieces land:
1. Project website with stable URL paths per release version (e.g., linesmith.oakoss.dev/schemas/{version}/schema.json).
2. schemastore.org submission for editor auto-detection without #:schema directive (lsm-eao3).

Until then: main-pinned is correct.
notes: Round-8 Codex review escalated this from P3 to P2 and the URL has now been switched to env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") tag form. Remaining work for this bead: ensure the release pipeline (release-plz / release.yml) commits the regenerated config.schema.json BEFORE tagging so the URL resolves on first install. Today's URL points at v0.1.1 — that tag exists but lacks config.schema.json (this commit landed post-tag), so dev binaries built from main between this commit and the next release write a 404 URL. Acceptable for pre-1.0 dev; users on tagged releases (v0.1.2+) get a working URL once release-plz is updated.

title: Add f64 boundary + current_usage missing-key tests for parse coverage gaps
description:
Two narrow test gaps flagged in lsm-9zvh round-4 review (pr-test-analyzer criticality 5):

1. f64 boundary symmetry: cost_lines_added_accepts_large_value_without_truncation pins u64 width preservation. Add a counterpart asserting try_f64_required accepts f64::MAX / subnormals as Some(_) — defends is_finite()-replacement (none today, but) or the as_f64() success path from over-tightening (e.g., someone adding  or ). Use a JSON literal at f64 boundary; verify Some round-trips.

2. current_usage inner missing-key: current_usage_inner_null_collapses_whole_turn_usage exists; the missing-key sibling doesn't. Per ADR-0014, try_u64_optional is silent on missing, the let-else still collapses TurnUsage to None — worth pinning since parse_current_usage's comment calls this out as deliberate. Test: payload omitting current_usage.input_tokens → cw.current_usage.is_none(), peer leaves like cw.size populate.

Both small (5-10 lines each). Could fold into next test pass on input.rs.
close_reason: ADR-0014 epic follow-ups: added current_usage_inner_missing and cost f64 success-path tests; reconciled input-schema.md with current Rust types (ModelInfo/WorkspaceInfo/TurnUsage rename, Percent::from_f64 constructor, InvalidValue carve-out wording); documented ParseError::MissingField as reserved (not currently constructed) and rewrote parse() rustdoc to describe the post-ADR-0014 contract.

title: Reconcile docs/specs/input-schema.md with current Rust types
description:
Spec drift accumulated pre-ADR-0014 and was only partially reconciled in lsm-9zvh.9:
- ModelInfo in spec shows 'pub id: String' but actual struct has only display_name (input.rs:54-56).
- WorkspaceInfo in spec shows cwd, current_dir, project_dir, added_dirs, git_worktree but actual struct has only project_dir + git_worktree (input.rs:58-62).
- TokenUsage spec name doesn't match the Rust TurnUsage type name.
- Status field on the spec says 'draft' / 'Version: 0.2'; should bump version and align with the now-shipped ADR-0014 contract.

Fix: walk every code block in input-schema.md against the actual Rust types in crates/linesmith/src/input.rs and reconcile. Bump spec status if appropriate.

Flagged in lsm-9zvh round-4 review (code-reviewer Critical #1 partially addressed by dropping SessionInfo; the rest of the drift remains).
close_reason: ADR-0014 epic follow-ups: added current_usage_inner_missing and cost f64 success-path tests; reconciled input-schema.md with current Rust types (ModelInfo/WorkspaceInfo/TurnUsage rename, Percent::from_f64 constructor, InvalidValue carve-out wording); documented ParseError::MissingField as reserved (not currently constructed) and rewrote parse() rustdoc to describe the post-ADR-0014 contract.

title: Decide on ParseError::MissingField — delete or document reservation
description:
After ADR-0014 round 4, no parser path constructs ParseError::MissingField anymore (the missing() helper was removed). Variant is still public, Display'd, and documented at input.rs:288-290. Either:
(a) delete the variant — breaking change since #[non_exhaustive] only protects against new variants, not removed ones. Bump major.
(b) keep declared as a reserved slot for future required-field policy, with a doc note explaining it's currently never constructed.

Recommendation: (b) for now (we're pre-1.0; option to delete remains). Update the variant doc to make 'reserved, currently unused in normalizer paths' explicit so callers don't write code that pattern-matches expecting it to fire.

Flagged by pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer during ADR-0014 round 4 review (criticality 6).
close_reason: ADR-0014 epic follow-ups: added current_usage_inner_missing and cost f64 success-path tests; reconciled input-schema.md with current Rust types (ModelInfo/WorkspaceInfo/TurnUsage rename, Percent::from_f64 constructor, InvalidValue carve-out wording); documented ParseError::MissingField as reserved (not currently constructed) and rewrote parse() rustdoc to describe the post-ADR-0014 contract.

title: Inject lsm_warn! sink for testability
description:
logging::emit (logging.rs:135) writes directly to io::stderr().lock() with no injectable sink — unlike emit_error_to. Per-leaf parser tests can therefore assert the degraded value but not 'exactly one warn fires at path X'.

Flagged by pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer during ADR-0014 review (criticality 4): ADR-0014 names lsm_warn! the diagnostic channel, but the channel is currently un-introspectable from tests. A future change that drops a warn would silently pass CI.

Fix shape: add emit_to(level, sink, msg) mirroring the existing emit_error_to, or thread a test-only buffer behind the macro. Tests can then assert exact warn count + path provenance for each warn-and-degrade leaf in input.rs.

Not blocking ADR-0014 epic ship; orthogonal logging refactor.

title: Multi-line plugin reuse: clone or Arc-share CompiledPlugin so a plugin can render on multiple lines
description:
Multi-line review (during lsm-bvu) flagged that a plugin id referenced in two [line.N] sections only renders on the first line. The second occurrence emits 'plugin already rendered on an earlier line' (specific warning landed in lsm-bvu) and skips. Real fix is to make CompiledPlugin shareable so each line can produce its own RhaiSegment.

**Why deferred:** v0.1 ships the limitation with a clear warning. Cross-line plugin reuse is a real but not-yet-blocking use case; the warn-and-skip behavior is documented in build_lines doc.

**Implementation options:**

1. **Arc-share CompiledPlugin** — change PluginRegistry::into_plugins() to return Vec<Arc<CompiledPlugin>>; build_one_line clones the Arc per use. Cheapest in memory; rhai::AST inside CompiledPlugin is already clone-cheap by design.
2. **derive(Clone) on CompiledPlugin** — straightforward but duplicates the AST per line. Acceptable for small plugin counts.
3. **Lazy compile-on-demand** — trade memory for compile time per line. Probably not worth it.

**Acceptance:** a multi-line config that references the same plugin id in two [line.N] sections renders the plugin's output on both lines (test mirroring build_lines_plugin_referenced_in_two_lines_warns_specifically_on_second). The cross-line warning becomes a no-op (delete or repurpose). Updates docs/specs/config.md changelog.

**Code pointers:**
- crates/linesmith/src/segments/builder.rs ~265 (lookup.remove → lookup.get + clone)
- crates/linesmith/src/segments/builder.rs ~280 build_one_line signature (drop consumed_plugins param)
- crates/linesmith/src/plugins/registry.rs ~44 CompiledPlugin struct (add Clone or wrap in Arc)

title: write_config_with_backup: test the rename-after-clobber breadcrumb path
description:
Pass-3 review (during lsm-5yd) flagged that the breadcrumb path in write_config_with_backup is uncovered. When a prior .bak exists and the policy clobbers it, then rename(path → .bak) fails after remove_file(.bak) succeeded, the helper appends a 'note: the previous .bak was removed just before this failed rename; it is gone' breadcrumb. Currently visually inspectable only.

**Why uncovered:** triggering rename failure portably between a successful remove_file and rename requires interposition (race) or cross-mount setup. A read-only parent breaks remove_file too, so it never reaches rename.

**Suggested approach (per pass-3 review):** spike a #[cfg(unix)] test that arranges for remove_file to succeed but rename to fail. One option: use a path where the source is a non-empty directory and the rename target's location requires permissions the user lacks at rename time only. Another: use a different filesystem (cross-mount) — heavyweight in CI.

**Acceptance:** test that exercises the clobbered_prior_bak=true → rename Err branch and asserts the breadcrumb message lands in stderr alongside the primary 'could not back up' error. Skip if portable trigger turns out impossible; document the gap in a code comment that survives.

title: linesmith init: honor cli_main's injected stdin (dialoguer bypasses)
description:
Codex pass-2 review (during lsm-5yd) flagged that init_action calls dialoguer::Select::interact(), which reads from the real terminal instead of the stdin parameter that cli_main exposes. presets_apply's overwrite prompt honors injected stdin; init breaks the contract. Embedders or test harnesses driving cli_main(..., Cursor::new(...), ...) cannot script init.

**Three options to evaluate:**

1. Drop the stdin parameter from the init dispatch path entirely (acknowledge the contract violation, document init as TTY-only). Cheapest, but makes the cli_main signature lie about what callers can do for this subcommand.
2. Roll our own Select-style prompt that reads from the injected stdin (~30 LOC). Loses dialoguer's arrow-key UX for embedded callers but preserves the cli_main contract.
3. Document init as terminal-only and detect non-TTY stdin up front, refusing with a clear error. Embedders use 'linesmith presets apply <name>' for scripted setup (which already works).

**Why not blocked on v0.1:** lsm-5yd's bead explicitly scoped init as 'interactive prompts via dialoguer'. presets_apply already covers the scriptable setup path. The contract violation is real but the user-visible workaround exists.

**Acceptance:** pick one of options 1-3, implement, write driver-level tests proving the chosen behavior. If option 2, also confirm the rolled-prompt UX is good enough that we're not making interactive callers worse off.

title: release.yml path-filtered pull_request auto-trigger
description:
Implement [ADR-0017](docs/adrs/0017-release-workflow-pr-validation.md): hand-edit `release.yml` so a `pull_request:` trigger with paths filter auto-fires the dry-run when release-infra files change. Builds on lsm-9ns (workflow_dispatch dry-run path).

**Shipped scope:**
- `pull_request:` trigger with `paths:` filter for `release.yml`, `dist-workspace.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `crates/*/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`. `release-plz.toml` and `release-plz.yml` deliberately excluded as false coverage (release.yml's matrix runs cargo-dist, not release-plz).
- `compute-tag` step extended with `pull_request` case using `github.event.pull_request.head.sha[:7]` (PR head, not merge SHA that `${GITHUB_SHA}` provides on PR events).
- `build-local-artifacts` `if:` gate widened to admit `event_name == 'pull_request'` (composes with the existing `pr_run_mode == 'upload'` clause and the lsm-9ns `workflow_dispatch` clause).
- `retention-days` ternaries widened to give PR builds the same 7-day retention as workflow_dispatch builds; tag-push runs keep the 90-day default.
- Fork-PR guard on the `Attest` step: `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`. Without this, fork PRs hit the step with clamped `id-token: write` and fail.
- Workflow-level `concurrency:` block with `cancel-in-progress: true` for `pull_request` events so superseded PR pushes cancel their predecessor's 7-target build. Tag-push and dispatch runs queue normally.
- Spec `docs/specs/release-process.md` §Dry-run workflow updated with both auto-trigger and dispatch paths, validation-surface caveats, fork-PR Attest guard rationale, and ADR-0017 cross-reference.

**Out of scope:**
- `release-plz.toml` / `release-plz.yml` PR-time validation: filed as lsm-amav (no off-the-shelf check mode in release-plz; bounded blast radius — broken release-plz config typically surfaces at next push:main release-plz run).
- cargo-dist `pr-run-mode = "upload"` migration: ADR explicitly chose against this because cargo-dist emits a bare `pull_request:` (no native paths filter), and getting fork guard + retention split + concurrency requires the same hand-edits regardless.
- Un-allow-dirty regen cycle: deferred until cargo-dist version bump or non-trivial toml shape change.

**Constraints honored:**
- `release.yml` is cargo-dist autogenerated; `dist-workspace.toml`'s `allow-dirty = ["ci"]` preserves these hand-edits across regen (Round 3 §2 of release-workflow-patterns research confirms "skip the file entirely" semantics).
- Tag-push trigger unchanged; lsm-9ns's `workflow_dispatch` path unchanged.

**Validation:** `actionlint` clean for new edits (only pre-existing autogen'd shellcheck warnings remain in cargo-dist sections), markdownlint + prettier clean. Real validation requires a `pull_request` triggering against release-infra files post-merge.
close_reason: release.yml hand-edits per ADR-0017: pull_request paths-filter trigger, compute-tag PR case (head SHA), build-local gate widening, retention-days split (7-day on PR/dispatch, 90 on tag-push), fork-PR Attest guard, workflow-level concurrency cancellation. Spec updated. release-plz.toml validation gap deferred to lsm-amav. cargo-dist regen cycle deferred.

title: Did-you-mean warning for typo'd [layout_options].separator keywords
description:
The current `parse_layout_separator` contract is intentional: anything not a reserved keyword (`space`, `powerline`, `capsule`, `flex`) renders as a literal. This means `separator = \"powereline\"` silently emits the literal text 'powereline' between segments. `layout_separator_typo_renders_as_literal_not_warn` pins this as deliberate.

Suggested follow-up: emit a one-line suggestion (`unknown separator keyword 'powereline'; did you mean 'powerline'?`) when the trimmed normalized input is alphabetic, single-token, and within Levenshtein distance ≤2 of a reserved keyword. Must NOT fire on multi-character literals like \" | \", \" · \", or any input with non-alphabetic characters. Update the typo test to assert the warning fires for 'powereline' but not for 'PIPE' or '<<'.

title: Powerline-passthrough gap: hardcoded Powerline defaults ignore [layout_options].powerline_width
description: Currently `apply_layout_separator` and `apply_separator_override` only swap segments whose default/runtime separator is `Space` or `Theme`. If a future segment hardcodes `Separator::powerline()` (i.e., `Powerline { width: One }`) as its default and the user sets `[layout_options].powerline_width = 2`, the segment keeps width One — silently undercounting layout cells. Pinned today by `layout_separator_does_not_double_wrap_when_default_already_powerline` as deliberate v0.1 behavior. Fix candidates: (a) widen the override match to also rewrite `Some(Powerline { .. })` so the configured width wins, or (b) document the limitation in the apply_layout_separator doc + spec so plugin/segment authors know. Linked to lsm-herx.2 (per-item separators) since the right long-term answer ties into separators-as-items.

title: True bg-transition powerline once Style.bg lands
description:
The lsm-1my MVP renders the powerline chevron with Role::Border foreground only — no bg-transition wedge. The bead originally specified 'chevron between two adjacent segments gets Role::Surface for bg, next segment's role for fg' but Style today has no bg field; this bead is blocked on that infrastructure.

**Prereq:** Style gains pub bg: Option<Color> (parallel to fg). sgr_open emits the SGR 48-series for bg. plugins/output.rs threads bg through.

**Then in lsm-1my's domain:**
- separator_style for Powerline returns a Style with bg=Role::Surface and fg=<previous-segment's role color>
- This requires the layout flatten step (items_to_runs) to know each chevron's left neighbor's role. Today separator runs don't carry this context — needs threading.

**Acceptance:** powerline-themed terminals see colored wedge transitions between adjacent segments matching ccstatusline's powerline rendering, not just a Border-colored chevron glyph.

title: Powerline separator: 2-cell font width support
description:
The current powerline implementation hardcodes Separator::Powerline.width() = 1 (segments/mod.rs). Most modern Nerd Fonts render U+E0B0 as 1 cell, but some fonts/sizes render it as 2; on those terminals the layout's total_width undercounts and the line overflows by one cell per separator. Codex flagged this in lsm-1my review as a real correctness concern.

**Options:**
- Add [layout_options].powerline_width = 1|2 (default 1) — explicit user knob
- Detect via terminal-cap-detection if such a probe exists for chevron width (unlikely)
- Document the limitation in user-facing docs and accept the failure mode

**Acceptance:** users on 2-cell-rendering Nerd Fonts can configure powerline_width = 2 and the layout engine charges 2 cells per chevron in total_width, preventing overflow.
close_reason: Shipped as part of lsm-1my: [layout_options].powerline_width = 1|2 knob plus a typed PowerlineWidth { One, Two } enum at the Separator::Powerline variant so the invalid-width class of bug is unrepresentable downstream. validate_powerline_width is the single config-boundary that maps u16 user input to the typed value with warn-and-fallback on anything other than 1 or 2.

title: Release-tag-time hyperfine bench: publish numbers in release notes (ripgrep pattern)
description:
Per docs/research/perf-benchmarking-survey.md, ripgrep publishes hyperfine numbers in their benchsuite/README.md at major releases — light-touch but honest. linesmith adopts the same pattern.

Current state (v0.1):
- mise run bench:cold-start runs hyperfine on demand against target/release/linesmith
- Numbers are not captured anywhere automated

Scope:
- Add a release-time step (in release.yml or release-runbook.md): run mise run bench:cold-start, capture stdout+JSON, attach to the release notes via gh release edit
- Decide: gate the release on numbers exceeding a budget (e.g. p95 > 30ms), or just publish without gating?
- Document the release-time step in docs/ops/release-runbook.md
- Optional: capture historical numbers in a CSV checked into docs/research/ so trends across releases are visible

Acceptance: every cargo-dist release has its hyperfine numbers visible in the GitHub Release notes; users evaluating linesmith vs ccstatusline can see actual cold-start times without running locally.

Cross-ref: docs/research/perf-benchmarking-survey.md §Recommendation.

title: Evaluate CodSpeed for managed bare-metal CI perf gating (v0.2+)
description:
Per docs/research/perf-benchmarking-survey.md: the only Rust projects with serious CI perf gating (uv, ruff) converged on CodSpeed (codspeed-criterion-compat / codspeed-divan-compat) on bare-metal runners. GitHub-hosted runners have ~15% wall-clock variance — Criterion+absolute-thresholds is low-signal at our scale.

Current state (lsm-jedb closed v0.1):
- crates/linesmith/benches/render.rs is local-only (mise run bench), not gated
- mise run bench:cold-start runs hyperfine end-to-end against the release binary on demand
- CI bench gate + bash budget script were dropped in v0.1 as low-signal

Scope for this bead (v0.2+):
- Sign up for CodSpeed open-source plan
- Adopt codspeed-criterion-compat in benches/render.rs (drop-in replacement for criterion::*)
- Wire .github/workflows/codspeed.yml per CodSpeed's docs
- Reference uv's bench.yml (https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) for the canonical two-axis composition (walltime + simulation)
- Decide thresholds: regression-vs-main % gate, not absolute
- Update README How fast section to reflect the new CI signal

Acceptance: PRs see per-bench regression deltas vs main in the PR thread; significant regressions block merge.

Trigger to revisit: when render volume grows enough that local-only bench feels insufficient, or when a regression slips through that the new gate would have caught.

title: OutputStyle: lift non-empty-string invariant into the type via constructor (ADR-0008 conformance)
description:
Code review (type-design-analyzer P1) flagged that OutputStyle::name is constructible empty externally despite the parser's empty-string filter at the boundary. The parser route is well-covered, but a downstream test fixture or plugin host can build 'OutputStyle { name: String::new() }' and bypass the filter — segments that do 'if ctx.output_style.is_some() { render(name) }' would then render a blank pill.

The codebase already commits to the 'constructor enforces invariants' pattern via Percent::new (input.rs:194-200). OutputStyle and agent_name regress from that standard for the same invariant.

Scope:
- Add OutputStyle::new(name: String) -> Option<Self> mirroring Percent::new
- Make 'name' field non-public; expose via accessor 'name(&self) -> &str'
- Decision call: do the same for agent_name? Either introduce a NonEmptyString newtype reused by both, or accept the asymmetry as deliberate and document it on the field
- Update parse_output_style + parse_agent_name to use the new constructor
- Update test fixtures (segments/output_style.rs, plugins/ctx_mirror.rs, input.rs tests) to use the new constructor
- Document the new invariant in docs/specs/input-schema.md

Acceptance: OutputStyle { name: "" } no longer constructible from outside the crate; the non-empty invariant lives in the type system, not as a parser-only contract.

Cross-ref: ADR-0008 (canonical type refinements). Rated P1 by type-design-analyzer.

title: GitHub repo metadata: set topics + homepage for discoverability
description:
Repo description is set; topics is empty array, homepage is null. Empty topics means linesmith won't surface in GitHub topic searches (claude-code, statusline, rust, ai). One-time fix, but visible at launch.

Scope:
- gh api PATCH /repos/oakoss/linesmith — set topics: [claude-code, statusline, rust, ai-coding, claude, cli, anthropic, terminal, prompt-tool] (verify GitHub topic name conventions; max 20)
- Set homepage: pick between docs.rs/linesmith (when published), github.io page (none yet), or omit until there's a real landing page
- Document the gh api command in docs/specs/release-process.md so future repos get the same treatment

Cargo.toml keywords/categories already set correctly (statusline/claude-code/claude/cli/ai, command-line-utilities/development-tools); skip cargo side.

Acceptance: linesmith appears in GitHub topic searches for claude-code + statusline; topics + homepage visible on repo landing.

title: docs/USAGE.md — user-facing configuration + segment reference
description:
Today docs/specs/ exists but is contributor-facing (decision rationale, internal contracts). Users wanting to configure linesmith have no consolidated reference; they grep through 17 segment files + spec docs. ccstatusline ships docs/USAGE.md + docs/WINDOWS.md as user-facing.

Scope:
- docs/USAGE.md:
  - Install + first-run walkthrough (cross-link README, lsm-5yd init flow)
  - Config file location + resolution order
  - Each shipped segment: id, what it shows, full TOML option table, common patterns
  - Theme reference (built-ins + user-theme path)
  - Layout options (separators, multi-line once lsm-bvu lands)
  - Plugin segment authoring overview (cross-link plugin-api.md spec)
  - Troubleshooting (common stderr messages, doctor command from lsm-l35)
- README links to docs/USAGE.md prominently
- (Defer docs/WINDOWS.md to v0.3+ unless Windows-specific quirks accumulate)

Acceptance: a user can configure linesmith end-to-end without reading code or contributor specs.

title: TOML schema migration policy + breaking-change protocol
description:
lsm-gao publishes config.schema.json via schemars; need a written policy on what happens when the schema changes between versions. Without it, schema breakage is ad-hoc, surprising, and risks frustrating early adopters who automated config generation.

Scope:
- docs/specs/config-migration.md (or section in existing config spec):
  - Schema versioning approach (separate from crate SemVer? or tied?)
  - Deprecation cycle: when a field is renamed/removed, how many minor versions does the old form work?
  - Breaking-change protocol: what triggers a major version bump (v1 → v2) for config?
  - Migration runner: do we ship 'linesmith config migrate' subcommand or expect manual edits?
  - Schema diff in release notes (cliff config?)
- Apply policy to existing schema work; bump schema_version constant if not present

Cross-link from CONTRIBUTING (lsm-00f) and release-process.md.

Acceptance: schema changes follow a documented protocol; users can predict migration cost from a release version bump alone.

title: Spike: burn-rate / survival projection segment (research signal #6)
description:
Research signal #6 (user-demand-research-for-claude-code-statuslines-ranked memory): AndrewTKent mockup at anthropics/claude-code#43271 shows demand for burn-rate + projected-survival ('at current pace, you'll hit 5h limit in ~2h'). No tool ships this today.

Scope (spike, not full feature):
- Research note (docs/research/) on:
  - Data sources: stdin context_window deltas? JSONL token rate? OAuth usage endpoint window?
  - Burn-rate computation window (last 5min? last hour? rolling?)
  - Projection model: linear extrapolation vs exponential vs piecewise
  - Failure modes: idle sessions, /resume noise, /compact reset
- Mock segment output across 3-4 scenarios
- Decision: ship as new segment vs extension of context_window/rate_limit_*

Acceptance: research note + draft ADR; promotion to full feature gated on findings.

title: README: privacy / no-telemetry statement + network-call disclosure
description:
linesmith makes zero network calls except the optional OAuth usage endpoint when the user opts in to rate-limit segments. This needs to be visible in README (not buried in docs/) so users evaluating the npm-supply-chain alternative see the safety story. Aligns with linesmith-project-vision differentiator #4 ('single-binary kills npx supply-chain risk').

Scope:
- README §Privacy or §Network behavior
- Concrete list:
  - No telemetry, no analytics, no error reporting
  - One outbound call: api.anthropic.com OAuth usage endpoint, only when ctx.usage() is called by an enabled segment
  - Credentials read from macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json; never written elsewhere
  - HTTPS_PROXY honored (cross-link lsm-zzzz once it lands)
- Pointer to docs/specs/data-fetching.md for full network contract

Acceptance: a privacy-conscious user can audit the network surface from README in under 30s.

title: Spike: cache-hit / cache-creation countdown segment (research signal #8)
description:
Research signal #8 (user-demand-research-for-claude-code-statuslines-ranked memory): users want visibility into cache-hit/cache-creation token economics ('how much of the next call will be cached vs fresh'). CC stdin already exposes cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens (per StatusContext.TurnUsage).

Scope (spike):
- Research note: what does 'cache countdown' mean concretely? Time until cache TTL expires? Cache-hit ratio over rolling window? Cost saved by cache hits?
- Survey what's actually in the API headers (cache TTL not exposed today; would need inference)
- Mock segment renders: '95% cached' vs 'cache TTL: 4m' vs 'saved /bin/zsh.42 from cache'
- Decision: which subset is feasible without API changes

Acceptance: research note + ADR or 'wontfix' decision with reasoning. Promotion to full feature gated on data availability.

title: Git widget expansion: PR/MR, file counts, origin/upstream owner+repo, SHA segments
description:
ccstatusline ships ~25 distinct git widgets beyond branch+dirty+ahead/behind. Our composite git_branch covers basics; users wanting fine-grained control need separate segments.

Scope (parity, not full surface):
- segments/git_pr.rs — gh/glab CLI integration; render PR# + optional review status + title
- segments/git_origin.rs — owner / repo / owner-repo combinations from remote URL
- segments/git_upstream.rs — upstream-fork detection + owner/repo
- segments/git_sha.rs — short SHA
- segments/git_files.rs — staged/unstaged/untracked file counts (or sub-config of git_branch)
- segments/git_changes.rs — insertions/deletions counts (+42 -10 style)

Each: separate config, hide-when-empty, opt-in. May share a GitContext data layer to avoid duplicate gix walks.

Acceptance: ccstatusline users migrating can recreate their statusline without losing widgets.

title: Terminal width modes: full / full-minus-N / dynamic-until-compact
description:
ccstatusline lets users choose how terminal width is computed: full / full-N (default 40) / dynamic-until-compact (% threshold, default 60%). Avoids edge-case wraps in tmux/iTerm/IDE-integrated terminals.

Scope:
- [layout_options].terminal_width_mode enum
- Optional offset value
- RenderContext threading (already in place)
- Snapshot tests for each mode + boundary

Acceptance: users with terminal-width quirks can tune width-detection without forking.

title: Segment: skills — render hook-driven skill/agent/MCP activity (research signal #7)
description:
ccstatusline ships a Skills widget driven by hooks; modes: last/count/list, hide-when-empty, list-limit, most-recent-first. Maps to research signal #7 (claude-hud at 19.8k stars proves demand for live skill/agent/MCP visibility).

Scope:
- Determine data source: CC hook events or stdin-derived agent field (latter already covered by lsm-iy9z but skills is broader)
- Hook event capture infrastructure (likely via local cache file written by a CC hook script)
- segments/skills.rs with mode enum
- TOML schema + opt-in default off
- Snapshot tests + cache-staleness tests

Acceptance: users can see currently-active skill/agent/MCP without context-switching to CC UI.

title: Segment: workspace fish-style abbrev — abbreviate long cwd paths like fish/zsh prompt
description:
ccstatusline ships fish-style cwd abbreviation (e.g. /Users/jace/.code/github/oakoss/linesmith → /U/j/.c/g/oakoss/linesmith). The workspace segment today shows the full project_dir basename or path; needs an opt-in abbrev mode.

Scope:
- workspace.rs Config: 'abbrev: AbbrevMode' enum (None, Fish, Tail(N))
- Fish: every dir except last keeps first char (or .X for hidden)
- Tail(N): keep last N path segments
- ~ home abbreviation (separate or part of mode)
- Snapshot tests covering each mode + edge cases

Acceptance: long paths render compactly when fish/tail mode enabled; default (None) preserves current behavior.

title: Segment: terminal_width — render current terminal column count
description:
ccstatusline ships a terminal-width widget. Useful for debugging layout/truncation issues. Trivial: read RenderContext.terminal_width.

Scope:
- segments/terminal_width.rs
- Format option (number, 'cols: N')
- Snapshot tests

Acceptance: renders current terminal cell count.

title: Engine: install-time refreshInterval writeback for CC ≥2.1.97
description:
ccstatusline writes statusLine.refreshInterval (1–60s, default 10s) into Claude settings.json when CC ≥2.1.97 is detected. Reduces statusline spawn frequency.

Scope:
- linesmith init / linesmith config TUI (lsm-herx.28) — add refresh_interval prompt
- Detect CC version (from existing settings.json or 2.1.119 (Claude Code))
- Atomic write-back into Claude settings.json with comment-preserving merge
- Range validation 1–60s; default 10s
- Snapshot tests for the merge

Acceptance: install/onboarding writes refreshInterval when CC version supports it; older CC versions skip silently.

title: Segment: model — infer 1M context window from model-name suffix when JSON omits size
description:
ccstatusline infers 1M context from model name suffixes ([1m], '1M context') when the CC payload's context_window_size is missing. We already strip '(X context)' from model display name (lsm-rkxh); adding inference for the size is the symmetric correctness win.

Scope:
- model.rs / context_window.rs: detect [1m] / 1M context suffixes in ModelInfo.display_name / model.id
- When ContextWindow.size is missing/null but pattern matches, default to 1_000_000
- ADR or short note in spec since this introduces a small behavior heuristic
- Tests covering matched/unmatched/explicit-size cases

Acceptance: 1M-context users see correct context_bar / context_window output even when CC payload omits size.

title: Token speed segments: input/output/total streaming-speed widgets
description:
ccstatusline ships Input Speed / Output Speed / Total Speed widgets — rolling-window (0–120s, 0=full session) tokens-per-second from JSONL stream. Subagent-aware. Useful for users wanting throughput visibility.

Requires: streaming-window plumbing on top of jsonl aggregator (currently aggregates totals but no time-windowed deltas).

Scope:
- Extend jsonl aggregator to expose rolling rate over configurable window
- 3 new segments (tokens_speed_in, tokens_speed_out, tokens_speed_total)
- Window config (default 30s; 0 = full session)
- Format options: tok/s, tok/min
- Snapshot + window-edge tests

Acceptance: speed widgets render reasonable values across short and long windows; subagent activity counted.

title: Snapshot tests via TestBackend + insta
description: Pin TUI screen rendering with ratatui's TestBackend + insta snapshots. Each screen state gets a snapshot test exercising representative model input. Catches accidental layout drift / SGR regressions. Includes resize handling tests.

title: Self-demonstrating controls (color swatches, separator glyphs, theme mini-previews)
description: Inline preview rendering for individual config controls. Color Level row shows a swatch in that color level. Separator picker rows show the actual glyph. Theme picker rows render a mini-statusline at that theme. Reuses layout::render_to_runs scoped to a single token/row.

title: EnvironmentWarning widget (Capability-aware footer warnings)
description: Reusable inline-warn widget. Slots into Color editor, Terminal Options, Powerline Setup, Install screen. Detects the user's terminal capabilities via existing Capability enum + env-var heuristics; surfaces remediation hints when the selected option won't render correctly (e.g., 'VSCode Users: minimumContrastRatio setting may distort colors'). Image 6 shows the pattern.
close_reason: EnvironmentWarning footer ships: NoColorSet / NoColorSupport / LimitedPalette(LimitedTier) / VsCodeContrastShim / TmuxNoTrueColorPassthrough variants, rendered as additional rows in the preview-header warnings panel via prepend_env_warnings. Compute is pure on a snapshotted env (EnvironmentSnapshot::from_process); LimitedTier sub-enum makes the palette-tier invariant compile-time. Color-policy aware: Auto fires the full ladder, Always suppresses ladder but keeps terminal-specific (VSCode/tmux), Never silences the panel entirely. Tmux remediation is tier-gated (only Palette16/256, not None) and softened to acknowledge the outer-terminal-doesn't-support-truecolor case. 1804 tests, mise check clean. 6 review iterations (1 toolkit + 5 codex) addressed 14+ findings: data-loss / parse-regression / silent-failure / type-design / doc-rot. 2 follow-up beads filed for v0.2 polish (panel separator UX, tmux signal split).

title: Nerd Font detection wiring (for Powerline screen)
description: Detect whether a Nerd Font is active in the current terminal. Can't perfectly verify, but heuristics: try rendering a Nerd Font glyph and check terminal-reported width, or check common env vars (TERMINAL_FONT_NAME etc.). Used by Powerline Setup screen to show 'Font Status: ✓ Installed / ✗ Not detected'.

title: Install to Claude Code screen + detection + atomic write-back (folds lsm-5yd)
description: Image 11 in ccstatusline. PropertyScreen-based. Detects existing ~/.claude/settings.json, shows current state (✓ Installed / ✗ Not installed), offers install/uninstall toggle. Atomic write with backup of the existing settings file. Folds lsm-5yd (linesmith init) into the TUI surface. Also keeps a non-TUI `linesmith init` command path for users who don't want to launch the TUI.

title: Global Overrides screen (PropertyScreen flat-properties)
description: Image 10 in ccstatusline. PropertyScreen-based. Toggles for the 3 engine knobs (Inherit Colors, Minimalist Mode, Global Bold) plus existing global config (claude_padding via [layout_options], default separator, default padding). Multi-paragraph 'Note:' footer with bullet definitions. Blocked by all 3 engine knob beads.

title: Engine knob: Global Bold (overlay Style.bold on every segment)
description: New theme-layer feature surfaced through Global Overrides. Composes at SGR-emit time. Trivial: Style.bold |= global_bold before encoding.

title: Engine knob: Minimalist Mode (strip decorative prefixes/labels)
description:
New layout-engine feature surfaced through Global Overrides. Strips icon + label from every segment (the 'decorative prefix' framing).

Implementation easier post-lsm-1o70 (Starship-parity templates): becomes 'evaluate template with $icon and $label masked.' Without templates, requires a per-segment 'is_decorative' flag.

Recommend deferring until lsm-1o70 lands.

title: Engine knob: Inherit Colors (separators take preceding widget's foreground)
description:
New layout-engine feature surfaced through Global Overrides. When enabled, separators emit with the foreground color of the preceding segment instead of their own. Architecture: separator stays stateless data; layout engine looks up neighbor at emit time.

No external bead deps. v0.2.

title: Terminal Options screen + Terminal Width sub-screen + Color Level
description: Image 8/9 in ccstatusline. PropertyScreen-based main entry → drilldown to Terminal Width sub-screen (with three modes including 'compact at threshold') and Color Level sub-screen. Color Level row shows a color swatch rendered at the current setting (self-demonstrating control).

title: User-theme discovery wiring (existing registry → TUI)
description: Wire ThemeRegistry::with_user_themes into the TUI boot path so user-authored themes from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/linesmith/themes/*.toml flow through to the theme picker alongside built-ins. Snapshot at boot — quit-and-reopen picks up new user themes, no mid-session reload (filed separately as a v0.2 follow-up).
close_reason: ThemeRegistry::with_user_themes wired into TUI boot via runtime::themes::build_theme_registry; user themes flow through to the picker alongside built-ins. Boot-time snapshot; reload-on-save deferred to lsm-zmnn.

title: Theme picker screen
description: Lists built-in themes (default, minimal, 4 Catppuccin variants) + user-discovered themes from the user themes dir. Cursor-driven preview: while the picker is active, the global preview header at the top of the screen renders with the theme at the cursor (live override), so Up/Down shows each theme's effect on the user's current segments. Per-row inline mini-previews are tracked separately as a v0.2 UX enhancement.
close_reason: Theme picker: ListScreen-driven row list of every registered theme (built-ins + user-discovered), Esc-back to MainMenu, Enter commits to document with decor preservation + non-scalar refusal, cursor-driven global preview swaps theme on Up/Down, unknown-theme banner in title for typo defense. Per-row inline mini-previews deferred (lsm-bhjf).

title: Color editor (single-screen, row-IS-preview, all segments at once)
description:
Image 6 in ccstatusline. List of segments where each row's text is rendered in that segment's current color (the list IS the preview). Verb keys: ↔ cycle foreground, (f) toggle bg/fg, (b)old, (h)ex, (r)eset, (c)lear all, (s)how separators toggle. 'Current foreground (8/17): Cyan' counter shows position in palette cycle.

Decision still open: edit at the role level (theme-wide) or segment level (override). Likely segment-level overrides, matching [segments.<id>].style today.

VSCode warning footer (from Capability detection) when terminal doesn't support truecolor — uses the EnvironmentWarning widget (lsm-herx.31).

title: Per-segment wiring: tokens_* family → boolean+string template
description: Wire tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_cached, tokens_total. Mostly identical config shape; might end up as a single editor that switches mode.

title: Per-segment wiring: rate_limit_* family → format-enum + threshold templates
description: Wire rate_limit_5h, rate_limit_7d, rate_limit_5h_reset, rate_limit_7d_reset, extra_usage through their respective templates. Format enum (percent|progress|duration), thresholds (progress_width), icon+label.

title: Per-segment wiring: git_branch (composite) → composite template
description: Wire git_branch through the composite template. Sub-tables: dirty (enabled, format, indicator, hide_below_cells), ahead_behind (enabled, ahead_format, behind_format, hide_when_zero, hide_when_no_upstream, hide_below_cells). Plus top-level: icon, label, max_length, truncation_marker, short_sha_length.

title: Per-segment wiring: context_window + context_bar → threshold + composite templates
description: Wire context_window (simple) and context_bar (composite with thresholds + characters sub-tables) through templates.

title: Per-segment wiring: model + workspace + cost + effort + session_duration → templates
description: Wire the simple-config segments through the format-enum and boolean+string templates. Mostly mechanical once templates exist. Includes per-segment description text (pulled from doc-comments or inline) for the bottom-of-screen description area.

title: Per-segment editor template: plugin segment free-text TOML editor
description:
Plugin segment configs are script-defined and not formally schema'd; the TUI can't form-generate them. Provide a tui-textarea-backed multi-line TOML editor with syntax-aware validation (parses the user's input as TOML, shows inline error if invalid, blocks save until valid).

Save target: the [segments.<plugin-id>] table extras.

title: Per-segment editor template: composite (sub-tables like dirty + ahead_behind)
description:
Reusable form template for segments with nested config sub-tables. Renders each sub-table as its own collapsible section. Drilldown to a sub-screen for editing within the section.

Used by: git_branch (dirty.* / ahead_behind.* nested tables), extra_usage (similar shape), context_bar (thresholds.green / thresholds.yellow + characters.full/partial/empty).

title: Per-segment editor template: boolean+string (enabled flags + indicator strings)
description:
Reusable form template for the (boolean toggle + string field) pair pattern. Used by: workspace, effort, segments with enabled+icon+label triples.

Composable with the threshold template for segments that mix both.

title: Per-segment editor template: threshold (hide_below_cells, max_length, etc.)
description:
Reusable form template for u16 cell-threshold fields. Numeric input with bounds validation; arrow-keys to step.

Used by: context_bar (cells, thresholds), git_branch (max_length, dirty.hide_below_cells, ahead_behind.hide_below_cells), rate_limit_*_reset (progress_width).

Soft dep on lsm-vla9: revisit if width.max audit changes which segments expose width fields.
