Belongs in crates/linesmith/tests/integration.rs or a new tests/plugins.rs. Pair with the RhaiSegment wrapper (Phase 4) since the end-to-end value of this test is 'plugin is registered AND reachable by the render path' — RhaiSegment is what makes the second half true.

**Acceptance:** a test fixtures two dirs each with one plugin, one collision, and one bad plugin; asserts PluginRegistry::load registers the two good plugins in declaration order, reports the collision + compile error, and get() returns the right plugin.
close_reason: End-to-end plugin test landed: tests/integration.rs::xdg_plugin_renders_via_full_driver_path drives cli_main → load_plugins → build_segments → RhaiSegment::render with a real .rhai file under XDG.

title: Resolve 0-byte plugin file spec vs impl discrepancy
description:
plugin-api.md:448 §Edge cases: 'Plugin file is 0 bytes → Compiled as a no-op AST; render call returns (); segment hides'.

Current Phase 3 registry.rs compile_plugin requires `const ID`, so a 0-byte file raises PluginError::Compile { message: 'missing required const ID' } rather than silently hiding.

Two valid paths: update the spec to match impl ('0-byte file is a compile error'), or update the impl to match spec (treat empty source as silent skip). Decide which, then add a test asserting the chosen behavior.

**Acceptance:** spec and impl agree on 0-byte behavior; a registry test pins the chosen path.

title: PluginError design follow-ups (non_exhaustive review, source chain, path sharing)
description:
Deferred items from Phase 2 type-design review of `crates/linesmith/src/plugins/errors.rs`. None blocking for Phase 2-6 of lsm-ewa; revisit when concrete callers surface.

**Items:**

1. **Re-evaluate `#[non_exhaustive]` on PluginError.** Phase 2 kept the attribute as a defensive default. The type-design reviewer argued it's overkill for a currently-crate-private concept and forces needless `_ =>` arms in doctor matchers. Audit once lsm-l35 (doctor) wires a match site: if every variant needs explicit handling, drop the attribute; if we truly expect variants to grow across releases, keep it. Decision should be recorded in this bead's notes.

2. **Wire `std::error::Error::source()` chain for `Compile`.** Today the variant carries `message: String` (rhai's error stringified). When Phase 3 wires `rhai::Engine::compile_file()`, preserve the underlying `rhai::ParseError` as `source` so doctor / debug output can surface line+column info programmatically instead of regex-scraping the formatted message.

3. **Consider `Arc<Path>` in `Compile` + `IdCollision`.** Current `PathBuf` is fine at today's scale (< 100 plugins). If a long-running daemon retains error history across many reloads, the clone-cost becomes a real thing. Revisit when daemon mode lands (or after profiling shows a hotspot).

4. **`Timeout` → `WallclockTimeout` rename.** Would disambiguate from `ResourceExceeded { limit: MaxOperations }`. Kept the current name in Phase 2 to avoid bikeshed; if the wrapper work (Phase 5) makes the ambiguity more real, rename then.

**Acceptance:** at least #1 decided + recorded; #2 wired when real rhai::ParseError hits the code (Phase 3). #3 + #4 re-triaged.

title: Add serde::Serialize to DataDep for telemetry + explain output
description:
DataDep currently has Debug + Display (lowercase tokens matching the `@data_deps` header syntax). When telemetry, a `linesmith explain` command, or debug-dump CLI lands, it'll want to emit a segment's declared deps as structured data (JSON / TOML). Add `#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]` at that point.

**Scope:**
- Add serde feature flag (if not already on by default for this crate).
- Derive Serialize + Deserialize on DataDep with the lowercase-token representation (`#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`).
- Keep Display impl identical — both should produce the same wire name.

**Why deferred:** no current consumer. Adding now risks adding a serde dep for no immediate use. Pair with whichever feature first needs structured output.

**Acceptance:** `serde_json::to_string(&DataDep::Git)` returns `"git"`; round-trip deserialization succeeds.

title: Add data_deps declaration-vs-usage truthfulness test harness
description:
Phase 1 of lsm-ewa landed `Segment::data_deps()` but nothing enforces that a segment's declared deps match the sources its `render()` actually reads. A segment can call `ctx.usage()` without declaring `DataDep::Usage` and the code compiles + runs (lazy accessor initializes on demand). Once the runtime's union-and-prefetch pass lands with real fetchers, under-declaring segments will trigger lazy fetches that the prefetch skipped — silently slower, defeating the whole point of declaring deps.

**Scope:**
- Instrument `DataContext` with a test-only accessor-tracker (e.g., `#[cfg(test)]` fields that record which lazy accessors were called).
- Add a contract test per built-in segment: build the segment, run `render` against an instrumented DataContext, assert the touched accessor set is a SUBSET of `data_deps()`.
- Run the same harness against plugin/rhai segments in Phase 2 testing.

**Why now vs later:** the bug doesn't manifest until real fetchers land (lsm-y6m for usage, lsm-8jl for git). File as a follow-up so the invariant gets a typed enforcement before it can rot.

**Acceptance:** a built-in segment that reads `ctx.usage()` without declaring `DataDep::Usage` fails the contract test with a clear message.

title: Wire cargo-audit into mise + add audit task
description:
Pre-release runbook (docs/ops/release-runbook.md) and spec §Release runbook both want `cargo audit` as a pre-flight check for new advisories against Cargo.lock. Currently `cargo audit` is neither installed nor a mise task, so the runbook can't literally reference it.

**Scope:**
- Add `cargo-audit` as a mise-managed tool in .mise.toml [tools]
- Add a `mise run audit` task (maps to `cargo audit --quiet --deny warnings` or similar)
- Update the pre-flight section of docs/ops/release-runbook.md to include the new task
- Optionally include it in `mise run check` so CI catches advisories on every PR too

**Acceptance:** fresh clone + `mise install` gets cargo-audit; `mise run audit` exits 0 on clean state; runbook references it as a real task, not a note.

title: ADR-0012: Per-process execution model (daemon deferred to v0.2+)
description:
Codify the per-process decision from data-fetching-strategy.md §10 + session discussion into a MADR v4.0 ADR.

Decision: each invocation spawns a fresh linesmith process; no persistent daemon. Daemon mode documented as v0.2+ escape hatch if cold-start measurements exceed targets despite optimizations.

Acceptance:
- docs/adrs/0012-per-process-execution.md exists, follows 0000-template.md
- Status: accepted
- Cites data-fetching-strategy.md §10
- Captures: per-process rationale (simplicity, no IPC, matches all competitors), daemon-mode tradeoffs, measurement criteria for revisiting
- Independent of ADR-0009/0010/0011 (can be written in parallel with them)
notes: Fourth of 4 ADRs. Independent. Shorter than the others (~80 lines).
close_reason: ADR-0012 written: docs/adrs/0012-per-process-execution.md. Locks in per-process invocation model for v0.1. Daemon mode documented as the v0.2+ escape hatch if cold-start target can't be hit with per-process + segment-driven lazy loading (ADR-0010). All 4 competitor Claude Code statuslines surveyed use per-process — no daemon precedent. Data-fetching architecture from ADR-0010 composes cleanly with future daemon mode (DataContext ports to daemon-owned without segment-code changes).

title: Research: CCometixLine (Rust peer) data sources + Rust patterns
description:
ccstatusline-widget-internals.md nailed the TS dominant tool. CCometixLine (~2.7k⭐, Rust/TOML) is our closest architectural peer. Cross-check to confirm (a) no different rate-limit data source (i.e., they also hit /api/oauth/usage or use a different path), (b) Rust-specific patterns worth adopting: binary size, HTTP client, caching, credential reading, gix usage.

Acceptance:
- Locate the repo, identify maintainer + license
- Document data-source cascade (HTTP endpoint? cache? JSONL fallback?)
- Note any rate-limit source that ccstatusline doesn't use
- Catalog Rust-specific implementation choices (ureq vs reqwest, cache format, credential reader)
- Compare binary size / startup time claims if documented
- If nothing new: close with verdict 'parity with ccstatusline findings; no new patterns to adopt'
notes: Lower priority than the earlier batch since ccstatusline internals are already documented. Main value is Rust-peer comparison.
close_reason: CCometixLine hits identical /api/oauth/usage endpoint with same oauth-2025-04-20 beta header — no new data source. Rust patterns captured in docs/research/ccometixline-rust-patterns.md: adopt ureq + serde + chrono, config-driven base_url/TTL/timeout (CCometixLine), lock file + 429 handling (ccstatusline), cargo release profile tuning (lto/strip/codegen-units=1/panic=abort). Avoid: npm-subprocess User-Agent. Recommend skipping claude-powerline/claudia-statusline/felipeelias — design space is covered.

title: Research: rate-limit data source per plan tier (free / pro-max / api)
description:
Tier-aware rate-limit fallback: refine derivation heuristic if users report mismatches.

ADR-0011 (docs/adrs/0011-rate-limit-data-source.md) locks in the primary derivation:
- `stripe_subscription` + `hasOpusPlanDefault=true` → Max
- `stripe_subscription` + `hasOpusPlanDefault=false` → Pro
- missing/other → Free

Inferred from Max-tier capture only (maintainer on Max plan, not downgrading). Pro and Free rows are educated guesses.

Acceptance (repurposed — no longer a proactive spike):
- Stay open as a catch-all for tier-mismatch bug reports
- If a user files 'my tier shows as X but I'm on Y' — update the table in ADR-0011 via a follow-up ADR (per immutability rule)
- If a volunteer with Pro/Free access offers to capture the endpoint response + oauthAccount block, their data updates the table via the same follow-up ADR
- Close when either the table is confirmed correct across all three tiers OR v0.2 ships without tier-mismatch reports
notes: Repurposed from proactive spike to passive issue-tracker. The original 'capture free-tier response' acceptance is unblocked only by community contribution; not on linesmith v0.1 critical path. Reason: maintainer is on Max plan and not downgrading.
close_reason: Tier detection is out of scope for v0.1 per ADR-0011. No surveyed Claude Code statusline (ccstatusline, CCometixLine, claudia-statusline, claude-powerline) does tier detection; they all display raw endpoint utilization %. linesmith follows the same approach. Tier-aware behavior deferred to v0.2+ and gated on a concrete product need. If we ever want it, derivation can pull from ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.billingType + hasOpusPlanDefault, but that's a future ADR.

title: Research: distinguish bare repo / linked worktree / main checkout
description:
Stdin `workspace.git_worktree {name, path}` tells us WHICH worktree, not which KIND. For correctness-first worktree isolation (ccstatusline#190) we need to know:

- Main checkout: `.git` is a directory
- Linked worktree (`git worktree add`): `.git` is a file with `gitdir: ...` pointer
- Bare repo: no worktree; repo discovery returns kind=bare

`gix` exposes this via `Repository::kind()`. Need to confirm API, test against fixtures.

Acceptance:
- Document gix API for repo/worktree kind detection
- Confirm behavior on all three layouts + submodule edge case
- File follow-up bead for worktree-kind signal in workspace segment (or dedicated segment) if useful

title: Research: detect effort/thinking level from JSONL or settings
description:
Effort segment with reliable detection. ccstatusline-style JSONL parse for `<local-command-stdout>Set model to ... with {EFFORT} effort` has reliability holes documented in docs/research/claude-data-files.md §7:
1. /model invocations that DON'T change effort emit 'Kept model as X' (no effort) — regex misses
2. /effort-only invocations emit a different marker — regex misses
3. Cancelled runs write nothing to JSONL
4. Session-start with no transcript writes returns undefined

Implement with dual-source approach:
- JSONL backwards scan for BOTH /model and /effort markers (two regexes)
- Configured fallback default (xhigh per docs)
- Optional: monitor additionalModelOptionsCache in ~/.claude.json once Anthropic populates it

Forward-compat: store unknown effort tokens as {value, known: false}. Known set: low | medium | high | xhigh | max.
notes: Reopened after docs/research/claude-data-files.md §7 documented reliability holes the prior close reason didn't capture. Original close pointed only to ccstatusline's single-regex approach.

title: Add rustfmt.toml + clippy.toml + taplo.toml for consistent tooling
description:
Relies on tool defaults today, which drift across Rust versions and contributors. Mirrors jbabin91/autocomplete-rs configs as the baseline.

**Scope:**
- rustfmt.toml: pin max_width, imports_granularity, group_imports, reorder_imports, use_field_init_shorthand, other stable rustfmt options. Start from autocomplete-rs config verbatim and tweak if 'cargo fmt' produces unexpected changes on existing code.
- clippy.toml: pin msrv (to match Cargo.toml rust-version = 1.80), cognitive-complexity-threshold, disallowed-types/methods, doc-valid-idents if needed.
- taplo.toml: TOML formatter config — column_width, align_entries, reorder_keys. Consistent formatting for Cargo.toml, *.toml configs, fixtures/*.toml.

**Process:**
1. Copy the three files from autocomplete-rs as starting points
2. Run 'cargo fmt', 'cargo clippy -- -D warnings', 'taplo format --check' — fix any drift
3. Add 'taplo format --check' or similar to mise check task if not there already

**Acceptance:** mise run check is still green; diffs from 'cargo fmt --all -- --check' are stable; future contributors get the same formatting regardless of their rustfmt/clippy/taplo version (within reason).

title: PR template + bug/feature issue templates + ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml
description:
Add GitHub Issue + PR templates. **GitHub Issues are the intake funnel for beads** — external users file issues, maintainers triage them into bd. Templates must collect bead-ready information so conversion is friction-free.

**Scope:**
- .github/pull_request_template.md: Summary + Resolves (bead footer reminder, lsm-xxx format) + Test plan checkbox (mise run check, mise run test, manual smoke if UI/output changed)
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml: fields shaped to become a bead description directly:
  - Steps to reproduce
  - Expected vs actual
  - linesmith --version
  - OS + terminal + shell
  - Claude Code version
  - Relevant env vars (NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR, COLUMNS, TERM, COLORTERM)
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml: fields matching a feature-bead shape:
  - Problem statement (what's missing, who is it hurting)
  - Proposed solution
  - Alternatives considered
  - Links to related ADR / spec / idea / existing bead
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml: contact_links pointing to oakoss GitHub Discussions for questions. Do NOT disable blank issues — some reports genuinely don't fit a template and forcing a template creates friction.

**Workflow documented in CONTRIBUTING.md (lsm-00f):**
- External reporters file a GH Issue via template
- Maintainer triages into a bead (bd create) if real work; closes issue with 'Tracked as lsm-xxx' pointer
- Or: keeps issue open, links bead in description, closes issue when bead closes

**Skip for now:** CODEOWNERS (single maintainer), separate security template (oakoss/.github/SECURITY.md covers it).

**Acceptance:** new PRs open with the template prefilled; bug and feature templates appear on 'New Issue' with fields that a maintainer can copy/paste directly into a bead description.

title: Write project-specific CONTRIBUTING.md for linesmith
description:
Overrides the org-level oakoss/.github CONTRIBUTING.md for this repo. linesmith's workflow differs meaningfully — beads is the source of truth for tracking work, and GitHub Issues serve as the public intake funnel.

**Scope (~100 lines max):**
- Quick start: mise install, mise run check, mise run test
- How work gets done:
  - External users: file a GitHub Issue (bug or feature template); maintainer triages into a bead (bd) and links back
  - Internal contributors: bd ready to find/claim work; read AGENTS.md for the full contract; docs/specs/ for feature-area specs
- Docs pipeline summary: research → ideas → ADRs → specs → beads (point at docs/README.md for details)
- Pull requests: conventional commits enforced by cog (pre-commit hook), wait for review before committing, no proactive commits, one logical change per commit, bead footer in subject (lsm-xxx)
- Optional callout on the review cadence: de-slopify → multi-agent PR review → Codex review → close bead → commit is the project's standard slice cycle
- Org-wide guidelines pointer: link to oakoss/.github for code of conduct, security reporting, support channels

**Why project-specific:**
- AGENTS.md is heavy; CONTRIBUTING.md is a softer on-ramp that points at it
- Beads + GitHub-Issues-as-intake workflow is unusual and worth explaining
- mise + lefthook + cog stack differs from Bun/pnpm projects the org-level CONTRIBUTING assumes
- Docs pipeline is distinctive

**Keep inherited from org-level:**
- CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
- SECURITY.md
- SUPPORT.md
- FUNDING.yml

**Acceptance:** a new external user reads CONTRIBUTING.md and knows in under 2 minutes how to file an issue and what happens next; a new internal contributor knows how to find work, how PRs get reviewed, and where the pipeline docs live.

title: Extend workspace segment to surface worktree name in hybrid format
description:
Part of lsm-8jl epic. Differentiator per docs/ideas/0001-feature-parity-matrix.md — 'per-worktree state isolation'. Extends the existing workspace segment rather than creating a new one.

**Scope:**
- Workspace segment currently renders project_dir basename (e.g., 'linesmith') or git_worktree name when inside a worktree (e.g., 'linesmith/feat-segments').
- Verify current behavior matches spec; if not, align.
- Add worktree-linked detection (.git file vs directory) for visual distinction if spec requires (TBD in lsm-5wu).
- No new segment; no new config key unless spec adds one.
- Tests: primary checkout shows repo name only; worktree shows repo/worktree; non-repo shows basename.

**Depends on:** lsm-5wu (spec decides exact format).
close_reason: workspace segment sources worktree name from ctx.git() (RepoKind::LinkedWorktree). Gix errors now log once at the data layer; render path uses wildcard match for SemVer safety with #[non_exhaustive] RepoKind. Integration test covers real git worktree add + workspace/git_branch coexistence.

title: .github/renovate.json — dep automation mirroring oakterm
description:
Part of lsm-h74 epic. Configure Renovate for oakoss/linesmith.

**Renovate is already installed on the oakoss org** (installation ID 101978047). Only need to:
1. Add .github/renovate.json mirroring oakoss/oakterm verbatim:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": [
    "config:recommended",
    "group:allNonMajor",
    "helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests",
    "schedule:earlyMondays",
    ":maintainLockFilesMonthly",
    ":semanticCommits",
    ":semanticCommitTypeAll(chore)"
  ],
  "labels": ["dependencies"],
  "cargo": { "enabled": true },
  "rangeStrategy": "bump",
  "automerge": true,
  "platformAutomerge": true,
  "platformCommit": "enabled",
  "commitBody": "",
  "prConcurrentLimit": 5
}
```
2. In Renovate app settings, ensure oakoss/linesmith is in the allowed-repo list (may require opening Renovate org settings at https://github.com/organizations/oakoss/settings/installations).
3. Non-major dep bumps auto-merge after CI passes.
4. Major bumps open PRs for human review.
5. GitHub Action SHAs updated weekly.
6. Lockfile maintained monthly.

**Depends on:** lsm-pud (CI must be green + required on main before Renovate auto-merge is safe).

**Acceptance:** Renovate opens its first dep-update PRs on oakoss/linesmith within a week; non-major ones merge automatically after CI green.
notes:
Final renovate.json shape diverges from oakterm in 5 ways (codified during pre-commit review on 2026-04-25):

1. platformCommit: true (boolean) instead of 'enabled' (string) — oakterm's value is invalid per renovate-config-validator (caught here, oakterm not yet fixed; tracked in bd memory oakterm-renovate-platformcommit-bug).
2. platformAutomerge: false (was true) — Renovate's default platformAutomerge=true uses GitHub native auto-merge which respects ONLY branch-protection-required checks. With our setup (only CI Summary required, audit + codeql non-required), platformAutomerge=true would let a vulnerable cargo dep auto-merge if cargo-deny failed. platformAutomerge=false makes Renovate run its own merge logic that waits for ALL checks to be green. See bd memory renovate-platformautomerge-vs-required-checks for details.
3. vulnerabilityAlerts override added: schedule=['at any time'], labels=['security']. Without this, schedule:earlyMondays preset would delay CVE-driven PRs by up to 5 days.
4. packageRules ungroups cargo from group:allNonMajor — per-crate PRs ease bisect when one bump breaks. Other ecosystems (github-actions, npm) stay grouped.
5. commitBody: '' override removed — Renovate's default body includes release-notes block, useful for git-blame archaeology.

Renovate org installation has repository_selection='all' so linesmith auto-picks-up on next scheduled run.
close_reason: Renovate config (.github/renovate.json) added: mirrors oakterm baseline + 5 deliberate divergences (platformCommit boolean fix, platformAutomerge=false to gate on all-green not just required checks, vulnerabilityAlerts schedule override, ungrouped cargo for per-crate bisect, default commitBody for release-notes). renovate-config-validator clean. Renovate org installation has repository_selection=all so linesmith auto-picks-up on next scheduled run (Monday or sooner for CVE-driven). Branch protection (lsm-j2o) ruleset 'Required CI Checks' gates auto-merge via 'CI Summary' check; platformAutomerge=false adds belt+suspenders gating on audit.yml + codeql.yml.

title: README install section + docs/ops/release-runbook.md
description:
Part of lsm-c2i epic. User-facing install docs + contributor-facing release runbook + Rust-specific dev setup.

**Context:** oakoss/.github provides org-wide CONTRIBUTING.md which says 'check the project's README for package manager, installation steps, development commands, test instructions.' linesmith's README must satisfy that pointer.

**Scope:**
- README.md install section covering: curl | sh shell installer, PowerShell installer, brew install oakoss/tap/linesmith, cargo install linesmith, download-from-releases fallback; Claude Code settings.json snippet
- README.md dev-setup section: mise install, mise run check, mise run test, cargo fmt / clippy conventions, lefthook hooks, bd workflow pointer to AGENTS.md
- README.md status block (pre-1.0 note)
- README badges: crates.io version, docs.rs, GH release, CI, license
- docs/ops/release-runbook.md: exact steps to cut a release (bump via release-plz PR, review CHANGELOG, merge, cargo-dist auto-fires on tag push, verify artifacts, announce)

**Acceptance:** a new contributor reads README → AGENTS.md → runbook and can cut a patch release without asking for help; a new user installs linesmith via one of the documented paths and gets a working status line in Claude Code.
close_reason: README + release runbook landed for v0.1.0. README: 4 shields.io badges (crates.io, docs.rs, GH release, license); pre-1.0 semver status block; real install commands for all four paths (shell, PowerShell, Homebrew, cargo install); SLSA provenance verify (scoped to prebuilt artifacts, not cargo install output); macOS Gatekeeper workaround; Configure section trimmed to v0.1.0 built-ins (model, workspace, context_window, cost, effort, rate_limit, rate_limit_5h, rate_limit_7d) with roadmap note for git_branch + context_bar + rhai; Development section now points at AGENTS.md + runbook. docs/ops/release-runbook.md: contributor playbook covering pre-flight checks, release-plz PR review, merge + publish flow, 6-job release.yml walkthrough, verify, announce, pre-release (RC) flow, dry-run pointer, rollback, first-release bootstrap recipe. Cross-checked against actual v0.1.0 release state.

title: Treat broken-pipe on presets_apply success line as exit 1
description:
Follow-up from lsm-kb6 review. Today if stdout is a broken pipe when presets_apply writes its final 'wrote preset "{name}" to {path}' confirmation, the write is dropped via 'let _ = writeln!' and the process still exits 0. The config file IS written, but a user watching stdout sees nothing and may assume failure.

**Scope:**
- Detect broken-pipe on the final stdout confirmation in presets_apply (and other user-visible success lines going to stdout like themes_list) and return exit 1.
- Consistent with run_cli's approach: run_with_context errors on stdout write fail and returns 1.
- Add a test with a failing stdout writer that exits 1.

**Why deferred from lsm-kb6:** The file-write contract is correct (file IS on disk); the only miss is user-visible confirmation. A user who cares about the exit code is likely scripting, and scripting callers use --force with a known name and don't need the confirmation. Not a blocker for ship.

**Acceptance:** presets_apply with a failing stdout writer returns 1, not 0. Existing tests (stdout OK) still pass.

title: Thread color-parse error context through parse_color
description:
Follow-up from lsm-1o0 review. theme::user::parse_color currently returns Result<Color, ()>, collapsing all internal failure modes (bad hex length, non-hex char, rgb channel overflow, rgb arity, unknown named color) into a unit error. Both StyleParseError::InvalidFg and ThemeParseError::InvalidColor wrap that unit with .map_err(|_| ...), producing warnings like 'invalid fg color rgb(300,0,0)' without hinting that channel-300 is the real issue.

**Scope:**
- Introduce ColorParseError enum (bad-hex-length, non-hex-digit, rgb-channel-overflow, rgb-arity, unknown-name) in theme::user
- Change parse_color / parse_hex / parse_rgb_args / parse_named signatures to return Result<_, ColorParseError>
- Thread into StyleParseError::InvalidFg (carry a ColorParseError payload or compose the Display)
- Thread into ThemeParseError::InvalidColor
- Update tests to pin variant-level assertions where helpful

**Why:** Current user-facing warnings echo the input but not the reason; channel-overflow looks identical to a typo. Not load-bearing for lsm-1o0 ship — flagged as pre-existing and deferred.

**Acceptance:** parse_color returns a typed error; 'invalid fg color rgb(300,0,0)' becomes something like 'invalid fg color rgb(300,0,0): channel value out of range'. Existing callers still compile; warnings still go through the same callback path.

title: Wrap external-crate error types leaking through linesmith's public API
description:
Several external-crate error types leak through public surfaces, coupling our API to third-party crate choices:

1. `cli::parse()` returns `Result<Action, lexopt::Error>` — `lexopt::Error` is public in our API. Swapping lexopt for another arg parser would be a breaking change.
2. `config::ConfigError::Parse { source: toml::de::Error }` — toml's error type is a public field. Swapping the toml crate would break downstream matchers.
3. `input::parse()` probably surfaces `serde_json::Error` somewhere — verify during implementation.

Fix: introduce our own error types that wrap the external ones with `std::error::Error::source()` chains. Pattern:

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ArgParseError(Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>);
impl From<lexopt::Error> for ArgParseError { ... }
impl std::error::Error for ArgParseError { ... }
```

Audit all `pub fn` / `pub struct field` / `pub enum variant` signatures under `crates/linesmith/src/` for external-crate types. Wrap the ones that surface. Domain-legitimate types (`chrono::DateTime<Utc>`, `std::path::PathBuf`, `std::io::Error`) stay as-is.

Motivation: the project values swap-ability for dependency choices. Wrappers make that possible without breaking downstream consumers.

Scope: single focused refactor, no behavior changes. Tests that match on `lexopt::Error` / `toml::de::Error` variants adapt to the new wrapper types.

title: Replace Style.role + Style.fg precedence with Tint enum
description: Follow-up to lsm-7kn (type-design-analyzer). Style currently has both Option<Role> and Option<Color>; precedence 'fg wins over role' is enforced only in resolve_fg(). A Tint::{Role(Role), Fg(Color), None} variant would make the invariant structural (exactly one tint source at compile time) instead of a runtime resolution step.\n\nDecorations stay as bools since they're orthogonal. Public API change, pre-1.0 fine. Pair with the Palette256 newtype refactor for a coherent type-design slice.

title: Make Color::Palette256 disjoint from Palette16 via newtype
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (type-design-analyzer). Color::Palette256(u8) admits n in 0..=15 which overlaps semantically with Palette16(AnsiColor). Two distinct values mean the same color; palette256_to_ansi16 and downgrade have to special-case n<16.

Fix: introduce a newtype Palette256Index(u8) with TryFrom<u8> rejecting n<16, OR redefine Palette256 to only represent 16..=255. Disjoint variants make the taxonomy structural and eliminate the double-path in downgrade.

Breaking change for Color's public API but we're pre-1.0. Do this alongside the Tint refactor (separate bead) for a clean type-design slice.

title: Improve rgb_to_ansi16 + palette256_to_ansi16 accuracy for Catppuccin
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (code-reviewer P90 + P88 findings). Current downgrade heuristics aren't exercised by MVP built-ins (default uses Palette16 directly, minimal is NoColor) but will matter when Catppuccin lands (lsm-b7u) — those are TrueColor themes and users on legacy terminals need reasonable fallbacks.

Two fixes:
1. rgb_to_ansi16: dominance table steals green hues. Example: (130, 220, 30) routes to Yellow via the (_, dominant_g, _, r_hi, _, _) arm even though the color is lime green. Likely need a proper HSV-nearest or weighted nearest-RGB algorithm, or a precomputed lookup against AnsiColor RGB triples.
2. palette256_to_ansi16 grayscale ramp: 0..=7→Black, 8..=15→BrightBlack, 16..=19→White, 20..=23→BrightWhite has a step 15→16 where a 10-point RGB jump flips dark→white. Rebalance the boundaries.

Tests should snapshot Catppuccin mocha/latte under Palette16 and assert plausible output. Filed P3 (not blocking MVP; matters once lsm-b7u is in progress).

title: Extract shared TempDir test helper (dedupe config.rs + lib.rs)
description: Follow-up from lsm-lyf pr-test-analyzer (severity 5). Two byte-identical TempDir structs and tempdir() helpers exist: config.rs::tests (lines ~357-381) and lib.rs::cli_main_tests (bottom of module). Extract to a #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod testutil in lib.rs or src/testutil.rs so future test modules reuse the same helper.\n\nNote: the hand-rolled version skips cleanup on panic (unwind bypasses Drop on some configs). Either document the limitation or adopt the tempfile dev-dep.

title: Surface VarError::NotUnicode in CliEnv::from_process
description:
Follow-up from lsm-lyf code review (silent-failure-hunter, MEDIUM). CliEnv::from_process uses std::env::var(...).ok() which collapses NotUnicode into None. A HOME with invalid UTF-8 becomes indistinguishable from unset, producing a misleading 'HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME both unset' diagnostic from --check-config.

Fix: match on VarError, log NotUnicode to stderr before treating as None. Or switch to env::var_os and lossy-decode with a warning. Path env vars especially deserve this — it's the exact scenario users will hit and struggle to debug.

Pre-existing behavior (detect_config_path had the same drop). Not a regression from lsm-lyf.

title: Propagate stderr through run_with_segments_and_width
description: Follow-up to lsm-lyf. run_with_segments_and_width currently writes its parse-error line directly to io::stderr().lock() (lib.rs:67). That bypasses the stderr sink that cli_main threads through, so cli_main_tests can't capture 'linesmith: parse: ...' messages on malformed JSON — only the '?' stdout marker.\n\nAdd a stderr Write param to run_with_segments_and_width (and plumb through run_with_width / run), or inject a closure. Update integration tests and cli_main_tests to assert stderr content on malformed payloads. Minor touch — mostly signature plumbing.
close_reason: Superseded: addressed in lsm-lyf. Added run_with_segments_width_and_stderr + layout::render_with_warn; cli_main routes all render-path diagnostics through the injected stderr sink.

title: Harden segment text against Unicode spoofing (bidi overrides, zero-width chars)
description: Follow-up to lsm-8y0. The char::is_control() sanitizer strips C0/C1/DEL but permits Unicode bidi-override and zero-width chars that enable visual spoofing without emitting escape sequences: U+202E RLO, U+200E/U+200F LRM/RLM, U+2066–U+2069 LRI/RLI/FSI/PDI, U+200B/U+200C/U+200D ZWSP/ZWNJ/ZWJ. A project dir named 'linesmith\u{202E}exe.txt' could render deceptively (Trojan Source, CVE-2021-42574). Out of lsm-8y0 scope (which targeted terminal injection, not visual spoofing). Decide: strip category Cf + selected bidi overrides, or normalize via unicode-security crate. Add tests covering RLO/ZWJ/ZWSP in worktree names and project_dir basenames.

title: Add test covering Config::from_str via .parse::<Config>() turbofish
description:
From lsm-u8u test-coverage review: Config implements FromStr, but every test call uses Config::from_str(...) directly. Nothing exercises s.parse::<Config>() or let c: Config = s.parse()? — the documented idiomatic Rust shape.

Low-severity but trivial: one test anywhere that does 'toml-string'.parse::<Config>()? (or let c: Config = s.parse()?) would pin the ergonomic against a future FromStr refactor that accidentally breaks trait-method dispatch.

title: Revisit build_segments warn callback API shape before 1.0
description:
From lsm-u8u final code review: build_segments takes impl FnMut(&str) which is ergonomic but has two post-1.0 pains:
1. Monomorphizes per caller — binary bloat grows with plugin count.
2. Can't add a second callback or change shape without a breaking change.

Options to evaluate:
A. &mut dyn FnMut(&str) — one codegen, slightly less ergonomic.
B. Return (Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>, Vec<Warning>) — caller chooses sink.
C. Typed Warning enum (already flagged earlier) — works well with option B.

Pick before 1.0 tag so the signature doesn't churn for plugin-era consumers.

title: Honor macOS Application Support path as config fallback
description:
From lsm-u8u Codex review (P1): docs/specs/config.md §File location precedence step 5 says macOS should fall back to '~/Library/Application Support/linesmith/config.toml' when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset, after the ~/.config path.

Current config::resolve_config_path ignores this macOS convention, so a Mac-first user who puts their config in Application Support will have it silently ignored.

Fix: add a platform-conditional fallback after home/.config:

    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    if xdg_config_home is None {
        check ~/Library/Application Support/linesmith/config.toml
    }

Low user impact today (nothing released), but easy to get right before 0.1 tag.

title: Consider builder pattern for linesmith::run* entries before SemVer lock
Distinguish env::VarError::NotUnicode from NotPresent in config path resolution
description:
From slice-8 silent-failure review: config.rs:detect_config_path uses std::env::var(...).ok() which collapses VarError::NotUnicode (non-UTF-8 env value) into the same 'unset' case as NotPresent.

Extremely rare in practice (pathological locales / filesystem paths with invalid UTF-8), but when it hits the user sees 'echo $HOME shows something but linesmith acts like HOME is unset' with no diagnostic.

Fix: match explicitly on VarError, log to stderr on NotUnicode, preserve .ok() fast-path for NotPresent.

title: Surface config parse/load errors visibly in rendered line, not just stderr
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) silent-failure review: when Config::load fails (parse error, permissions), main.rs logs one line to stderr then silently falls back to built-in defaults. Claude Code may not display stderr at all; user edits their config, saves, sees no change, has no clue why.

Proposal: on config load error in normal run mode, emit a visible sentinel segment at the far left (e.g. '⚠ cfg' with role 'error'). The user sees it immediately, runs 'linesmith --check-config' for details.

Decision needed: does 'never crash the terminal' preclude rendering an error marker, or is a one-cell sentinel acceptable? --check-config already handles the strict path.

Related: review also flagged that the current one-stderr-line-per-invocation is near-silent given the statusline runs once per prompt.

title: Rename Separator::None to avoid Option::None shadowing in match arms
description: From slice-4 type-design review: the Separator variant 'None' shadows Option::None when brought into scope via 'use Separator::*'. Readability footgun. Consider 'Empty' or 'NoSeparator' before plugins depend on the name.

title: Introduce Priority newtype with named constants for SegmentDefaults
description: From slice-4 type-design review: SegmentDefaults.priority is a bare u8, and the 'descending drop order, 0 never drops' semantics are encoded in the layout engine. Plugin authors will stare at raw u8 values. Add either a Priority newtype with Priority::never_drop() / default() / drop_first() constructors, or at minimum pub const NEVER_DROPS/DEFAULT/DROP_FIRST constants on SegmentDefaults for vocabulary.

title: Probe /dev/tty for terminal width before falling back to 200
description: From slice-4 review: when stdout/stderr/stdin are piped (Claude Code statusline case), terminal_size() returns None and we fall through to COLUMNS (rarely exported) then 200. Starship and ccstatusline open /dev/tty directly via ioctl to get real width. Add this as a middle step before the 200 constant fallback.

title: Log to stderr when layout overflows with only priority-0 segments remaining
description: From slice-4 review: when the drop loop exits with total_width still > terminal_width (all remaining are priority-0), the line renders overfull silently. Spec says this is intentional, but users have no hint linesmith made the call. Add debug-gated stderr log naming the overfull-by-N cells count.

title: Emit stderr breadcrumb when text_width saturates at u16::MAX
description: From slice-4 silent-failure review: a segment producing text wider than u16::MAX cells (plugin bug or pathological input) is silently clamped to u16::MAX with no diagnostic. Add a debug-only stderr log when UnicodeWidthStr::width > u16::MAX so misbehaving plugins are discoverable.

title: Slice 3 review follow-ups: cosmetic/stylistic items
description: Non-blocking reviewer suggestions deferred from slice 3. (1) Named ParseEffortLevelError instead of FromStr Err=(); breaking change if EffortLevel becomes public API — revisit. (2) EffortLevel::XHigh → VeryHigh rename; keep 'xhigh' wire slug. (3) RateLimits::windows() tuple accessor returning (Option<&>, Option<&>) for callers wanting both windows at once. (4) format_countdown_until 'expired' variant when resets_at < now (vs current 'now' collapse). (5) Far-future countdown clamp (>999d → e.g. '>2y').

title: Workspace segment: distinguish non-UTF-8 from missing basename
description: WorkspaceSegment currently collapses two silent-None cases: (1) project_dir has no basename (e.g. '/'), (2) project_dir basename is not valid UTF-8. Slice-1 reviewer flagged this as a debug-visibility gap. When structured logging lands (part of the rendering pipeline work), distinguish the cases: no-basename is a legitimate render-None; non-UTF-8 should emit a one-shot debug log to stderr so the user can diagnose. No action today — requires logging infrastructure that arrives with slice-5 cache + slice-8 config work.

title: Slice 2 review follow-up: refactor path_tail to two-arg helpers
description: Reviewers flagged path_tail as fragile — silently fails if a JSON key contains a literal dot. Current keys are safe. Fix when the second tool normalizer is added (input/normalizers/*.rs split), since each new normalizer multiplies the footgun. Alternative: two-arg helpers (key: &str for lookup, path: &str for error reporting).

title: Integrate beads hooks into lefthook
description: Wire beads' git hooks through lefthook.yml rather than via bd's own core.hooksPath installation. Target hooks: prepare-commit-msg (agent identity trailer for forensics), post-merge (auto-import issues after pull/merge), post-checkout (sync on branch switch), pre-push (validation before push). Each is a ~3-line lefthook entry that runs 'bd hooks run <event>'. Defer until we have a git remote or start using branches — most of these are no-ops in current solo/local setup. Reference: bd hooks --help for event semantics.
close_reason: Beads hooks integrated via lefthook for all 5 events (pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, post-merge, post-checkout, pre-push). Extracted safety shim into .lefthook/bd-hook.sh (exit 3/124 swallow, optional timeout via coreutils, graceful no-op on macOS). Verified end-to-end: commit e7f3b06 fired hooks, bd exported 8 issues and 3 memories during pre-commit. Research sources: jdelfino/eval lefthook.yml, beads v0.61 shim .beads/hooks/*.

title: EnvironmentSnapshot.tmux_active: split into TmuxSignal enum if a future diagnostic needs to disambiguate
description: Per type-design-analyzer review of lsm-herx.34. The tmux_active: bool field collapses two distinct env signals (TMUX env var set + TERM starts with 'tmux') into one. Today's warning text only asks 'are we under tmux?', so the bool is correct. If a future diagnostic needs to distinguish (e.g., 'screen started inside tmux' detection where TERM=screen but TMUX is set), split into Option<TmuxSignal { Inside, TermPrefix }>. Current code has a comment on the field documenting the historical reason.
notes: Surfacing review: type-design-analyzer (lsm-herx.34 PR review).

title: EnvironmentWarning: visual separator between env and runtime warnings
description: Per silent-failure-hunter review of lsm-herx.34. The env warnings (NO_COLOR, palette tier, VSCode shim, tmux) and runtime warnings (segment errors, save failures) currently render with the same '⚠ ' prefix and dim-italic style in the preview panel. Users can't visually distinguish 'your terminal is misconfigured' (env, persistent) from 'your last save failed' (runtime, transient). Options: (a) prefix env messages with a different glyph (e.g., '🖥' or '[env]') in EnvironmentWarning::message(); (b) split warnings: &[String] into (env_warnings, runtime_warnings) in render_preview with a blank-line gap. Option (a) is one-line.
notes: Surfacing review: silent-failure-hunter (lsm-herx.34 PR review).

title: Out-of-band token revalidation to close fresh-cache revocation window
description:
lsm-jes0 mitigated the multi-process / post-401 case: peer invocations no longer serve revoked-token data through the fresh-cache short-circuit once SOME process has observed the 401. The single-process first-invocation latency remains: when a token is revoked while the user's cache is still fresh, every render returns at the top-of-cascade is_fresh check until the entry's TTL (default 180s) expires. Codex flagged this in the lsm-jes0 review as 'patch doesn't actually remove the latency window it is trying to fix; it only helps later peer invocations'.

Closing the first-invocation window requires out-of-band revalidation. Three rough sketches, none picked yet:
1. Background revalidation: each fresh-cache serve spawns a tokio/rayon task that fetches in parallel; if it returns 401, invalidate cache. Cuts the window to 1 render. Adds threading + concurrency surface.
2. Aggressive cache shortening: drop usage.cache_duration default from 180s to 30s. Linear tradeoff against API rate.
3. Credentials-file watch: when ~/.claude/.credentials.json mtime changes or the file is removed, invalidate the cache. Catches user-driven token rotation but not server-side revocation.

None of these are obviously right — pick once revocation is reported as a real user pain point. Until then the v0.1 cascade accepts the latency as a known limitation, documented in docs/specs/rate-limit-segments.md v0.2.1 changelog.

title: Add test for clear() failure path in cascade 401 arm
description:
silent-failure-hunter Finding 6 from lsm-jes0 review: the cascade's 401 arm logs at lsm_error! when c.clear() fails, but no test injects a clear() failure to verify the error path. Need a CacheStore wrapper or chmod-test infra to simulate the failure mode. Pre-req: lsm-jes0 landed.

Acceptance: test that exercises a clear()-fails scenario on the 401 path and asserts (a) the result is still UsageError::Unauthorized via JSONL fallback, (b) the failure-lock is still written, (c) the lsm_error! line fires.

title: Rename ChronoDuration alias to SignedDuration in cascade tests
description: cascade/tests.rs:5 still aliases jiff::SignedDuration as ChronoDuration after lsm-3912 — the alias was a search-and-replace cost-cutter. Future readers grepping for chrono will hit the alias; rename to drop the chrono breadcrumb.

title: Doctor self.binary_integrity: version vs build-metadata check
description:
Implement the actual 'Binary integrity' check per docs/specs/doctor.md §Self (currently slice .2 ships only self.binary_path which answers 'do we know where we live'; this bead covers the version-matches-build-metadata check from the same spec row).

Spec contract:
- PASS if linesmith --version matches build metadata
- WARN if build metadata missing (unusual)
- Hint: 'reinstall from a canonical source'

Implementation choices:
- vergen crate (rich build-time metadata; established in Rust ecosystem)
- built crate (alternative, similar shape)
- Manual option_env!('LINESMITH_BUILD_SHA') / env!('CARGO_PKG_VERSION') comparison (lightest)

Suggested ID: self.binary_integrity

Trigger: when there's user demand to detect corrupted / tampered binaries, OR alongside cargo-dist tweaks where build-time SHA capture becomes free.

References:
- docs/specs/doctor.md §Self (Binary integrity row)
- crates/linesmith/src/doctor/mod.rs (check_binary_path is the sibling)
- lsm-l35.2 (slice that intentionally deferred this)
close_reason: Self/binary_integrity check landed. Compile-time option_env!("LINESMITH_BUILD_SHA") surfaces on DoctorEnv as binary_build_sha: Option<&'static str>; check_self_binary_integrity reads the field. Some(sha) → PASS with 7-char prefix in the label ('Built from <sha> (linesmith <version>)') so users can copy into bug reports; None → WARN with the spec-stated 'reinstall from a canonical source' hint. WARN not FAIL because local cargo build is the dominant None trigger and gating exit-1 there would be hostile to contributors. Tests: 4 new (PASS-with-sha / WARN-when-missing / 40-char SHA truncates to 7 / 3-char SHA doesn't panic via len().min(7) slice) + plain_mode_coverage_envs entry for the WARN label. CARGO_PKG_VERSION continues to be the user-visible 'version' identifier; the new check answers the orthogonal 'is this binary traceable to a known commit' question. Spec change-log entry added. 1447 lib tests pass.

title: Doctor v1.1 hardening: linesmith_version newtype + sealed Report / Category
description:
Type-design pass 3 rated the doctor module v1.0-lock-ready but flagged two deferrable hardening items for v1.1 (additive, non-breaking when added under non_exhaustive):

1. linesmith_version: static str newtype. Currently Report.linesmith_version is a raw static str — any caller can construct Report with garbage. Only build_report() supplies it from CARGO_PKG_VERSION today, but the field is the contract surface for v0.2 JSON output. Add a single-construction newtype centralizing the SemVer invariant; prevents fixture-version drift in tests.

2. Seal Report / Category fields. Report.categories and Category.checks are pub (idiomatic for aggregation containers per std::process::Output). Mutable Vec exposure means in-crate code could empty a report after build_report() or push duplicate ids. Fine for v0.1 (one builder); worth sealing if check-id-uniqueness becomes a real invariant.

The module-doc encapsulation note already names this tripwire: 'If Category grows a non-empty-name invariant or Report gains check-id-uniqueness, both gain constructors and seal their fields.'

Trigger: when v0.2 JSON work or check-id-uniqueness audit makes either invariant load-bearing.

References: crates/linesmith/src/doctor/mod.rs (Report, Category, module-doc encapsulation note); type-design pass 3 lock-in concerns.

title: release-plz.toml PR-time validation gap
description:
ADR-0017 explicitly excluded release-plz.toml and release-plz.yml from release.yml's path-filtered pull_request trigger because release.yml's matrix runs cargo-dist, not release-plz — triggering on those files would burn 7 runner slots without exercising the changed automation (false coverage).

Round-2 research confirmed release-plz has no PR-time check mode (subcommand list: Update | ReleasePr | Release | GenerateCompletions | CheckUpdates | GenerateSchema | Init | SetVersion). `release-plz update` mutates the working tree but lacks `--check`. `release-plz release --dry-run` requires registry tokens and is the publish step. `release-plz generate-schema` produces a JSON schema for IDE completion only.

**Options:**
- (a) Custom validator in ci.yml: run `release-plz update` against a scratch checkout with `--allow-dirty`, then `git diff --exit-code` to verify the working tree didn't change unexpectedly. Catches release-plz.toml syntax errors + version-bump miscalculations.
- (b) JSON-schema validation in CI: use the schema from `release-plz generate-schema` to validate release-plz.toml syntax via a generic JSON-schema tool. Cheaper than running release-plz; catches less.
- (c) Accept the gap. Maintainer-discipline: hand-edit release-plz.toml carefully, run `release-plz update` locally before merging.

**Recommendation:** start with (c) and revisit if a release-plz.toml-related break ships. The blast radius is bounded — release-plz.toml mistakes typically surface at the next release-plz run on main, which auto-creates a release PR that fails to merge or behaves unexpectedly. Recoverable.

Filed per ADR-0017's 'File a follow-up bead' directive in the §Out of scope section.

title: Bench: assert no DataDep::Usage segments in render_all_no_usage_* (defensive runtime check)
description:
Code review of lsm-jedb (S1, pass 3) flagged that the bench's all_no_usage_ids() filter is naming-coupled (starts_with("rate_limit_") + extra_usage). The compile-time defense via build_named_segments catches "ID disappeared", but NOT "new DataDep::Usage segment was added with a different name prefix." If a future segment lands with DataDep::Usage and an unrelated id, the bench silently routes Keychain/JSONL/OAuth into measurements.

Scope (small, ~10 lines):
- In cold_bench / warm_bench (or a shared helper), walk the constructed segments and panic if any segment.data_deps() contains DataDep::Usage. Costs one segment construction per bench setup; closes the loop.
- Could fold into build_named_segments instead, but only when the caller is the all_no_usage_* bench — needs a flag.

Acceptance: a future segment that declares DataDep::Usage with an unrelated id panics this bench at startup, surfacing the filter-update need loudly.

Cross-ref: code-reviewer pass-3 review S1; lsm-jedb (closed).
close_reason: Defensive runtime check shipped: build_named_segments gained a forbid_usage flag (bench/render.rs); when set, walks the constructed segments and panics if any declares DataDep::Usage. cold_bench/warm_bench callers pass forbid_usage=true only for render_all_no_usage_*. Catches a future DataDep::Usage segment landing with an id pattern all_no_usage_ids' name-coupled filter doesn't match.

title: README: MSRV badge + visible Rust version pin
description:
lsm-fbar shipped CI MSRV check but README has no MSRV badge or visible version pin. Users evaluating linesmith for installation can't tell what Rust version is required without digging into Cargo.toml.

Scope:
- README badge (img.shields.io/crates/msrv/linesmith or similar)
- README §Install: 'Requires Rust X.Y.Z+' line
- Cross-link to Cargo.toml rust-version key
- Verify badge updates when Cargo.toml rust-version changes

Acceptance: README shows current MSRV at a glance; bumping rust-version in Cargo.toml is the single source of truth.

title: Segment: claude_session — session ID / session name / account email widgets
description:
ccstatusline ships 3 Claude session widgets: Session ID, Session Name (set via /rename), Account Email (reads ~/.claude.json honoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR).

Scope:
- segments/claude_session.rs (or split into 3 small segments)
- ~/.claude.json reader (opt-in, cached per-render — no per-segment file read)
- CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR honor
- Hide-when-empty; configurable label

Acceptance: session metadata renders for users who want it; missing file degrades silently.

title: Engine: widget merge mode — merge / merge-no-padding for label+value combos
description:
ccstatusline ships a per-widget 'merge' option: off / merge / merge-no-padding. Merge collapses an emoji/label widget with its value widget into a single visual unit (no separator between them).

Scope:
- Per-segment config: merge: MergeMode enum
- Layout engine: when merge=true, emit consecutive segments without separator + optional zero-padding
- Snapshot tests covering merged + standalone

Acceptance: e.g. icon segment + value segment can render as one visual unit when both opt in.

title: Engine: Powerline auto-alignment across multi-line layouts
description:
ccstatusline ships Powerline auto-alignment for columnar multi-line layouts (toggleable; depends on multi-line). When the user has multiple lines, Powerline arrows align in a column for a polished look.

Depends on: lsm-bvu (multi-line) + lsm-1my (powerline MVP).

Scope:
- After multi-line lands: post-render pass that pads each line so arrow positions align
- Opt-in [layout_options].powerline_align toggle
- Snapshot tests covering 2-line + 3-line layouts

Acceptance: Powerline arrows align vertically across lines when toggled.

title: Segment: memory — render process memory usage (system, not Claude Code)
description:
ccstatusline ships a Memory Usage widget showing 'Mem: used/total' system memory. Lower priority since it's system-level, not CC-specific, but ccstatusline parity.

Scope:
- New dep: sysinfo (or platform-specific syscalls)
- segments/memory.rs
- Format options: percent, GB used, used/total
- Snapshot tests with mocked sysinfo

Acceptance: memory usage renders cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows).

title: Free-text format-template editor with live validation + variable cheatsheet
description: Sixth editor template (post Starship-parity). Free-text tui-textarea for the [segments.<id>].format string. Live validation: parser runs every keystroke; inline error if invalid. Variable cheatsheet sidebar shows valid $variables for the current segment with green-check for ones the template references and yellow-flag for typos. Live preview keeps showing last valid template's output during transient invalid states.

title: Per-line config screen (color overrides per line)
description: Image 5 in ccstatusline. 'Select Line to Edit Colors' — drilldown from line picker into per-line color customization. Colors apply only to the selected line. Blocked by lsm-bvu (multi-line layout).

title: Line picker screen (depends on lsm-bvu multi-line)
description: Image 4 in ccstatusline. ListScreen-based. 'Select Line to Edit Items' — lists configured lines with widget count. (a) to append new line. ESC back to main menu. Auto-skipped when only one line is configured (jumps straight to Items editor).
close_reason: Superseded by lsm-herx.7's LinePicker module (crates/linesmith/src/tui/line_picker.rs). Multi-line configs now route MainMenu → LinePicker → ItemsEditor with LineKey::Numbered(N); add/delete via a/d verbs; auto-promotes empty-segments + numbered-tables-present configs. Zero-padded keys + dedup-by-parsed-numeric edge cases handled. Originally scoped against lsm-bvu (multi-line) which shipped earlier; LinePicker landed as part of the herx.7 finishing slice.

title: Powerline Setup screen (PropertyScreen)
description: Image 7 in ccstatusline. PropertyScreen-based. 'Font Status' header + 'Powerline Mode: ✗ Disabled - Press (t) to toggle' header. Greyed-out config when disabled (Separator, Start Cap, End Cap, Themes). Blocked by Nerd Font detection wiring AND lsm-1my (powerline separator engine support). v0.3+.

title: git_branch: stash count integration
description:
Child of lsm-1o70. Surface stash count in the segment, paralleling Starship's `$stashed` variable. Render with `[segments.git_branch].stash_format = "$N"` (default empty = no rendering).

Data-layer work: gix doesn't compute stash count for free. Add a lazy `stash` accessor to `GitContext` paralleling `dirty()` and `upstream()`:
- New `OnceCell<Arc<u32>>` field on `GitContext`
- `compute_stash` helper that walks `refs/stash` reflog entries
- Pre-seed helper for tests (parallels `preseed_dirty_state` and `preseed_upstream`)

Composes with lsm-3esp via a new `$stash` variable.

Blocked by lsm-3esp.

title: git_branch: up_to_date indicator for in-sync branches
description:
Child of lsm-1o70. When the working tree is clean AND the branch is in sync with upstream (`!is_dirty() && ahead == 0 && behind == 0`), render an explicit positive marker like `✓`. Currently the segment hides all markers in that state (`dirty.hide_when_zero` + `ahead_behind.hide_when_zero`), which gives no positive signal — users can't visually distinguish "in sync" from "unknown."

Add `[segments.git_branch].up_to_date_indicator = "✓"` (default empty = today's behavior; opt-in).

Composes with lsm-3esp via a new `$up_to_date` variable that only renders when all the negative-state variables (`$dirty`, `$ahead_behind`, `$diverged`) are empty.

Blocked by lsm-3esp.

title: git_branch: diverged-state marker distinct from ahead+behind
description:
Child of lsm-1o70. Starship treats "diverged" (`ahead > 0 && behind > 0`) as its own marker, not a composition of ahead and behind. Add `ahead_behind.diverged_format` (or similar) so users can render `⇕` instead of `↑2 ↓1` when both counts are non-zero.

Composes with lsm-3esp's format template via a new `$diverged` variable that only renders when both ahead and behind are non-zero. The existing `$ahead_behind` variable could be split into `$ahead` / `$behind` / `$diverged` to give users full control.

Open question: when `diverged` is non-empty, do we suppress the individual ahead/behind markers, or render all three? Starship's behavior is to render only diverged in that case. Pin in spec.

Blocked by lsm-3esp.

title: Refine RenderContext type-design (drop Copy, accessor, lifetime, terminal_width=0 doc)
description:
Type-design feedback on lsm-xdyp gathered four small refinements that share a common goal — keep the type SemVer-safe through the dynamic-segment work coming in lsm-1no9, lsm-rkxh, lsm-z0ai, and beyond. Defer until at least one of those lands so the changes are motivated by real call sites.

1. **Drop `Copy`, keep `Clone`.** The current single `u16` field works fine as `Copy`, but adding a `&[NeighborInfo]` field later (one of the spec's named future fields) would force a SemVer break to remove `Copy`. Since the trait threads `&RenderContext`, nothing benefits from `Copy` today.

2. **Hide `terminal_width` behind an accessor.** Convert `pub terminal_width: u16` to a private field plus `pub fn terminal_width(&self) -> u16`. Matches the existing `WidthBounds` shape (the closer parallel than `SegmentDefaults`, which is segment-authored output). Keeps the contract method-shaped so future computed accessors (`cells_remaining()`, `width_for_segment(idx)`) don't fragment call sites.

3. **Reserve a lifetime parameter `RenderContext<'_>`.** Going from `RenderContext` to `RenderContext<'_>` later is a breaking change for every public signature naming it (the trait, every segment impl, the plugin builder). Adopting it now with `PhantomData<&'a ()>` (or just elided `'_`) costs nothing at the type level and prepares for borrowed-data fields.

4. **Document `terminal_width = 0` semantics.** Reachable in production via `driver.rs` saturating subtraction when `claude_padding > raw_width`. The layout engine handles it gracefully (drops every priority>0, emits whatever remains). Add a one-line note to the field doc-comment, and optionally a `debug_assert!(terminal_width > 0)` in `new` to catch upstream config bugs.

Follow-up to lsm-xdyp.

title: Strengthen SegmentDefaults type: TruncationPolicy enum + type-level floor
description:
Type-design feedback on lsm-66k flagged two limits of the current `truncatable: bool` design:

1. **Bool can only express end-ellipsis truncation.** Future modes (middle-ellipsis for path-like content, abbreviator for numeric, leading-ellipsis for git refs) cannot be added additively without touching every `with_truncatable(true)` call site. Replace with a small enum:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum TruncationPolicy {
    #[default]
    Disallow,
    EndEllipsis,
    // future: MiddleEllipsis, Abbreviate, LeadEllipsis, ...
}
```
`#[non_exhaustive]` lets new modes ship without breaking plugin code that matches on the enum. `render_items` keeps its one-line check (`policy != Disallow`); `try_reflow` branches on the policy when a second mode lands.

2. **The 2-cell floor is a runtime-only invariant.** Currently `max(width.min, 2)` lives in `try_reflow`; a segment author who declares `WidthBounds::new(1, 80)` plus `truncatable=true` silently has min clamped up. Either:
   - Document the clamp at the field, or
   - Expose `SegmentDefaults::min_truncated_width(self) -> u16` so the invariant lives on the type and `try_reflow` consumes it.

Also flagged: `with_truncatable(false)` is a no-op; the project's `with_*` builder convention is symmetric so it stays for consistency, but worth a one-line decision in the bead.

Follow-up to lsm-66k.

title: Revisit width.max declarations on built-in segments after reflow lands
description:
lsm-66k added a reflow pass: under width pressure the layout engine now shrinks `truncatable` segments before dropping. That partly subsumes `width.max` for prose-like segments — width.max was originally a defensive cap for pathologically wide segments (e.g. an absurdly long workspace name) that helped on narrow terminals but at the cost of always truncating regardless of the actual budget.

Audit:
- workspace: currently no width.max. With reflow, leave it that way unless we see real overflow under wide budgets.
- git_branch: declares width.max via builder.rs:335 (?). Verify whether the cap is still useful or if reflow makes it redundant.
- Other built-ins (model, cost, percent, countdowns): truncatable=false; width.max may still matter as a hard cap.

Also revisit the design question raised on lsm-66k: should there be a separate truncation priority (independent of drop priority)? Today they share one knob. A `truncate_first: bool` flag (preemptive shrink before any drops) is the simpler extension if a real user case appears.

Driving bead: lsm-66k.

title: Re-add aarch64-pc-windows-msvc to cargo-dist when upstream xwin/cc-rs/ring builds clean
description:
Dropped from dist-workspace.toml during v0.1.1 release recovery. Root cause: cargo-xwin emits MSVC-style include paths as `/imsvc /path` (two args), but cc-rs treats `/imsvc` as the arg and `/path` as a separate filename, breaking ring crates C build. Affects all Rust crates using ring on aarch64-pc-windows-msvc cross-compile.

Audience for native Windows ARM64 binary is small (Snapdragon X laptop users running CC directly in PowerShell, not WSL2 which gets aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu). Source build via `cargo install linesmith` continues to work.

Re-add when:
- cargo-xwin or cc-rs ships an interop fix (track upstream)
- OR cargo-dist gets first-class native windows-11-arm runner support, removing the xwin path entirely
- OR a real user reports needing the prebuilt binary

P4 marker so the decision has a path back; not a blocker.

title: git.rs tests: drop restate-what '// Shared base commit.' comment
description:
fixture_with_upstream has '// Shared base commit.' at the setup boundary. The next three lines self-evidently do exactly that (write file, add, commit). Per AGENTS.md 'Don't restate WHAT', the comment should go.

Scope: one-line deletion in crates/linesmith/src/data_context/git.rs.

title: UpstreamState: private new() constructor
description:
UpstreamState fields are pub, #[non_exhaustive] blocks external construction but in-crate code (and preseed_upstream callers) can still construct with empty upstream_branch or zero-length strings. compute_upstream always produces valid state but preseed_upstream doesn't validate.

Recommendation: add UpstreamState::new(ahead: u32, behind: u32, upstream_branch: String) with debug_assert!(!upstream_branch.is_empty()), route compute_upstream construction through it. Fields stay pub for read access.

title: preseed_upstream: debug_assert head/upstream consistency
description:
GitContext::preseed_upstream accepts any Option<UpstreamState>, including nonsensical combinations like Head::Detached + Some(UpstreamState{...}). The render path filters these out but the data layer permits them.

Add:
debug_assert!(value.is_none() || matches!(self.head, Head::Branch(_)));

Cheap, catches test-fixture misconfiguration in debug builds, zero release cost.

title: UpstreamState.upstream_branch: add short-name docstring
description:
UpstreamState has a type-level docstring but no field-level note that upstream_branch is prefix-stripped (e.g. 'origin/main' not 'refs/remotes/origin/main'). Head::Branch has that context on its field; UpstreamState doesn't. Rhai plugins comparing ctx.git.data.upstream.upstream_branch.split('/').count() == 2 may be bitten by unusual refspecs where strip_prefix doesn't match and the full refname passes through.

Scope: one-line field doc on UpstreamState.upstream_branch + a test lock (assert upstream_branch doesn't start with 'refs/remotes/' on the common case).

title: git_branch: spec-level decision on OtherRef + hide_when_no_upstream=false
description:
render_ahead_behind returns None for non-Branch HEADs unconditionally, including Head::OtherRef. A user who explicitly opted in to hide_when_no_upstream=false wanting the '?' marker visible everywhere won't see it on a checkout where HEAD is e.g. a tag or remote-tracking ref.

Behavior is intentional but documented only in a code comment. Decision needed: (a) keep current (hide for OtherRef), document in git-segments.md §Edge cases or Ahead/behind computation; or (b) show '?' on OtherRef too when hide_when_no_upstream=false.

Spec impact: git-segments.md §Ahead/behind computation or §Edge cases table.

title: count_ancestors_excluding: use gix Platform::selected for subtree pruning
description:
Current count_ancestors_excluding walks stop's full ancestry into a HashSet, then walks tip's full ancestry, skipping (not pruning) matches one at a time. For a 100k-commit shared history this is 4 × shared-history work per render — would blow past the <5ms warm budget in git-segments.md.

gix 0.67 Platform::selected(|id| !excluded.contains(id)) prunes the entire subtree rooted at a match. Switching would reduce the second walk to O(|tip ∖ stop|) — the exact commits we need to count.

Requires benchmark first to confirm it matters (criterion fixture with a large repo). Until then the current shape is simple and correct.

title: Config: extract DirtyConfig to match AheadBehindConfig nesting
description:
segments/git_branch.rs Config is half-flat (dirty_enabled / dirty_indicator / clean_indicator at top level) and half-nested (ahead_behind: AheadBehindConfig). Inconsistent; also fights the TOML shape [segments.git_branch.dirty].

Scope:
- Introduce DirtyConfig { enabled, indicator, clean_indicator } with Default
- Add #[non_exhaustive]
- Migrate from_extras and render_dirty call sites
- No TOML compat needed (TOML shape stays the same; internal struct shape changes)

title: git_branch: tighten detached-HEAD test + isolate init.defaultBranch
description:
Two small test hardening items from lsm-4cf review:

1. The detached-HEAD test asserts 'shape' (parens + 9 chars) but not content. gix::ObjectId::empty_tree is a git protocol constant (SHA-1 '4b825dc6...'); pin the exact hex so slice-side-bugs ('render last N instead of first N') are caught. Also add a second test with a non-constant OID (e.g. hex 'deadbeef...') to catch 'rendered the wrong slice' bugs that constant-prefix could hide.

2. The two unborn-HEAD tests accept 'main || master' to tolerate users with init.defaultBranch=master in ~/.gitconfig. Neutralize the user-config dependency by setting GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null in those tests, then assert exactly 'main'. Cleaner + catches regressions where gix stops respecting the default.

title: jsonl aggregator: cap pathological far-future timestamps in 5h block
description:
Review of lsm-26y noted an edge case: a `compute_active_block` walking entries that include a far-future timestamp (e.g., 2099 from a corrupted JSONL) keeps the "active" 5h block open indefinitely. Mild clock skew (minutes-to-hours) is intentionally tolerated — the user should see their current session even with a fast system clock. But an unbounded future timestamp parks the block forever.

Scope: add a ceiling on how far into the future `actual_last_activity` can be before the block is rejected. Candidates: 1h (matches MAX_LOCK_DURATION_SECS in cache.rs; aligns with the existing "mild skew" framing) or a dedicated `MAX_FUTURE_CLOCK_SKEW` constant. Requires a spec amendment to jsonl-aggregation.md §Edge cases table.

Also in scope: spec tightening — the §Edge cases table currently defines future-timestamp behavior for 5h blocks but not for 7d window. lsm-26y landed a `<= now` guard for the 7d path; codifying it in the spec closes the gap.
design: Deferred from lsm-26y because the "how far is too far" question needs a design decision rather than a correctness fix. Current behavior is spec-compatible and benign for realistic clock drift.

title: Surface int_from_u64 clamp via warn channel
description: ctx_mirror::int_from_u64 silently clamps u64 > i64::MAX to i64::MAX. Comment says forensics survive on ctx.status.raw, which is true, but the layout engine swallows the divergence. Wire a one-shot warn (rate-limited per-process) when the clamp triggers — this signals an upstream parser regression, not a display issue. Today there's no warn channel reachable from inside a Segment::render call; design: either (a) reach into a process-global warn sink, (b) convert the value-conversion path into something that returns Result and surfaces via SegmentError, (c) just leave the comment and rely on raw inspection. Low priority; hits zero real Claude statusline fields today.

title: Spike: verify /usage command data source (live API vs cached stdin)
description:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED via live endpoint capture on 2026-04-18 (docs/research/claude-data-files.md §Raw data). The OAuth /api/oauth/usage endpoint is confirmed real; shape is captured; ccstatusline + CCometixLine both hit it. ADR-0011 codifies the endpoint as linesmith's primary rate-limit source.

Remaining open question: does Claude Code's /usage slash command hit the SAME endpoint, or does it add data unavailable via the endpoint alone?

Running /usage in a live CC session shows three windows (5h, 7d all-models, 7d Sonnet-only) plus 'What's contributing to your limits usage' analysis. The three windows match the endpoint response exactly (we captured both — shape identical). The burn analysis is local JSONL aggregation, not endpoint data.

Conclusion: /usage likely hits the same endpoint plus local JSONL for the burn breakdown. No new data sources unlocked. Original acceptance criteria met enough to close.

Close this bead once confirmed by one more check: does /usage ever hit a /api/oauth/usage endpoint with different fields when linesmith's endpoint capture returns null buckets? If yes, there's a CC-only endpoint variant worth documenting. If no, close.
notes: Updated 2026-04-20 with partial-resolution status. Originally filed to verify /usage data source; live endpoint capture in tonight's research resolved most of the question. Remaining work is low-value; priority lowered to P4.

title: Test presets_apply rename-backup permission failure path
description:
Follow-up from lsm-kb6 review. The fs::rename failure branch in presets_apply (driver.rs: 'linesmith: could not back up {} to {}: {e}') exists in code but has no dedicated test. A regression to the error message, exit code, or which stream it writes to would ship silently.

**Scope:**
- Add a test that triggers fs::rename to fail deterministically. The classical Unix approach is chmod 0o500 on the parent dir, but that's flaky across CI environments (Docker root, macOS/Linux differences).
- Portable options to explore:
  - Pre-seed config.toml.bak as a directory (fs::rename over an existing directory should fail on most platforms).
  - Use a platform-specific #[cfg(unix)] test with chmod.
  - Mock the filesystem (overkill for one test).
- Verify stderr contains both source and backup paths so users can debug manually.

**Why deferred from lsm-kb6:** No portable deterministic trigger without platform-specific code; the create_dir_all branch already pins the exit-1 + stderr contract shape.

**Acceptance:** fs::rename failure path has a test that asserts (a) exit code 1, (b) stderr includes both source and backup paths, (c) the original config.toml is unharmed.

Host-emitted rhai script aborts must use a module-private Rust marker type (e.g. DeadlineAbortMarker) passed via on_progress as Dynamic::from(marker), then matched in the segment classifier with token.is::<Marker>(). Never use a string sentinel — plugins can throw arbitrary strings, and string-equality classification lets a script forge any host classification by throwing the matching payload (Codex flagged this in lsm-f4r). Pattern lives at crates/linesmith/src/plugins/engine.rs (DeadlineAbortMarker) and segment.rs (classify_render_error). Apply when adding any new host-emitted abort cause: memory limit, network limit, etc.

User demand research for Claude Code statuslines (ranked by signal strength): (1) Rate-limit/plan-usage visibility — 44+ reactions on anthropics/claude-code#8412, loudest single signal. Scrape from API headers like ccusage does. (2) Effort/thinking level visibility — 13+ separate issues, CC doesn't re-emit on /effort change. (3) Accurate context % — breaks in 1M context, post-/compact, post-/resume, during 429s. Table stakes, nobody has nailed it. (4) Worktree isolation — model/state leaks across worktrees, ccstatusline#190. (5) Preset onboarding — ccstatusline#42/#226/#277. (6) Burn-rate + survival projection — AndrewTKent mockup #43271. (7) Live skill/agent/MCP visibility — claude-hud at 19.8k stars proves demand. (8) Cache-hit/cache-creation countdown. Top complaints: npx spawns 30+ processes/3GB RAM (ccstatusline#103, #22, chongdashu PR#4), supply-chain risk of @latest (#298), context % wrong more often than right, rendering brittle across tmux/iTerm/IntelliJ/Windows. Competitors: ccstatusline (7.7k TS dominant), CCometixLine (2.7k Rust/TOML), claude-powerline/Owloops (1k TS), claude-hud (19.8k plugin-style), claudia-statusline (Rust+SQLite), felipeelias (Go/TOML). No tool has real plugin API — biggest architectural gap.

linesmith project vision: new AI coding CLI status line tool in Rust (tool-agnostic — supports Claude Code + Qwen Code today, Codex/Copilot when they ship their statusLine APIs). Differentiators: (1) real plugin API via rhai scripting — none exist in ecosystem, all tools hardcode widgets; (2) correctness-first on context %/rate limits/worktree isolation — biggest user pains per research; (3) curated presets for onboarding (Catppuccin/Dracula/Nord/Gruvbox/Tokyo Night/Rose Pine + minimal/default); (4) single-binary (~3-5MB) kills npx supply-chain risk. Architecture: segment/widget system with priority/width hints, file-based caching, async, conditional visibility, sub-composition. GitHub: oakoss/linesmith. Stack: Rust + serde_json + owo-colors + gix + toml + rhai + ureq + lexopt + dialoguer + terminal_size + supports-hyperlinks + cargo-dist.

Renovate's platformAutomerge=true uses GitHub native auto-merge which respects ONLY branch-protection-required checks. With platformAutomerge=false (verified 2026-04-25), Renovate runs its own merge logic that waits for the ENTIRE branch status to be green (every reported check_run must be success/skipped). For a repo with non-required checks like audit.yml or codeql.yml that should still gate Renovate auto-merge: set platformAutomerge=false. Path-filtered checks that don't trigger contribute nothing — they don't block. requiredStatusChecks config is deprecated and only accepts null.

TOML serde flatten with a sibling typed field: use BTreeMap<String, toml::Value>, not BTreeMap<String, TypedStruct>. The typed-struct shape rejects unknown scalar siblings (e.g. typo'd keys, future scalar fields) at parse time, breaking the spec's 'unknown keys are warnings, not errors' forward-compat contract. With toml::Value, the parse stays declarative and validation moves to the builder, which can warn-and-drop per-key. Discovered while implementing lsm-bvu multi-line layout: `#[serde(flatten)] numbered: BTreeMap<String, NumberedLine>` failed parse on `[line] segmnts = [...]` typos; switching to `BTreeMap<String, toml::Value>` plus a builder-side `extract_line_segments` helper preserved the forward-compat rule. Same pattern likely applies to any future Config field that captures arbitrary-keyed sub-tables alongside known scalar fields.
